## Kronos — AI · ML · Quantum Library (open, CC BY 4.0)
Reference on the algorithms, machine learning, quantum logic gates and quantum computing behind Kronos Fusion Energy, plus the helium-3 quantum-computing case. Design figures are computed and reproducible; no economics.

### AI & Foundations
- [APIs and Interfaces](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/apis-and-interfaces.html): An interface is a contract between parts of a system; honoring it lets pieces built by different people, at different times, work together.
- [Abstraction and Modularity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/abstraction-and-modularity.html): Hiding detail behind clean boundaries lets large systems be understood, built, and changed one piece at a time.
- [Algorithmic Complexity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/algorithmic-complexity.html): Complexity describes how an algorithm’s time and memory grow with problem size, which decides what is feasible at scale.
- [Automation vs Autonomy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/automation-vs-autonomy.html): Automation executes a fixed procedure a human specified; autonomy chooses its own actions toward a goal, and the gap is where risk lives.
- [Benchmark Suites and Leaderboards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/benchmark-suites-and-leaderboards.html): Collections of benchmarks and public rankings drive progress and distort it in equal measure; the ranking is not the goal.
- [Causal Inference Basics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/causal-inference-basics.html): Estimating the effect of an action from data requires assumptions that go beyond the data; making them explicit is the whole discipline.
- [Code Review for Science](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/code-review-for-science.html): A second reader catches faults that authors are blind to, and turns private correctness into shared, defensible correctness.
- [Computational Thinking](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/computational-thinking.html): A way of framing problems so a machine can solve them: decompose, find patterns, abstract away detail, and specify a procedure.
- [Computing Across the Plant Lifecycle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/computing-across-plant-lifecycle.html): Computation carries a fusion machine from first design sketch through simulation, construction, commissioning, and daily operation.
- [Confounding and Controls](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/confounding-and-controls.html): A confounder is a hidden common cause that fakes a relationship; controls are the methods that strip its influence away.
- [Containers and Computational Environments](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/containers-and-computational-environments.html): Code runs the same only when its surroundings are the same; capturing the whole environment makes a result portable and durable.
- [Continuous Integration for Science](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/continuous-integration-for-science.html): Automatically building, testing, and checking code on every change turns quality from an occasional event into a standing property.
- [Control Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-systems.html): A control system measures a plant, compares it to a target, and adjusts actuators to drive the difference toward zero.
- [Correlation vs Causation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/correlation-vs-causation.html): That two things move together does not mean one drives the other; mistaking association for cause is the most common inferential error.
- [Coupling Physics Domains](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/coupling-physics-domains.html): Real systems obey many kinds of physics at once; coupling separate solvers correctly is where much of the difficulty and the error lives.
- [Data Formats and Standards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-formats-and-standards.html): Shared, self-describing data formats let simulations, diagnostics, and analysis tools exchange results without loss or ambiguity.
- [Data Pipelines and Provenance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-pipelines-and-provenance.html): A data pipeline moves and transforms data through defined stages; provenance records where every value came from.
- [Data Provenance and Lineage](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-provenance-and-lineage.html): Knowing where data came from and every transformation it passed through is what lets you trust, debug, and correct any analysis built on it.
- [Data vs Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-vs-models.html): Data are records of what happened; models are compressed theories of why; neither replaces the other and confusing them causes error.
- [Data-Driven vs First-Principles Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-driven-vs-first-principles.html): First-principles models start from physical law; data-driven models start from observations. The best systems combine both.
- [Determinism vs Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/determinism-vs-learning.html): Deterministic code does exactly what it was told; learning systems infer what to do from data. Fusion plants need both, kept in their lanes.
- [Digital Twin](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/digital-twin.html): A digital twin is a live, data-fed model of a physical system that mirrors its state and predicts its behavior.
- [Digital Twins](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/digital-twins-concept.html): A digital twin is a model kept in step with a real system by live data, used to monitor, predict, and test changes before making them.
- [Discretization and Meshing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/discretization-and-meshing.html): Discretization breaks a continuous region into finite pieces so a computer can solve physics on it; the mesh is that decomposition.
- [Documentation as a Deliverable](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/documentation-as-deliverable.html): Undocumented code and data are only half delivered; the record of what something does and why is part of the work, not an extra.
- [Emulation vs Simulation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/emulation-vs-simulation.html): Simulation models how a system behaves from its inner mechanisms; emulation reproduces the input-output behavior without the mechanism.
- [Epistemic vs Aleatory Uncertainty](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/epistemic-vs-aleatory-uncertainty.html): Some uncertainty comes from what we do not yet know and shrinks with study; some is inherent randomness that no amount of study removes.
- [Explainability and Interpretability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/explainability-and-interpretability.html): Being able to say why a model produced an output is what lets humans check it, debug it, and decide whether to act on it.
- [FAIR Data Principles](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fair-data-principles.html): Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable: four properties that make data useful to others and to your future self.
- [Falsifiability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/falsifiability.html): A claim earns scientific standing by risking refutation; a theory that forbids nothing explains nothing.
- [Floating-Point Arithmetic](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/floating-point-arithmetic.html): Computers represent real numbers with finite precision, so arithmetic carries small, structured errors that engineers must respect.
- [Floating-Point and Reproducibility](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/floating-point-reproducibility.html): Finite-precision arithmetic obeys its own rules; knowing them explains why numerical results drift and how to keep them stable.
- [GPU Acceleration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gpu-acceleration.html): Graphics processors run thousands of simple operations in parallel, accelerating the regular arithmetic common in simulation and learning.
- [Garbage In, Garbage Out](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/garbage-in-garbage-out.html): No method, however sophisticated, extracts truth from flawed inputs; the quality of a result is capped by the quality of its data.
- [Ground Truth and Labels](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ground-truth-and-labels.html): Every supervised result rests on labels assumed to be true; when that assumption is shaky, so is everything built on it.
- [High-Performance Computing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/high-performance-computing.html): High-performance computing marshals many processors together to solve problems too large or slow for a single machine.
- [Human-in-the-Loop Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/human-in-the-loop-systems.html): Keeping a person in the decision path pairs machine speed with human judgment, but only if the human is positioned to actually intervene.
- [Inverse Problems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/inverse-problems.html): An inverse problem infers hidden causes from observed effects, such as reconstructing internal state from external measurements.
- [Linear Algebra for Simulation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/linear-algebra-for-simulation.html): Nearly every large physics simulation reduces to solving systems of linear equations, making linear algebra the workhorse of computation.
- [Machine Learning Basics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/machine-learning-basics.html): Machine learning fits models to data so they can make predictions on inputs they have not seen, guided by measured error.
- [Model Cards and Documentation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-cards-and-documentation.html): A short structured record of what a model is for, how it was built, and where it fails makes responsible use possible.
- [Model Selection Principles](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-selection-principles.html): Choosing among candidate models means balancing fit against complexity and, above all, estimating how each will perform on unseen cases.
- [Model Validation and Benchmarking](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-validation-and-benchmarking.html): Validation checks a model against reality; benchmarking checks it against other trusted codes and known reference cases.
- [Monte Carlo Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/monte-carlo-methods.html): Monte Carlo methods estimate answers by simulating many random samples, which is ideal for high-dimensional and transport problems.
- [Multiscale Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multiscale-modeling.html): Phenomena spanning atoms to devices cannot be captured at one resolution; multiscale modeling links models across scales that no single method reaches.
- [Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neural-networks.html): Neural networks compose many simple weighted units into flexible function approximators trained by gradient descent.
- [Numerical Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/numerical-methods-overview.html): Numerical methods approximate the answers to math problems that have no closed-form solution, which describes most real physics.
- [Numerical Reproducibility Across Platforms](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/numerical-reproducibility-across-platforms.html): The same code can give different last digits on different machines; understanding why is the key to reproducing results anywhere.
- [Numerical Stability and Convergence](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/numerical-stability-and-convergence.html): Stability keeps errors from growing during a computation; convergence ensures the answer approaches truth as resolution improves.
- [Occam's Razor and Parsimony](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/occams-razor-and-parsimony.html): Among explanations that fit equally well, prefer the simpler; added complexity must earn its place by explaining more.
- [Open Science and Preregistration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/open-science-and-preregistration.html): Making methods, data, and intentions public before results are known guards against selective reporting and lets others check the work.
- [Open Science and the Published Record](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/open-science-and-published-record.html): Publishing methods, data, and code turns private claims into a record others can check, cite, and extend.
- [Optimization Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/optimization-methods.html): Optimization finds the inputs that best satisfy an objective under constraints, which is the mathematical core of engineering design.
- [Overfitting and Generalization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/overfitting-and-generalization.html): A model that memorizes its training data fails on new data; the goal is to capture the signal without fitting the noise.
- [Parallelism and Concurrency](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/parallelism-and-concurrency.html): Concurrency is structuring work to overlap; parallelism is running it truly at the same time. Both speed up modern computing.
- [Partial Differential Equations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/partial-differential-equations.html): Partial differential equations relate how quantities change across space and time, and they describe nearly all continuum physics.
- [Peer Review and Scientific Scrutiny](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/peer-review-and-scientific-scrutiny.html): Independent expert critique before and after publication is how a field decides which claims to provisionally trust.
- [Random Number Generation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/random-number-generation.html): Computers produce reproducible pseudo-random sequences from a seed, which makes stochastic methods both random enough and repeatable.
- [Random Seeds and Stochastic Reproducibility](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/random-seeds-and-stochastic-reproducibility.html): Randomized computations reproduce only when their randomness is controlled; a recorded seed turns chance into a repeatable input.
- [Real-Time Computing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/real-time-computing.html): Real-time computing guarantees not just correct answers but answers delivered within a strict, predictable time bound.
- [Reduced-Order Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reduced-order-modeling.html): Reduced-order models compress a high-fidelity simulation into a much smaller one that keeps the behavior that matters.
- [Regression Testing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/regression-testing.html): A regression test freezes a trusted result so that any future change altering it raises an alarm before the change ships.
- [Reproducible Computational Environments](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reproducible-computational-environments.html): Pinning the exact software environment lets a computation be rerun elsewhere and later with the same result.
- [Reproducible Research](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reproducible-research.html): A result you cannot regenerate from its inputs is a claim, not a finding; reproducibility is what makes computational science checkable.
- [Scientific Visualization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/scientific-visualization.html): Scientific visualization turns large numerical results into images the human eye can reason about, without distorting the data.
- [Sensitivity Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sensitivity-analysis.html): Sensitivity analysis measures how much each input matters to an output, focusing effort on the variables that actually drive results.
- [Simulation Governance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/simulation-governance-foundations.html): The organizational practices, roles, and standards that decide when a simulation may be relied on, keeping trust a process rather than a habit.
- [Simulation vs Experiment](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/simulation-vs-experiment.html): Simulation and experiment are complementary sources of truth; each checks and extends the reach of the other.
- [Software as an Engineering Discipline](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/software-as-engineering-discipline.html): Scientific software that drives real decisions must be built with the rigor of any other load-bearing engineering.
- [Surrogate Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/surrogate-models.html): A surrogate model is a fast approximation of a slow simulation, trained to reproduce its outputs across a design space.
- [Surrogate Models and Emulators](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/surrogate-models-and-emulators.html): A fast approximation trained on a slow model lets you explore vast design spaces, as long as you respect where it was trained.
- [Technical Debt](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/technical-debt.html): Shortcuts that speed today's work borrow against tomorrow's; unpaid, the interest compounds until change becomes nearly impossible.
- [Testing Scientific Software](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/testing-scientific-software.html): Testing code whose correct output is unknown requires standing in for the missing answer with limits, symmetries, and convergence.
- [Testing and Continuous Integration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/testing-and-continuous-integration.html): Automated tests catch errors as they are introduced; continuous integration runs those tests on every change, keeping code trustworthy.
- [The Bias-Variance Trade-off](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bias-variance-tradeoff-foundations.html): Prediction error splits into a part from wrong assumptions and a part from sensitivity to data; reducing one tends to raise the other.
- [The Design-to-Operation Pipeline](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/design-to-operation-pipeline.html): A software pipeline carries a fusion design from parametric study to fabrication data to live plant control.
- [The Epistemics of Simulation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/epistemics-of-simulation.html): Simulation produces knowledge only under conditions; understanding those conditions is what separates a result from a rendered picture.
- [The Intelligence Layer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/intelligence-layer-overview.html): The intelligence layer is the software and models that turn raw plant data into predictions, decisions, and design insight.
- [The Limits of Computation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/limits-of-computation.html): Some problems no computer can solve, others none can solve fast enough, and finite precision bounds what any calculation can know.
- [The Role of Benchmarks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/role-of-benchmarks.html): Shared reference problems let different methods be compared on equal terms, but only for the narrow thing the benchmark measures.
- [The Scientific Method In Silico](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/scientific-method-in-silico.html): Simulation extends the experimental method into regimes no laboratory can reach, under the discipline that the code is itself a hypothesis.
- [The Scientific Software Lifecycle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/scientific-software-lifecycle.html): Research code that others will rely on passes through the same disciplined stages as any engineered software, adapted for evolving physics.
- [Time Integration Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/time-integration-methods.html): Time integration advances a simulation from one instant to the next; the scheme chosen sets its stability, accuracy, and cost.
- [Trustworthy AI](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/trustworthy-ai.html): Trust in an AI system rests on properties that must be engineered and evidenced: reliability, transparency, robustness, fairness, and accountability.
- [Uncertainty Quantification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/uncertainty-quantification-foundations.html): A prediction without an honest error bar is only half a result; UQ is the discipline of attaching credible uncertainty to model outputs.
- [Uncertainty Quantification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/uncertainty-quantification.html): Uncertainty quantification tracks how imperfect inputs and models translate into uncertainty in predictions, turning point estimates into honest ranges.
- [Unit, Integration, and System Testing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/unit-integration-system-testing.html): Tests form a pyramid: many fast checks of small parts, fewer checks of their assembly, and a handful of end-to-end runs.
- [Verification and Reproducibility](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/verification-and-reproducibility.html): A result you cannot reproduce is a rumor; verification and reproducibility turn computation into evidence.
- [Verification vs Validation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/software-verification-vs-validation.html): Verification asks whether you built the model right; validation asks whether you built the right model. Both are required.
- [Verification, Validation, Certification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/verification-validation-certification.html): Three separate gates: solving the equations right, choosing the right equations, and satisfying an external authority that both were done.
- [Version Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/version-control.html): Version control records every change to code and data so history is auditable, mistakes are reversible, and teams can collaborate safely.
- [Version Control and Provenance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/version-control-and-provenance.html): Recording exactly what was done, by whom, and when turns a computation from an unrepeatable event into an auditable, recoverable record.
- [When to Trust a Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/when-to-trust-a-model.html): Trust in a model is earned per question, per regime, and per required accuracy, never granted to the model as a whole.

### Classical Logic Gates
- [AND Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/and-gate.html): The AND gate outputs 1 only when all of its inputs are 1, implementing logical conjunction.
- [Boolean Algebra Laws](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/boolean-algebra-laws.html): The identity, complement, distributive, absorption, and other Boolean laws let logic expressions be simplified and rearranged safely.
- [Buffer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/buffer-gate.html): A buffer passes its input to its output unchanged, restoring signal strength and adding controlled drive or delay.
- [Combinational Logic](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/combinational-logic.html): Combinational logic produces outputs that depend only on the present inputs, with no memory of the past.
- [De Morgan's Laws](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/de-morgans-laws.html): De Morgan's laws convert between AND and OR through inversion, letting any gate be rebuilt from its dual.
- [Digital Comparator](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/comparator-logic.html): A comparator compares two binary numbers and reports whether one is equal to, greater than, or less than the other.
- [Fan-In and Fan-Out](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fan-in-and-fan-out.html): Fan-in is how many inputs a gate accepts; fan-out is how many inputs one output can reliably drive.
- [Functional Completeness](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/functional-completeness.html): A set of logic operations is functionally complete if every Boolean function can be expressed using only that set.
- [How to Read a Logic Diagram](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/how-to-read-logic.html): A practical primer on reading gate symbols, signal lines, bubbles, and truth tables so schematics become legible at a glance.
- [Karnaugh Maps](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/karnaugh-maps.html): A Karnaugh map is a grid arrangement of a truth table that makes Boolean simplification a matter of grouping adjacent 1s.
- [Logic Gate Symbols](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/logic-gate-symbols.html): A reference to the standard distinctive-shape symbols for the basic gates and the bubble convention that ties them together.
- [Logic Levels and CMOS](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/logic-levels-and-cmos.html): Logic levels map continuous voltages onto 0 and 1 with noise margins, and CMOS is the transistor style that realizes them efficiently.
- [Minterms and Maxterms](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/minterms-and-maxterms.html): Minterms and maxterms are the canonical product and sum terms that pin a Boolean function to individual truth-table rows.
- [Modeling Logic Gates in Simulation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/logic-gates-in-simulation.html): How gate behavior, timing, and unknown states are represented in digital logic simulators used to verify designs before fabrication.
- [NAND Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/nand-gate.html): The NAND gate outputs 0 only when all inputs are 1; it is an AND followed by inversion and is functionally complete.
- [NOR Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/nor-gate.html): The NOR gate outputs 1 only when all inputs are 0; it is an OR followed by inversion and is functionally complete.
- [NOT Gate (Inverter)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/not-gate.html): The NOT gate, or inverter, outputs the logical complement of its single input, turning 1 into 0 and 0 into 1.
- [OR Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/or-gate.html): The OR gate outputs 1 when at least one input is 1, implementing inclusive logical disjunction.
- [Product of Sums](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/product-of-sums.html): Product-of-sums expresses a function as an AND of OR terms, read from the truth-table rows that output 0.
- [Sum of Products](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sum-of-products.html): Sum-of-products expresses a function as an OR of AND terms, read directly from the rows of a truth table that output 1.
- [Truth Tables](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/truth-tables.html): A truth table lists every possible input combination and the output the circuit produces, defining a Boolean function exactly.
- [Universal Gates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/universal-gates.html): A universal gate can build any Boolean function on its own; NAND and NOR each have this property.
- [XNOR Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/xnor-gate.html): The XNOR gate outputs 1 when its inputs are equal; it is the complement of XOR and acts as an equality detector.
- [XOR Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/xor-gate.html): The XOR gate outputs 1 when its inputs differ, implementing exclusive-OR and modulo-2 addition of bits.

### Digital Logic & Circuits
- [ASIC vs FPGA vs CPU vs GPU](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/asic-fpga-cpu-gpu.html): Four ways to run computation trade flexibility against efficiency: general processors, parallel GPUs, reconfigurable FPGAs, and fixed ASICs.
- [Arithmetic Logic Unit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/alu.html): An ALU is the combinational core of a processor that performs arithmetic and logic operations selected by control lines.
- [Asynchronous Circuits](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/asynchronous-circuits.html): Asynchronous circuits coordinate through local handshakes instead of a global clock, trading design complexity for potential efficiency.
- [Barrel Shifter](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/barrel-shifter.html): A barrel shifter moves a word left or right by any number of positions in one pass, using layered stages of multiplexers.
- [Binary Subtractor](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/binary-subtractor.html): A binary subtractor computes A minus B, most often by adding A to the two's complement of B using an ordinary adder.
- [Booth Multiplier](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/booth-multiplier.html): Booth's algorithm encodes the multiplier so runs of ones become a single add and subtract, cutting the number of partial products.
- [Branch Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/branch-prediction.html): Branch prediction guesses the outcome and target of a branch so a pipeline can keep fetching instead of stalling for the decision.
- [Bus](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bus.html): A bus is a shared set of wires that carries data, addresses, or control signals between components in a digital system.
- [CRC and Error Detection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/crc-error-detection.html): A cyclic redundancy check appends bits computed by polynomial division so hardware can detect errors in transmitted or stored data.
- [Cache Coherence and MESI](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cache-coherence-mesi.html): When multiple cores cache the same memory, a coherence protocol like MESI keeps their private copies consistent.
- [Cache Design and Associativity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cache-design-and-associativity.html): A cache holds recently used data close to the processor; associativity decides how freely a memory block may be placed within it.
- [Carry-Lookahead Adder](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/carry-lookahead-adder.html): A carry-lookahead adder computes all carries in parallel from generate and propagate signals, breaking the ripple-carry bottleneck.
- [Carry-Save Adder](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/carry-save-adder.html): A carry-save adder sums three numbers into two without propagating carries, deferring the single slow carry step until the very end.
- [Clock Divider](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/clock-divider.html): A clock divider produces a slower clock from a faster one by counting edges, supplying different parts of a system with different rates.
- [Clock Domains and Metastability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/clock-domains-and-metastability.html): A flip-flop clocked while its input is changing can enter metastability, hovering between 0 and 1 for an unbounded time.
- [Clock and Power Gating](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/clock-and-power-gating.html): Clock gating stops the clock to idle logic to cut switching power; power gating cuts supply to idle blocks to remove leakage.
- [Clock-Domain Crossing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/clock-domain-crossing.html): Clock-domain crossing techniques move signals safely between circuits on unrelated clocks despite the risk of metastability.
- [Clocking](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/clocking.html): A clock is the periodic signal that synchronizes a digital system, defining the moments when all storage elements update.
- [Combinational versus Sequential Logic](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/combinational-vs-sequential.html): Combinational logic depends only on present inputs, while sequential logic also depends on stored state, giving circuits memory.
- [Content-Addressable Memory](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/content-addressable-memory.html): Content-addressable memory searches all its stored words in parallel and returns where a match is found, rather than reading by address.
- [Control Unit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-unit.html): The control unit decodes instructions and generates the signals that steer the datapath through each step of execution.
- [Cross-Coupled Feedback](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cross-coupled-feedback.html): Cross-coupled gates create the feedback loop that lets a circuit remember a bit, the principle behind every latch and static memory cell.
- [D Flip-Flop](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/d-flip-flop.html): A D flip-flop captures its data input on a clock edge and holds it until the next edge, the standard storage element of synchronous logic.
- [D Latch](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/d-latch.html): A D latch stores the value on its data input while enabled and holds the last value when disabled, with no forbidden state.
- [DRAM Cell](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dram-cell.html): A DRAM cell stores a bit as charge on a tiny capacitor, achieving high density but requiring periodic refresh.
- [Decoder](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/decoder.html): A decoder activates exactly one of its many outputs according to the binary code on its inputs.
- [Demultiplexer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/demultiplexer.html): A demultiplexer takes one input and routes it to one of several outputs chosen by select lines, the inverse of a multiplexer.
- [Digital Comparator](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/digital-comparator.html): A digital comparator tests two binary numbers and reports whether one is greater than, equal to, or less than the other.
- [Digital Comparators](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/comparator-circuits.html): A digital comparator determines whether one binary number is equal to, greater than, or less than another, bit by bit.
- [Direct Memory Access](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/direct-memory-access.html): Direct memory access lets peripherals move data to and from memory without the processor copying every byte, freeing it for other work.
- [Encoder](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/encoder.html): An encoder converts one active input among many into a compact binary code identifying which input was active.
- [FIFO Buffers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fifo-buffers.html): A FIFO buffer stores data in first-in, first-out order, decoupling a producer and consumer that operate at different rates.
- [FPGA](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fpga.html): A field-programmable gate array is a chip of configurable logic blocks and interconnect that can be programmed to implement arbitrary digital circuits.
- [FPGA Fabric](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fpga-fabric.html): An FPGA implements arbitrary logic on a fabric of programmable lookup tables, flip-flops, and configurable routing set after manufacture.
- [Floating-Point Unit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/floating-point-unit.html): A floating-point unit implements real-number arithmetic in hardware following the IEEE 754 format of sign, exponent, and mantissa.
- [Full Adder](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/full-adder.html): A full adder sums three bits, two operands plus a carry-in, giving a sum and a carry-out, and is the building block of wider adders.
- [GPU Architecture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gpu-architecture.html): A GPU packs thousands of simple cores that run threads in lockstep groups, trading single-thread speed for enormous parallel throughput.
- [Gray Code](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gray-code.html): Gray code orders binary values so consecutive numbers differ in exactly one bit, avoiding transient errors when a value changes.
- [Half Adder](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/half-adder.html): A half adder sums two single bits, producing a sum bit and a carry bit, but cannot accept an incoming carry.
- [Hardware Description Languages](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hardware-description-languages.html): Verilog and VHDL describe digital hardware as text, letting engineers specify behavior and structure that tools turn into circuits.
- [Hardware Multithreading](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multithreading-hardware.html): Hardware multithreading keeps a core busy by running several instruction streams, filling stalls from one thread with work from another.
- [Hardware Prefetching](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/prefetching.html): A hardware prefetcher predicts which memory a program will need next and fetches it into cache before the request arrives.
- [Instruction Set Architecture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/instruction-set-architecture.html): An instruction set architecture is the contract between software and hardware, defining the instructions, registers, and behavior a processor exposes.
- [Interrupts and Exceptions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/interrupts-and-exceptions.html): Interrupts and exceptions divert the processor from its current work to handle an event, then restore it precisely afterward.
- [JK Flip-Flop](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/jk-flip-flop.html): A JK flip-flop extends the SR flip-flop by defining the once-forbidden input combination as a toggle.
- [Linear-Feedback Shift Registers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lfsr-prng.html): A linear-feedback shift register cycles through a long pseudo-random sequence of states using only a shift register and XOR gates.
- [Logic Synthesis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/logic-synthesis.html): Logic synthesis transforms a register-transfer HDL description into an optimized network of real gates from a technology library.
- [Mealy Machine](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mealy-machine.html): In a Mealy machine the outputs depend on both the current state and the current inputs, reacting faster but risking glitches.
- [Memory Consistency Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/memory-consistency-models.html): A memory consistency model defines the order in which one core's memory operations become visible to others in a shared-memory system.
- [Memory Controllers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/memory-controllers.html): A memory controller translates a processor's memory requests into the precise timed command sequences that DRAM chips require.
- [Memory Hierarchy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/memory-hierarchy.html): The memory hierarchy stacks storage from small and fast to large and slow, using locality to give the illusion of both.
- [Metastability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/metastability.html): Metastability is the unstable, undefined state a flip-flop can enter when its timing rules are violated, resolving only after an unpredictable delay.
- [Microcode](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/microcode.html): Microcode implements a processor's complex instructions as sequences of simpler internal steps stored in on-chip control memory.
- [Moore Machine](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/moore-machine.html): In a Moore machine the outputs depend only on the current state, giving glitch-free outputs synchronized to the clock.
- [Multiplexer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multiplexer.html): A multiplexer selects one of several data inputs and routes it to a single output under control of select lines.
- [On-Chip Power Delivery](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/power-delivery-network.html): A power delivery network distributes stable supply voltage across a chip despite rapidly changing current demand from switching logic.
- [Out-of-Order Execution](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/out-of-order-execution.html): Out-of-order execution runs instructions as soon as their inputs are ready rather than in program order, hiding latency.
- [Parity Generator and Checker](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/parity-generator.html): A parity circuit adds or checks a single bit that makes the number of ones in a word even or odd, catching single-bit errors.
- [Phase-Locked Loop](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/phase-locked-loop.html): A phase-locked loop generates a clock locked in phase and frequency to a reference, and can multiply frequency for on-chip clocking.
- [Pipelining Basics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pipelining-basics.html): Pipelining overlaps the stages of instruction execution so several instructions are in progress at once, raising throughput.
- [Pipelining Hazards and Forwarding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pipelining-hazards-and-forwarding.html): Pipelining overlaps instruction stages for throughput, but data, control, and structural hazards can stall it unless resolved.
- [Place and Route](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/place-and-route.html): Place and route assigns each gate a physical location on the chip and draws the wires that connect them, meeting timing and space limits.
- [Priority Encoder](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/priority-encoder.html): A priority encoder outputs the index of the highest-priority active input, resolving the case where several inputs are asserted at once.
- [Program Counter](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/program-counter.html): The program counter is the register that holds the address of the next instruction, advancing each cycle and redirected by branches.
- [Propagation Delay](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/propagation-delay.html): Propagation delay is the time a gate takes for a change at its input to appear at its output, setting the speed of digital logic.
- [Read-Only Memory](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/read-only-memory.html): Read-only memory holds fixed data that persists without power and can also implement any combinational function as a lookup table.
- [Register](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/register.html): A register is a group of flip-flops that stores a multi-bit word and updates all its bits together on a clock edge.
- [Register File Design](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/register-file-design.html): A register file is a small, fast multi-ported memory holding a processor's working registers, read and written every cycle.
- [Reset and Initialization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reset-and-initialization.html): Reset logic drives a chip's sequential elements into a known starting state; how reset is applied and released is a design decision with subtle hazards.
- [Ripple Counter](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ripple-counter.html): A ripple counter chains toggle flip-flops so each stage clocks the next, giving simple hardware but a staggered count.
- [Ripple-Carry Adder](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ripple-carry-adder.html): A ripple-carry adder chains full adders so each carry-out feeds the next stage, giving simple hardware but delay that grows with word width.
- [SIMD Units](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/simd-units.html): A SIMD unit applies one instruction to many data elements at once, packing several values into a wide register and processing them in lockstep.
- [SR Latch](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sr-latch.html): The SR latch is the simplest memory element, holding one bit using two cross-coupled gates with set and reset inputs.
- [SRAM Cell](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sram-cell.html): An SRAM cell stores one bit in cross-coupled inverters, holding data as long as power is applied with no refresh needed.
- [Scan Chains and Design for Test](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/scan-chain-dft.html): Scan chains stitch a chip's flip-flops into shift registers so manufacturing defects can be detected after fabrication.
- [SerDes and High-Speed Links](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/serdes-links.html): A SerDes converts parallel data to a fast serial stream and back, letting chips communicate over few wires at very high rates.
- [Setup and Hold Time](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/setup-hold-time.html): Setup and hold times define a window around the clock edge during which a flip-flop's data input must stay stable.
- [Seven-Segment Decoder](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/seven-segment-decoder.html): A seven-segment decoder converts a binary-coded digit into the seven signals that light the correct segments of a numeric display.
- [Shift Register](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/shift-register.html): A shift register moves its stored bits one position each clock edge, converting between serial and parallel data.
- [State Encoding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/state-encoding.html): State encoding is the choice of binary patterns assigned to a state machine's states, affecting logic size and speed.
- [Static Timing Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/static-timing-analysis.html): Static timing analysis verifies that every path in a chip meets its timing without simulating any specific input pattern.
- [Superscalar Processors](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/superscalar-processors.html): A superscalar processor issues and executes several instructions per cycle by having multiple parallel execution units.
- [Synchronous Counter](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/synchronous-counter.html): A synchronous counter clocks all its flip-flops from the same edge, so every bit updates simultaneously without ripple delay.
- [System Buses and AXI/AMBA](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/system-buses-axi-amba.html): On-chip interconnect standards like ARM's AMBA and its AXI protocol define how processors, memory, and peripherals exchange data.
- [T Flip-Flop](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/t-flip-flop.html): A T flip-flop toggles its output on each clock edge when its input is high, making it a natural frequency divider.
- [The Datapath](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/datapath.html): The datapath is the collection of registers, ALU, and interconnect that performs a processor's data operations, steered by the control unit.
- [Translation Lookaside Buffer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/translation-lookaside-buffer.html): A translation lookaside buffer caches recent virtual-to-physical address translations so the processor avoids walking page tables on every access.
- [Tri-State Buffer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tri-state-buffer.html): A tri-state buffer can drive its output high, low, or disconnect it entirely, allowing many devices to share a bus.
- [Two's Complement in Hardware](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/twos-complement-hardware.html): Two's complement lets one adder handle signed and unsigned numbers, which is why nearly all digital hardware represents signed integers this way.
- [VLIW Architecture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/vliw-architecture.html): A VLIW processor executes wide instructions that bundle several independent operations chosen in advance by the compiler.
- [Von Neumann CPU](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/von-neumann-cpu.html): The von Neumann architecture stores program instructions and data in the same memory, fetched and executed in a repeating cycle.
- [Wallace and Dadda Multipliers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/wallace-dadda-multipliers.html): Wallace and Dadda trees reduce a grid of partial products to two rows in logarithmic depth, making hardware multiplication fast.
- [XOR in Arithmetic and Logic](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/xor-gate-usage.html): The exclusive-OR gate is the workhorse of digital arithmetic, comparison, parity, and controllable inversion.

### Number Systems & Information
- [ASCII](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ascii.html): ASCII is a 7-bit character code mapping 128 values to letters, digits, punctuation, and control codes.
- [Base Conversion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/base-conversion.html): Converting a number between bases uses repeated division for the integer part and repeated multiplication for the fraction.
- [Binary Number System](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/binary-number-system.html): Binary represents every number with just two digits, 0 and 1, matching the two states of a switch.
- [Bit Masking](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bit-masking.html): A bit mask selects, sets, or clears specific bits of a value using bitwise operations.
- [Bit Shifting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bit-shifting.html): Shifting moves the bits of a value left or right, multiplying or dividing by powers of two.
- [Bitwise Operations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bitwise-operations.html): Bitwise operations apply logic gates to each bit of an integer independently and in parallel.
- [Channel Capacity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/channel-capacity.html): Channel capacity is the maximum rate at which information can be sent reliably over a noisy channel.
- [Checksums](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/checksums.html): A checksum is a small value computed from data to detect accidental corruption during storage or transfer.
- [Conditional Entropy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/conditional-entropy.html): Conditional entropy measures the uncertainty remaining in one variable once another is known.
- [Cyclic Redundancy Check](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cyclic-redundancy-check.html): A CRC treats data as a polynomial and uses its remainder under division to detect errors robustly.
- [Data Compression Basics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-compression-basics.html): Compression shrinks data by removing redundancy, split into lossless and lossy families.
- [Endianness](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/endianness.html): Endianness is the order in which the bytes of a multi-byte value are stored in memory.
- [Fixed-Point Representation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fixed-point-representation.html): Fixed-point numbers store fractions by placing an implied radix point at a fixed bit position.
- [Floating-Point Special Values](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/floating-point-special-values.html): IEEE-754 reserves patterns for infinity, NaN, signed zero, and subnormals so computation degrades gracefully.
- [Hamming Code](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hamming-code.html): Hamming codes add overlapping parity bits so a single-bit error can be located and corrected automatically.
- [Hamming Distance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hamming-distance.html): The Hamming distance between two equal-length strings is the number of positions where they differ.
- [Hexadecimal Number System](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hexadecimal-number-system.html): Hexadecimal is base 16; each digit encodes exactly four bits, making it the standard shorthand for binary.
- [Huffman Coding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/huffman-coding.html): Huffman coding builds the optimal prefix code by repeatedly merging the two least likely symbols.
- [IEEE-754 Floating Point](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ieee-754-floating-point.html): IEEE-754 stores real numbers in binary scientific notation with a sign, exponent, and fraction.
- [Integer Overflow](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/integer-overflow.html): Overflow happens when an arithmetic result exceeds the range a fixed-width integer can hold.
- [Joint Entropy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/joint-entropy.html): Joint entropy measures the combined uncertainty of two random variables considered together.
- [Lossless vs Lossy Compression](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lossless-vs-lossy-compression.html): Lossless compression restores data exactly; lossy compression trades fidelity for much smaller size.
- [Machine Epsilon](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/machine-epsilon.html): Machine epsilon is the gap between 1.0 and the next representable float, bounding relative rounding error.
- [Mutual Information](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mutual-information.html): Mutual information quantifies how many bits one variable reveals about another.
- [Numerical Error](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/numerical-error.html): Finite precision introduces rounding, cancellation, and accumulation errors that careful numerics must control.
- [Octal Number System](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/octal-number-system.html): Octal is base 8, a compact shorthand for binary where each digit stands for exactly three bits.
- [One's Complement](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ones-complement.html): One's complement represents a negative number by inverting all the bits of its positive form.
- [Parity Bit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/parity-bit.html): A parity bit is a single extra bit that makes the number of 1s in a group even or odd for error detection.
- [Positional Notation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/positional-notation.html): Positional notation encodes a number as a sum of digits weighted by powers of a fixed base.
- [Prefix Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/prefix-codes.html): A prefix code assigns bit strings so that no codeword is a prefix of another, allowing instant decoding.
- [Rounding Modes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rounding-modes.html): When a result cannot be represented exactly, a rounding mode decides which representable value to pick.
- [Run-Length Encoding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/run-length-encoding.html): Run-length encoding compresses runs of a repeated value into a single value and a count.
- [Shannon Entropy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/shannon-entropy.html): Shannon entropy measures the average uncertainty, in bits, of a random source's outcomes.
- [Sign-Magnitude](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sign-magnitude.html): Sign-magnitude stores a number as a sign bit plus an ordinary magnitude, mirroring how people write negatives.
- [Signed Integers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/signed-integers.html): Signed integers represent both positive and negative whole numbers, most often using two's complement.
- [Source Coding Theorem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/source-coding-theorem.html): Shannon's source coding theorem sets entropy as the hard floor on lossless compression.
- [The Bit and the Nat](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/the-bit-and-nat.html): The bit and the nat are units of information, differing only by the logarithm base used to measure it.
- [Two's Complement](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/twos-complement.html): Two's complement is the standard way to store signed integers, giving one zero and uniform arithmetic.
- [UTF-8](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/utf-8.html): UTF-8 is a variable-length encoding of Unicode that stays byte-compatible with ASCII.
- [Unicode](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/unicode.html): Unicode assigns a unique number to every character across the world's writing systems.
- [Unsigned Integers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/unsigned-integers.html): An unsigned integer uses all its bits for magnitude, representing whole numbers from zero upward.

### Complexity & Computation
- [Approximation Algorithms](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/approximation-algorithms.html): An approximation algorithm runs in polynomial time and returns a solution provably close to optimal for a hard optimization problem.
- [Asymptotic Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/asymptotic-analysis.html): Asymptotic analysis studies how resource use grows as input size heads toward infinity, ignoring machine-specific constants.
- [BQP and Where Quantum Helps](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bqp-quantum-complexity.html): BQP is the class of problems a quantum computer can solve efficiently, and it is believed to strictly extend classical polynomial time for some tasks.
- [Big-O Notation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/big-o-notation.html): Big-O notation gives an upper bound on how a function grows, ignoring constants and low-order terms.
- [Big-Omega Notation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/big-omega-notation.html): Big-Omega notation gives a lower bound on a function's growth, stating the cost is at least a certain rate.
- [Big-Theta Notation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/big-theta-notation.html): Big-Theta notation gives a tight bound: the function grows at exactly the stated rate, up to constants.
- [Boolean Satisfiability (SAT)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/boolean-satisfiability.html): SAT asks whether a Boolean formula can be made true by some assignment of true and false to its variables.
- [Circuit Complexity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/circuit-complexity.html): Circuit complexity measures the size and depth of Boolean circuits needed to compute a function, offering a hardware-based view of difficulty.
- [Computational Problems in Fusion Design](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/complexity-of-optimization-in-fusion.html): Designing a fusion device is a stack of hard computational problems, from plasma simulation to combinatorial optimization of the machine.
- [Decidability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/decidability.html): A problem is decidable if some algorithm always halts with the correct yes-or-no answer for every input.
- [Decision versus Optimization Problems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/decision-vs-optimization.html): Complexity theory is framed around yes-or-no decision problems, but most practical tasks are optimization problems closely tied to them.
- [Dynamic Programming](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dynamic-programming.html): Dynamic programming solves problems with overlapping subproblems by storing subresults, turning exponential recomputation into polynomial time.
- [EXPTIME and Exponential Blowup](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/exptime-and-exponential-blowup.html): EXPTIME is the class of problems solvable in exponential time, and it provably contains problems that P cannot.
- [Finite State Machines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/finite-state-machine.html): A finite state machine has a fixed number of states and no external memory, making it weaker but far easier to analyze than a Turing machine.
- [Greedy Algorithms](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/greedy-algorithms.html): A greedy algorithm makes the locally best choice at each step, which yields a global optimum only for problems with the right structure.
- [Heuristics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/heuristics.html): A heuristic is a practical strategy that finds good solutions quickly without any guarantee of optimality or worst-case quality.
- [Kolmogorov Complexity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/kolmogorov-complexity.html): Kolmogorov complexity measures the information in a string by the length of the shortest program that produces it.
- [Lambda Calculus](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lambda-calculus.html): The lambda calculus is a minimal formal system of functions that is equivalent in power to the Turing machine.
- [NP-Complete Problems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/np-complete.html): NP-complete problems are the hardest in NP: every NP problem reduces to them, so a fast solution to one would solve all of NP.
- [NP-Hard Problems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/np-hard.html): An NP-hard problem is at least as hard as every problem in NP, but need not itself be in NP.
- [Nondeterminism](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/nondeterminism.html): A nondeterministic machine may branch into many possible next steps at once and accepts if any branch leads to acceptance.
- [PSPACE](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pspace.html): PSPACE is the class of problems solvable using a polynomial amount of memory, regardless of how much time they take.
- [Polynomial-Time Verification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/polynomial-time-verification.html): Verification asks whether a proposed answer can be checked quickly, which is the defining feature of the class NP.
- [Randomized Algorithms](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/randomized-algorithms.html): Randomized algorithms use random choices during execution to gain speed or simplicity, at the cost of some uncertainty.
- [Recursion and Recurrences](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/recursion-and-recurrences.html): Recursive algorithms solve a problem by solving smaller versions of it, and their cost is captured by recurrence relations.
- [Reducibility and Completeness](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reducibility-and-completeness.html): Completeness identifies the hardest problems in a class as those to which every member reduces, capturing the essence of the class.
- [Reductions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reductions.html): A reduction transforms one problem into another so that solving the second solves the first, transferring difficulty between them.
- [Rice's Theorem and Undecidability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/undecidability-beyond-halting.html): Rice's theorem shows that every non-trivial question about what a program computes is undecidable.
- [Space Complexity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/space-complexity.html): Space complexity measures how much working memory an algorithm needs as a function of input size.
- [The Church-Turing Thesis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/church-turing-thesis.html): The Church-Turing thesis claims that any function computable by any effective procedure is computable by a Turing machine.
- [The Class NP](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/complexity-class-np.html): NP is the class of problems whose yes-answers can be verified by a deterministic algorithm in polynomial time given a short certificate.
- [The Class P](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/complexity-class-p.html): P is the class of decision problems solvable by a deterministic algorithm in time polynomial in the input size.
- [The Class co-NP](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/co-np.html): co-NP contains problems whose no-answers have short, polynomial-time-checkable certificates.
- [The Complexity of Simulation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/simulation-complexity.html): Simulating physical systems can be computationally hard, which is why plasma and quantum systems strain even the largest classical computers.
- [The Cook-Levin Theorem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cook-levin-theorem.html): The Cook-Levin theorem proves that Boolean satisfiability is NP-complete, giving the first natural NP-complete problem.
- [The Halting Problem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/halting-problem.html): No algorithm can decide, for every program and input, whether that program eventually halts or runs forever.
- [The Master Theorem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/master-theorem.html): The master theorem gives a quick closed-form solution for the running time of many divide-and-conquer recurrences.
- [The P versus NP Question](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/p-vs-np.html): P versus NP asks whether every problem whose solution can be checked quickly can also be solved quickly.
- [The Traveling Salesman Problem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/traveling-salesman-problem.html): The traveling salesman problem asks for the shortest route visiting every city once and returning to the start.
- [The Turing Machine](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/turing-machine.html): A Turing machine is an abstract device with an infinite tape and a finite rulebook that defines the mathematical limit of what is computable.
- [Time Complexity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/time-complexity.html): Time complexity measures how the number of basic operations an algorithm performs grows with input size.
- [Tractable versus Intractable](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tractable-vs-intractable.html): Tractable problems have efficient (polynomial-time) algorithms; intractable ones require time that explodes with input size.
- [What Computation Is](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/what-is-computation.html): Computation is the mechanical transformation of input symbols into output symbols by following a fixed, finite set of rules.
- [Why Quantum Systems Are Hard to Simulate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-simulation-hardness.html): The state of a quantum system grows exponentially with its size, making exact classical simulation infeasible beyond small systems.

### Quantum Logic Gates
- [ABC Decomposition of Controlled Gates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/abc-controlled-gate-decomposition.html): The construction that realizes any controlled single-qubit gate with only two CNOTs plus single-qubit rotations.
- [Barenco Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/barenco-gate.html): A general two-qubit controlled rotation introduced in the proof that a fixed two-qubit gate plus single-qubit gates is universal.
- [Berkeley B Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/berkeley-b-gate.html): A special two-qubit gate that generates any two-qubit unitary with only two applications, the most efficient known primitive.
- [C3X and C4X Gates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/c3x-c4x-gates.html): The three- and four-control NOT gates, the small fixed cases of the multi-controlled X most often synthesized directly.
- [CNOT Gate (Controlled-X)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cnot-gate.html): The CNOT flips the target qubit if the control is |1⟩ — the two-qubit gate that creates entanglement and anchors nearly every quantum circuit.
- [CZ Gate (Controlled-Z)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cz-gate.html): The CZ gate applies a phase flip to |11⟩ — a symmetric, entangling gate that is native to many hardware platforms.
- [Canonical Two-Qubit Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/canonical-two-qubit-gate.html): The three-parameter entangling core that every two-qubit gate reduces to once local rotations are stripped away.
- [Clifford+T Synthesis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/clifford-t-synthesis.html): Compiling arbitrary gates into the fault-tolerant Clifford-plus-T basis, where T-count is the dominant resource.
- [Controlled-Controlled-Phase Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/controlled-controlled-phase-gate.html): Applies a phase only to the all-ones state of three qubits, the diagonal cousin of the Toffoli.
- [Controlled-Hadamard Gate (CH)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/controlled-hadamard-gate.html): Conditionally places the target into an equal superposition, a controlled-U with U equal to the Hadamard.
- [Controlled-Phase Gate (CP)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/controlled-phase-gate.html): Applies a chosen phase to the eleven amplitude only, the fundamental diagonal entangler of the quantum Fourier transform.
- [Controlled-RX Gate (CRX)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/controlled-rx-gate.html): A two-qubit gate that applies an X-axis rotation to the target only when the control qubit is set.
- [Controlled-RY Gate (CRY)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/controlled-ry-gate.html): Applies a real-valued Y-axis rotation to a target qubit conditioned on the control being in state one.
- [Controlled-RZ Gate (CRZ)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/controlled-rz-gate.html): Imparts a Z-axis phase rotation on the target qubit conditioned on the control, related to but distinct from controlled-phase.
- [Controlled-U Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/controlled-u-gate.html): The general recipe for conditioning any single-qubit unitary on a control, the parent of every controlled single-qubit gate.
- [Cross-Resonance Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cross-resonance-gate.html): The microwave-driven entangling interaction that produces CNOT on fixed-frequency superconducting qubits.
- [Deutsch Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/deutsch-gate.html): A three-qubit controlled rotation that was the first single gate proven universal for quantum computation.
- [Fredkin Gate (CSWAP)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fredkin-gate.html): The Fredkin gate is a controlled-SWAP — it exchanges two targets only when the control is |1⟩, a reversible, conservative logic primitive.
- [Gate Decomposition Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gate-decomposition-overview.html): How arbitrary unitaries are broken into the small fixed set of gates a machine can actually execute.
- [Gate Identities and Circuit Equivalences](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gate-identities-and-equivalences.html): The algebraic rewrite rules that let compilers transform one circuit into an equivalent, cheaper one.
- [Gate Synthesis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gate-synthesis.html): Turning a mathematically specified unitary into an explicit, resource-minimal sequence of executable gates.
- [Gate Teleportation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gate-teleportation.html): A protocol that applies a gate by consuming a pre-prepared entangled resource state and classical feedforward.
- [Givens Rotation Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/givens-rotation-gate.html): A two-qubit rotation in the single-excitation subspace, the primitive for orbital rotations in fermionic simulation.
- [Global Phase Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/global-phase-gate.html): Multiplies the entire state by a phase factor, invisible on its own but consequential when placed under a control.
- [Hadamard Gate (H)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hadamard-gate.html): The Hadamard gate creates superposition — it turns a definite |0⟩ or |1⟩ into an equal blend, and is the doorway to nearly every quantum algorithm.
- [Identity Gate (I)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/identity-gate.html): The identity gate leaves a qubit unchanged — the do-nothing operation and the algebraic anchor for every other gate.
- [Ising Coupling Gate RXX](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ising-xx-gate.html): A symmetric two-qubit entangler generated by the XX interaction, native to trapped-ion hardware.
- [Ising Coupling Gate RYY](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ising-yy-gate.html): The YY-generated two-qubit rotation, one of the three Cartan directions that classify every two-qubit entangler.
- [Ising Coupling Gate RZZ](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ising-zz-gate.html): A diagonal two-qubit phase gate generated by the ZZ interaction, the entangling core of QAOA and phase-sum circuits.
- [Magic Basis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/magic-basis-gate.html): A special maximally entangled basis in which two-qubit gate analysis and the KAK decomposition become tractable.
- [Margolus Gate (Relative-Phase Toffoli)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/margolus-gate.html): A simplified Toffoli that flips the target correctly but allows one extra sign, cheaper to build and safe when uncomputed.
- [Multi-Controlled X Gate (MCX)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multi-controlled-x-gate.html): Flips a target qubit only when every one of several control qubits is set, the multi-input generalization of CNOT and Toffoli.
- [Mølmer-Sørensen Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/molmer-sorensen-gate.html): The native entangling gate of trapped-ion processors, driving two or more ions through a shared motional mode.
- [Native Gate Sets](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/native-gate-sets.html): The small collections of physically executable gates that define what each quantum hardware platform can do directly.
- [Parity Gates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/parity-gates.html): Gates that compute or phase according to the parity of a set of qubits, central to error-correction stabilizer checks.
- [Pauli-X Gate (NOT)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pauli-x-gate.html): The Pauli-X gate is the quantum NOT — it flips |0⟩ and |1⟩ and rotates the Bloch vector 180° about the x-axis.
- [Pauli-Y Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pauli-y-gate.html): The Pauli-Y gate combines a bit flip and a phase flip — a 180° rotation of the Bloch vector about the y-axis.
- [Pauli-Z Gate (Phase Flip)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pauli-z-gate.html): The Pauli-Z gate flips the phase of |1⟩ while leaving |0⟩ alone — a 180° rotation about the z-axis.
- [Peres Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/peres-gate.html): A three-qubit reversible gate combining a Toffoli and a CNOT, a compact primitive for reversible arithmetic.
- [Phase Gate P(φ)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/phase-gate.html): The general phase gate P(φ) adds an arbitrary phase φ to |1⟩ — the parametric family that contains S (φ=π/2) and T (φ=π/4).
- [Quantum Logic Gates — How to Read Them](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-gate-basics.html): A one-page primer on reading quantum gates: unitaries, circuit symbols, the Bloch sphere, and why reversibility matters.
- [Quantum Shannon Decomposition](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-shannon-decomposition.html): A recursive method that breaks any n-qubit unitary into two-qubit gates, achieving near-optimal CNOT counts.
- [Quantum Transpilation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-transpilation.html): The full compiler pass that rewrites an abstract circuit into one a specific device can run efficiently.
- [RZX Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rzx-gate.html): A parametric ZX-interaction gate, the ideal operation realized by the cross-resonance drive and a flexible pulse-efficient primitive.
- [Rx(θ) Rotation Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rx-gate.html): Rx(θ) rotates a qubit by an arbitrary angle θ about the x-axis — a continuous, parametric bit-axis rotation.
- [Ry(θ) Rotation Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ry-gate.html): Ry(θ) rotates a qubit about the y-axis by θ — the real-valued rotation that moves amplitude between |0⟩ and |1⟩ without adding a phase.
- [Rz(θ) Rotation Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rz-gate.html): Rz(θ) rotates a qubit about the z-axis — a pure phase between |0⟩ and |1⟩, often free or nearly free on hardware.
- [S Gate (Phase, √Z)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/s-gate.html): The S gate is a quarter-turn phase gate — the square root of Z — adding a 90° phase to |1⟩.
- [SWAP Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/swap-gate.html): The SWAP gate exchanges the states of two qubits — essential for routing information across hardware where qubits aren't all connected.
- [Solovay-Kitaev Theorem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/solovay-kitaev-theorem.html): Guarantees that any discrete universal gate set fills the unitary group efficiently, with only polylogarithmic overhead.
- [Square-Root SWAP Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sqrt-swap-gate.html): A gate that, applied twice, exchanges two qubits, and applied once produces a half-swap that is a universal entangler.
- [Square-Root iSWAP Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sqrt-iswap-gate.html): A partial exchange gate, the entangler that many superconducting processors calibrate as their fundamental two-qubit operation.
- [T Gate (π/8, ⁴√Z)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/t-gate.html): The T gate is the non-Clifford π/8 gate — the ingredient that lifts a quantum computer from classically simulable to universal.
- [The Pauli Group](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pauli-group.html): The group generated by the Pauli matrices with phases, the algebraic backbone of stabilizer codes and error correction.
- [Toffoli Gate (CCX)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/toffoli-gate.html): The Toffoli gate flips the target only when both controls are |1⟩ — a reversible AND, and a universal gate for classical logic on a quantum computer.
- [Two-Qubit KAK Decomposition](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/two-qubit-kak-decomposition.html): The Cartan factorization that splits any two-qubit gate into local rotations around a canonical entangling core.
- [U1 Phase Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/u1-phase-gate.html): A single-parameter diagonal gate that phases the one-state, implementable as a zero-cost virtual frame change.
- [U2 Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/u2-gate.html): A two-parameter single-qubit gate fixing the polar angle at ninety degrees, the workhorse for superposition creation.
- [U3 General Single-Qubit Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/u3-general-single-qubit-gate.html): The three-parameter gate that realizes any single-qubit unitary up to global phase, the universal one-qubit primitive.
- [Weyl Chamber of Two-Qubit Gates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/weyl-chamber.html): The tetrahedral map of all inequivalent two-qubit entangling operations, one point per local-equivalence class.
- [XX+YY Exchange Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/xx-plus-yy-gate.html): An excitation-conserving two-qubit gate that mixes the single-excitation states while leaving zero- and double-excitation states fixed.
- [ZYZ Euler Decomposition](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/zyz-euler-decomposition.html): Any single-qubit gate as three rotations about the Z and Y axes, the standard way to lower a 2x2 unitary to hardware.
- [fSim Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fsim-gate.html): A two-parameter fermionic-simulation gate that captures a tunable exchange plus a controlled phase in one native operation.
- [iSWAP Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/iswap-gate.html): The iSWAP swaps two qubits and adds an i phase — a natural entangling gate for superconducting and spin qubits.
- [√X Gate (SX)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sqrt-x-gate.html): The √X gate is the square root of NOT — apply it twice and you get a bit flip. It is a native gate on much of today's superconducting hardware.

### Fusion Codes
- [1D Core Transport Solvers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/transport-solvers-1d.html): One-dimensional transport codes evolve plasma density, temperature, and current profiles along the minor radius using flux-surface-averaged conservation laws.
- [Activation and Dose Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/activation-and-dose-codes.html): Activation codes compute the radioactive inventory that neutrons induce in materials, and dose codes turn that inventory into radiation fields for shielding and safety.
- [Activation and Inventory Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/activation-inventory-codes.html): Activation codes evolve the nuclide inventory of materials under neutron irradiation, predicting radioactivity, decay heat, and waste classification over time.
- [Atomic and Nuclear Data for Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/atomic-data-for-codes.html): Fusion codes are only as accurate as the atomic, molecular, and nuclear data they consume: cross-sections, rates, and decay data underpin every result.
- [Beam-Tracing Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/beam-tracing-codes.html): Beam-tracing codes extend ray tracing to finite-width Gaussian beams, capturing diffraction and focusing that a zero-width ray cannot represent.
- [Blanket Thermal-Hydraulics Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/blanket-thermal-hydraulics-codes.html): Thermal-hydraulics codes model heat removal and coolant flow in the blanket, turning neutron heating into temperatures and stresses.
- [Bootstrap Current Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bootstrap-current-models.html): Bootstrap-current models predict the self-generated plasma current that arises from the pressure gradient, a key term in current-profile and scenario codes.
- [Bounce-Averaged Fokker-Planck Solvers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bounce-averaged-fokker-planck.html): Bounce averaging reduces the Fokker-Planck equation by averaging over fast orbital bounce motion, isolating the slow evolution of the distribution.
- [CAD-to-Neutronics Workflows](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cad-to-neutronics-workflow.html): Converting engineering CAD geometry into transport-code models is a distinct workflow, since neutronics codes need watertight, analyzable representations.
- [Code Benchmarking and Cross-Verification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/code-benchmarking-fusion.html): Benchmarking runs independent codes on identical problems to build confidence, expose bugs, and establish reference solutions the community can trust.
- [Code Benchmarking and Validation Databases](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/code-benchmarking-databases.html): Curated databases of well-characterized cases give codes a common yardstick, turning validation from anecdote into systematic evidence.
- [Codes for Mirror and Open Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mirror-and-open-system-codes.html): Open-field-line configurations like magnetic mirrors need codes that model end losses, ambipolar potentials, and direct energy conversion rather than closed flux surfaces.
- [Collision Operators in Kinetic Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gyrokinetic-collision-operators.html): Collision operators model the small-angle Coulomb scattering that relaxes distributions, a subtle numerical component that shapes kinetic-code results.
- [Comparing Gyrokinetic Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gyrokinetic-code-comparison.html): Cross-verification and benchmarking of gyrokinetic codes builds confidence that turbulence predictions reflect physics rather than numerical artifacts.
- [Core-Edge Coupling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/core-edge-coupling.html): Core-edge coupling joins a core transport model to a separate edge and scrape-off-layer model so the boundary condition on the core is computed, not guessed.
- [Coupling Strategies and Operator Splitting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/coupling-strategies-operator-splitting.html): Operator splitting advances coupled physics one process at a time, a simple scheme whose accuracy and stability depend on how the pieces are ordered and iterated.
- [Data Provenance for Simulation Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-provenance-simulation.html): Provenance records the complete lineage of a simulation result, so any number can be traced to the exact code, inputs, and environment that produced it.
- [Data Standards and Schemas for Fusion Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-standards-and-schemas.html): Shared data schemas define a common language for plasma state so independently developed codes can exchange information without custom translation.
- [Deterministic Neutron Transport](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/deterministic-neutron-transport.html): Deterministic transport codes discretize the Boltzmann transport equation on grids in space, angle, and energy, complementing Monte-Carlo methods.
