- [Disruption Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/disruption-modeling.html): Disruption codes simulate the rapid loss of confinement and current, predicting the thermal, electromagnetic, and runaway-electron loads a device must survive.
- [Disruption Modeling Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/disruption-modeling-codes.html): Disruption codes model the fast loss of plasma confinement, predicting the thermal quench, current quench, forces, and heat loads on the machine.
- [Divertor Heat-Flux Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/divertor-heat-flux-modeling.html): Divertor modeling predicts the concentrated heat and particle loads on exhaust targets and the mitigation needed to keep them within material limits.
- [EFIT-Class Equilibrium Reconstruction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/efit-equilibrium-reconstruction.html): Reconstruction codes fit a Grad-Shafranov equilibrium to magnetic and kinetic measurements, giving the best-estimate flux map of a real discharge.
- [Edge Kinetic Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/edge-kinetic-codes.html): Edge kinetic codes solve the plasma distribution function across the separatrix, capturing turbulence and non-Maxwellian effects that edge fluid closures cannot represent.
- [Edge and Scrape-Off-Layer Fluid Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/edge-sol-fluid-codes.html): Edge fluid codes such as the SOLPS class model plasma and neutrals in the boundary region, predicting the heat and particle loads reaching the divertor.
- [Electromagnetic and Eddy-Current Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/electromagnetic-eddy-current-codes.html): Electromagnetic codes compute induced currents and forces in conducting structures during field changes, essential for control and disruption loads.
- [Electron-Cyclotron Heating and Current Drive](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ecrh-current-drive-modeling.html): ECRH modeling combines ray-tracing and Fokker-Planck physics to predict the highly localized heating and current drive from electron-cyclotron waves.
- [Energetic Particle Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/energetic-particle-codes.html): Energetic particle codes follow fast ions from heating and fusion reactions through their slowing-down, tracking losses, redistribution, and wall loads.
- [Equilibrium Reconstruction Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/equilibrium-reconstruction-codes.html): Reconstruction codes fit a Grad-Shafranov equilibrium to experimental magnetic and internal measurements, inferring the plasma state that best explains the data.
- [Equilibrium and Shape Control Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/equilibrium-control-codes.html): Shape-control codes link real-time equilibrium estimates to coil commands, holding the plasma boundary and X-point at their targets throughout a discharge.
- [Equilibrium-to-Transport Mapping](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/equilibrium-to-transport-mapping.html): Mapping converts a two-dimensional equilibrium into the flux-surface geometry and metric coefficients that one-dimensional transport solvers require.
- [Extended MHD Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/extended-mhd-codes.html): Extended MHD codes add two-fluid, gyroviscous, and Hall terms to the ideal picture, capturing physics between single-fluid MHD and full kinetics.
- [Fixed-Boundary Equilibrium Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fixed-boundary-equilibrium-codes.html): Fixed-boundary solvers prescribe the plasma edge shape and compute only the interior flux surfaces, trading realism for speed and precision.
- [Fixed-Boundary Equilibrium Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fixed-boundary-equilibrium.html): When the plasma shape is prescribed, fixed-boundary solvers compute the interior equilibrium accurately and efficiently for stability and transport studies.
- [Flux-Tube versus Global Gyrokinetics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gyrokinetic-flux-tube-vs-global.html): Gyrokinetic simulations trade domain size for cost: flux-tube runs are local and cheap, global runs capture large-scale structure at far higher expense.
- [Fokker-Planck Current-Drive Solvers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fokker-planck-current-drive.html): Fokker-Planck solvers evolve the plasma distribution under collisions and wave-driven diffusion to predict non-inductive current drive and heating.
- [Fokker-Planck Solvers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fokker-planck-solvers.html): Fokker-Planck codes evolve the velocity-space distribution of a particle species under collisions and wave forces, quantifying heating and current drive.
- [Free-Boundary Equilibrium Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/free-boundary-equilibrium-codes.html): Free-boundary solvers compute the plasma shape and position self-consistently with external coil currents rather than prescribing the boundary.
- [Free-Boundary Equilibrium Solvers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/free-boundary-equilibrium-solvers.html): Free-boundary codes solve the plasma equilibrium together with the external coil fields, letting the plasma shape and boundary emerge from the solution.
- [Full-Wave ICRF Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/icrf-full-wave-codes.html): Full-wave codes solve Maxwell's equations in the plasma for ion-cyclotron waves, capturing interference and mode conversion that ray-tracing cannot.
- [Global Gyrokinetic Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/global-gyrokinetics.html): Global gyrokinetic codes simulate turbulence across a macroscopic plasma volume, retaining profile variation and long-wavelength transport that flux-tube codes omit.
- [Gyrofluid Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gyrofluid-codes.html): Gyrofluid codes take velocity-space moments of the gyrokinetic equation and add closures that mimic kinetic effects, trading accuracy for speed.
- [Gyrokinetic Turbulence Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gyrokinetic-turbulence-codes.html): Gyrokinetic codes simulate the microturbulence that dominates cross-field transport by solving a reduced kinetic equation on the gyro-averaged distribution.
- [HPC Coupling of Multiphysics Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hpc-multiphysics-coupling.html): Coupling multiphysics codes on high-performance computers requires moving data between parallel programs efficiently while keeping the coupled solution stable.
- [High-Performance Computing for Fusion Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/high-performance-computing-fusion.html): The most demanding fusion simulations run on supercomputers, and how codes parallelize across many processors and accelerators shapes what is feasible.
- [Ideal MHD Stability Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ideal-mhd-stability-codes.html): Ideal magnetohydrodynamic stability codes test whether a plasma equilibrium is stable to large-scale distortions by evaluating a potential-energy functional.
- [Impurity Transport Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/impurity-transport-codes.html): Impurity transport codes follow non-fuel ions through their charge states, predicting radiation, dilution, and accumulation in the plasma core.
- [Integrated Modeling Frameworks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/integrated-modeling-frameworks.html): Integrated frameworks orchestrate many physics codes into one self-consistent whole-device simulation, passing data between equilibrium, transport, heating, and edge modules.
- [Integrated Modeling Suites](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/integrated-modeling-suites.html): Integrated modeling frameworks orchestrate many physics codes behind a common data model, so equilibrium, transport, heating, and stability run as one workflow.
- [Irradiation Damage Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/irradiation-damage-modeling.html): Damage codes predict how energetic neutrons degrade materials over time, from atomic displacements to swelling, embrittlement, and property change.
- [Kinetic Edge Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/kinetic-edge-codes.html): Kinetic edge codes resolve the non-Maxwellian particle distributions of the boundary plasma, capturing physics that fluid edge models approximate.
- [Kinetic-MHD and Hybrid Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/kinetic-mhd.html): Kinetic-MHD codes couple a fluid bulk plasma to a kinetic treatment of energetic particles, capturing wave-particle resonances fluid models cannot.
- [Linear Ideal MHD Stability Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/linear-ideal-mhd-stability-codes.html): Ideal MHD stability codes test whether an equilibrium is stable to small perfectly conducting perturbations by solving an eigenvalue problem.
- [Local Gyrokinetic Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/local-gyrokinetics.html): Local (flux-tube) gyrokinetic codes simulate microturbulence in a small volume along one field line, delivering transport fluxes at modest cost.
- [MCNP-Class Radiation Transport](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mcnp-class-transport.html): MCNP-class codes are established general-purpose Monte-Carlo transport tools, long used as reference standards for neutronics, shielding, and dosimetry.
- [Magnetic Diagnostics for Equilibrium Reconstruction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/magnetic-diagnostics-for-reconstruction.html): Flux loops, magnetic probes, and Rogowski coils supply the measurements that equilibrium reconstruction codes fit, and their modeling is part of the code chain.
- [Mesh Generation for Fusion Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mesh-generation-for-fusion.html): Mesh generation builds the computational grids fusion codes solve on, aligning them to magnetic geometry while handling singular features like the X-point.
- [Mirror and Open-Field-Line Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mirror-and-open-field-codes.html): Open-field-line configurations such as magnetic mirrors need dedicated codes for confinement, end losses, and stability that differ from tokamak tools.
- [Monte Carlo Neutral Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/monte-carlo-neutral-codes.html): Monte Carlo neutral codes launch and follow statistical sample particles through collision physics to tally plasma sources in realistic geometry.
- [Monte-Carlo Neutronics Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/monte-carlo-neutronics.html): Monte-Carlo neutron transport follows individual particle histories through complex geometry to compute flux, heating, activation, and tritium breeding.
- [Neoclassical Transport Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neoclassical-transport-codes.html): Neoclassical codes compute collisional transport in toroidal geometry, including the bootstrap current that self-generates from the pressure gradient.
- [Neutral Beam Injection Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neutral-beam-injection-codes.html): Neutral-beam codes model how injected fast neutrals ionize, deposit, and slow down in the plasma, delivering heating, current, fueling, and rotation.
- [Neutral Particle Transport Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neutral-particle-transport.html): Neutral transport codes track un-ionized atoms and molecules through the plasma, supplying the fueling, recycling, and charge-exchange sources the plasma models need.
- [Neutral-Particle Transport at the Edge](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neutral-particle-transport-edge.html): Kinetic neutral codes track atoms and molecules recycling from surfaces, a physics essential to fueling, radiation, and divertor detachment.
- [Neutron Transport Codes for Fusion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neutron-transport-codes-fusion.html): Neutron transport codes track fusion neutrons through the blanket and structure to predict heating, breeding, and shielding.
- [Nonlinear MHD Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/nonlinear-mhd-codes.html): Nonlinear MHD codes evolve large-amplitude instabilities in time, following islands, sawteeth, ELMs, and disruptions past the linear regime.
- [OpenMC and Open-Source Neutronics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/openmc-overview.html): OpenMC is an open-source Monte-Carlo particle transport code widely used for fusion neutronics, with a scriptable interface and modern geometry support.
- [Pedestal and ELM Stability Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pedestal-and-elm-codes.html): Pedestal codes predict the height of the edge transport barrier and the stability limit that triggers edge-localized modes.
- [Pedestal and ELM Stability Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/peeling-ballooning-elm-codes.html): Peeling-ballooning codes predict the height of the edge pedestal and the onset of edge-localized modes that set the plasma boundary condition.
- [Pellet Ablation Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pellet-ablation-codes.html): Pellet ablation codes model how a frozen fuel or impurity pellet erodes as it flies into the plasma, setting fueling depth and injection strategy.
- [Pellet Fueling and Ablation Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pellet-fueling-codes.html): Pellet codes model how frozen fuel pellets ablate as they enter the plasma, predicting where fuel is deposited and how the density profile responds.
- [Plasma Control Simulation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-control-simulation.html): Control simulation codes model the plasma response to actuators so shape, position, and profile controllers can be designed and tested before operation.
- [Plasma Control Simulation Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-control-simulation-codes.html): Control simulation codes model the plasma as a dynamic system with sensors and actuators to design and test the feedback that holds a discharge.
- [Plasma Edge Fluid Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-edge-fluid-codes.html): Edge fluid codes solve Braginskii transport equations on a field-aligned mesh coupled to a Monte Carlo neutral model to predict divertor and scrape-off-layer plasma.
- [Predictive Transport Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/predictive-transport-codes.html): Predictive transport codes forecast plasma profiles for a proposed scenario by combining transport models, sources, and self-consistent equilibrium.
- [Provenance and Data Lineage](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/provenance-and-data-lineage.html): Provenance records the full history of a result: which codes, versions, inputs, and machines produced it, so any number can be traced to its origin.
- [Quasilinear Transport Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quasilinear-transport-models.html): Quasilinear models estimate turbulent transport quickly by combining linear gyrokinetic growth rates with a saturation rule, bridging first-principles codes and transport solvers.
- [RF Full-Wave Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rf-full-wave-codes.html): Full-wave codes solve the Maxwell wave equation in the plasma directly, capturing interference, mode conversion, and short-wavelength effects ray tracing omits.
- [Ray-Tracing Heating Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ray-tracing-heating-codes.html): Ray-tracing codes follow electromagnetic wave beams through the plasma along the geometric-optics path, computing where heating and current-drive power deposit.
- [Reproducible Simulation Pipelines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reproducible-simulation-pipelines.html): A reproducible pipeline lets anyone with the inputs regenerate a result exactly, through pinned environments, versioned data, and automated execution.
- [Resistive MHD Stability Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/resistive-mhd-stability-codes.html): Resistive stability codes admit finite resistivity, allowing reconnection and slow-growing tearing and resistive-wall modes that ideal analysis misses.
- [Resistive MHD and Nonlinear Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/resistive-mhd-stability.html): Resistive MHD codes allow magnetic field lines to reconnect, capturing tearing modes and the slower, nonlinear instabilities that ideal theory cannot describe.
- [Runaway Electron Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/runaway-electron-codes.html): Runaway electron codes model the birth and avalanche of relativistic electrons during disruptions and the schemes that dissipate them safely.
- [SOL and Edge Transport Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sol-edge-transport-codes.html): Scrape-off-layer codes model the open-field-line plasma between the separatrix and the wall, where parallel transport, recycling, and radiation set the heat load on surfaces.
- [Sawtooth and Internal Mode Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sawtooth-and-internal-modes.html): Sawtooth models describe the periodic core reconnection that flattens central profiles, a recurring instability that codes must predict and, ideally, control.
- [Scoping and Optimization Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/scoping-and-optimization-codes.html): Optimization codes search the design or operating space for points that maximize an objective subject to physics and engineering constraints.
- [Scoping and Point-Design Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tokamak-scoping-codes.html): Scoping codes rapidly evaluate candidate machine parameters using analytic scalings, mapping the operating space before detailed design begins.
- [Sensitivity Analysis in Code Workflows](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sensitivity-analysis-codes.html): Sensitivity analysis ranks which inputs most influence an output, focusing effort on the parameters that actually control a prediction.
- [Sputtering and Erosion Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sputtering-and-erosion-codes.html): Sputtering codes compute how incident ions eject surface atoms through collision cascades, providing the erosion yields wall models require.
- [Structural Finite-Element Analysis for Fusion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/structural-fea-fusion.html): Finite-element structural codes predict stress, deformation, and fatigue in fusion components under mechanical, thermal, and electromagnetic loads.
- [Superconducting Magnet Quench Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/superconducting-magnet-quench-codes.html): Quench codes model the transition of a superconducting magnet to the normal state, predicting temperature, voltage, and the protection a coil needs.
- [Surrogate Models and Machine Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/surrogate-models-ml-fusion.html): Surrogate models approximate expensive physics codes with fast learned functions, enabling real-time control, large scans, and optimization at reduced fidelity.
- [Surrogate Models in Code Workflows](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/surrogate-models-in-workflows.html): Surrogate models approximate expensive physics codes with fast statistical or machine-learned functions, enabling scans that would otherwise be infeasible.
- [Systems and Design Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/systems-design-codes.html): Systems codes use reduced physics and engineering models to size a whole device rapidly, exploring the trade space before detailed simulation.
- [TRANSP-Class Integrated Analysis Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/transp-integrated-analysis.html): Integrated analysis codes such as TRANSP combine equilibrium, transport, heating, and diagnostics into one time-dependent interpretation of a discharge.
- [Tearing Mode and Island Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tearing-mode-modeling.html): Specialized codes track magnetic islands from onset to saturation, predicting when tearing modes threaten confinement and how to suppress them.
- [The Kronos 81-Analysis Reproducible Suite](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/kronos-81-analysis-suite.html): Kronos organizes its design physics as a suite of independent, reproducible analyses, each versioned, provenance-tracked, and regenerable from its inputs.
- [The Reproducibility Toolchain](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reproducibility-toolchain.html): A reproducibility toolchain pins code versions, environments, inputs, and randomness so a simulation result can be regenerated exactly by anyone later.
- [Thermal-Hydraulics and CFD Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/thermal-hydraulics-codes.html): Thermal-hydraulic and computational-fluid-dynamics codes predict how coolant removes heat from fusion components and keeps temperatures within limits.
- [Transport Solver Frameworks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/transport-solver-frameworks.html): Transport solvers evolve the flux-surface-averaged density, temperature, and current profiles by integrating conservation equations with fluxes supplied by physics models.
- [Tritium Breeding Simulation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tritium-breeding-simulation.html): Neutronics codes compute the tritium breeding ratio of a blanket, the key figure of merit for a self-sufficient deuterium-tritium fuel cycle.
- [Uncertainty Propagation in Code Workflows](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/uncertainty-propagation-workflows.html): Uncertainty propagation carries input uncertainties through a chain of codes to produce honest error bars on the final predictions.
- [Verification and Validation Workflows](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/verification-and-validation-workflows.html): Verification checks that a code solves its equations correctly; validation checks that those equations describe reality. Both are needed to trust a prediction.
- [Verification, Validation, and Uncertainty Quantification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/verification-validation-uq.html): V&V and UQ establish whether a code solves its equations correctly, whether those equations describe reality, and how confident a prediction can be.
- [Wall and Plasma-Material Interaction Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/wall-pmi-codes.html): PMI codes model erosion, deposition, fuel retention, and material evolution at surfaces where the plasma meets the wall.
- [Workflow Orchestration Engines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/workflow-orchestration-engines.html): Orchestration engines schedule, connect, and manage the many code executions that make up an integrated fusion simulation.
- [Workflow Orchestration for Simulation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/workflow-orchestration-fusion.html): Orchestration tools run multi-code simulation pipelines reliably at scale, managing dependencies, parallelism, failures, and the data passed between steps.

### Quantum Algorithms
- [Amplitude Amplification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/amplitude-amplification.html): Amplitude amplification is the generalization of Grover — it boosts the probability of any 'good' subspace quadratically, wrapping many algorithms in a speedup.
- [Amplitude Amplification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/amplitude-amplification-general.html): The general procedure behind Grover search: boosting the amplitude of a marked subspace by iterated reflections.
- [Amplitude Estimation Without Phase Estimation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/amplitude-estimation-without-phase-estimation.html): Near-term variants recover the marked amplitude from Grover-power measurements, avoiding the deep quantum Fourier transform.
- [Bernstein–Vazirani Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bernstein-vazirani-algorithm.html): Bernstein–Vazirani recovers a hidden bit-string s from a single query to a linear oracle — a full n-bit answer where classical needs n queries.
- [Block Encoding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/block-encoding.html): Embedding an arbitrary matrix as a sub-block of a larger unitary so it can act on quantum states.
- [Boson Sampling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/boson-sampling.html): A restricted photonic model whose output distribution is classically hard to sample, offering evidence for quantum computational advantage.
- [Bravyi-Kitaev Transformation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bravyi-kitaev-transformation.html): A fermion-to-qubit mapping that reduces Pauli operator weight from linear to logarithmic in the number of orbitals.
- [Continuous-Time Quantum Walk](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/continuous-time-quantum-walk.html): A quantum walk that evolves under a graph Hamiltonian, requiring no coin register.
- [Cross-Entropy Benchmarking](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cross-entropy-benchmarking.html): A statistical test that estimates the fidelity of a random circuit's output by how often it produces high-probability bitstrings.
- [Deutsch–Jozsa Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/deutsch-jozsa-algorithm.html): Deutsch–Jozsa decides whether a black-box function is constant or balanced in a single query — the first clean, exponential quantum-classical separation.
- [Discrete-Time Quantum Walk](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/discrete-time-quantum-walk.html): A coined quantum walk whose step alternates a coin operator with a conditional shift, producing ballistic spreading.
- [Fixed-Point Grover Search](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fixed-point-grover-search.html): A variant of Grover search that converges monotonically to the target, eliminating the risk of overshooting the solution.
- [Gaussian Boson Sampling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gaussian-boson-sampling.html): A photonic sampling model using squeezed light instead of single photons, easier to scale and tied to matrix hafnians.
- [Grover Search with Multiple Targets](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/grover-with-multiple-targets.html): How Grover's algorithm behaves when several items are marked, and how to tune iterations when the count is unknown.
- [Grover's Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/grovers-algorithm.html): Grover's algorithm finds a marked item in an unsorted database of N entries in about √N steps — a quadratic speedup over any classical search.
- [HHL Algorithm (Quantum Linear Systems)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hhl-algorithm.html): HHL solves linear systems Ax=b with an exponential speedup in dimension — under conditions — by encoding the solution in a quantum state.
- [HHL Conditioning and Caveats](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hhl-conditioning-and-caveats.html): The fine print behind the HHL speedup: condition number, state preparation, readout, and when the exponential advantage survives.
- [Hamiltonian Simulation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hamiltonian-simulation.html): Simulating how a quantum system evolves under its Hamiltonian is the original motivation for quantum computing — and where a fusion company's physics interest is sharpest.
- [Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/harrow-hassidim-lloyd-algorithm.html): The HHL algorithm prepares a quantum state proportional to the solution of a linear system, with runtime polylogarithmic in dimension under strong assumptions.
- [Iterative Phase Estimation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/iterative-phase-estimation.html): Estimating an eigenphase one bit at a time using a single ancilla qubit and classical feedback.
- [Jordan-Wigner Transformation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/jordan-wigner-transformation.html): The canonical mapping that turns fermionic creation and annihilation operators into qubit Pauli operators.
- [Kitaev Phase Estimation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/kitaev-phase-estimation.html): A single-ancilla phase estimation scheme that reconstructs the eigenphase from measurement statistics without an inverse Fourier transform.
- [Measurement Error Mitigation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/measurement-error-mitigation.html): Correcting readout errors by characterizing and inverting the confusion between prepared and measured bitstrings.
- [Phase Kickback](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-phase-kickback.html): Phase kickback is the trick where a controlled operation pushes an eigenphase back onto the control qubit — the mechanism behind most quantum speedups.
- [Probabilistic Error Cancellation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/probabilistic-error-cancellation.html): Inverting the hardware noise channel by sampling from a quasi-probability representation of its inverse.
- [QAOA (Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qaoa.html): QAOA is a hybrid algorithm for combinatorial optimization — it alternates problem and mixing layers to approximate good solutions to hard discrete problems.
- [QAOA Parameter Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qaoa-parameter-optimization.html): Strategies for choosing and training the angles that control a Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm circuit.
- [QAOA for Constrained Selection Problems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qaoa-for-portfolio-optimization.html): Casting selection under a budget constraint as a QUBO and solving it with the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm.
- [QAOA for MaxCut](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qaoa-for-maxcut.html): The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm applied to graph MaxCut, its canonical benchmark problem.
- [QAOA for Scheduling Problems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qaoa-for-scheduling.html): Encoding job assignment and ordering constraints as an Ising cost function for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm.
- [Quantum Advantage: Definitions and Distinctions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-advantage-definitions.html): Separating contrived sampling supremacy from practical, useful, and provable quantum advantage.
- [Quantum Amplitude Estimation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-amplitude-estimation.html): A quantum routine that estimates the probability of a marked outcome quadratically faster than classical sampling.
- [Quantum Annealing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-annealing.html): Quantum annealing seeks the ground state of an optimization problem by slowly evolving from an easy Hamiltonian to the problem Hamiltonian, using quantum tunnelling to escape local minima.
- [Quantum Approximate Counting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-approximate-counting.html): Estimating the number of solutions to a search problem quadratically faster than classical sampling, without finding them.
- [Quantum Chemistry Workflow](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-chemistry-workflow.html): The end-to-end pipeline from a molecular Hamiltonian to a ground-state energy estimate on a quantum computer.
- [Quantum Counting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-counting.html): Quantum counting combines Grover's operator with phase estimation to count how many solutions exist — not just find one.
- [Quantum Counting Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-counting-algorithm.html): Combining Grover's operator with phase estimation to count the exact number of marked items in a search space.
- [Quantum Error Mitigation Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-error-mitigation-overview.html): Techniques that reduce the effect of noise on quantum results without the full overhead of error correction.
- [Quantum Feature Maps and Kernels](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-feature-maps-and-kernels.html): Encoding classical data into quantum states to define similarity measures that may be hard to compute classically.
- [Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-fourier-transform.html): The QFT is the quantum analogue of the discrete Fourier transform — implemented in O(n²) gates instead of O(n2ⁿ), it is the engine inside Shor and phase estimation.
- [Quantum Imaginary-Time Evolution](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-imaginary-time-evolution.html): Approximating the projection onto a Hamiltonian's ground state by simulating evolution in imaginary time.
- [Quantum Linear Algebra](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-linear-algebra.html): A toolkit of primitives - block encoding, linear combination of unitaries, and singular value transformation - for manipulating matrices as quantum operations.
- [Quantum Metropolis Sampling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-metropolis-sampling.html): A quantum analog of the Metropolis algorithm that samples from the thermal (Gibbs) distribution of a quantum Hamiltonian.
- [Quantum Monte Carlo Integration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-monte-carlo-integration.html): Estimating expectation values and integrals with a quadratic reduction in sample complexity using amplitude estimation.
- [Quantum Phase Estimation (QPE)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-phase-estimation.html): Phase estimation reads the eigenphase of a unitary onto a register of qubits — the workhorse subroutine behind Shor, HHL, and quantum chemistry.
- [Quantum Phase Estimation: Worked Example](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-phase-estimation-worked-example.html): A step-by-step walkthrough estimating the eigenphase of a single-qubit unitary using a small ancilla register.
- [Quantum Principal Component Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-principal-component-analysis.html): Extracting the dominant eigenvectors of a density matrix by using multiple copies of it as a Hamiltonian.
- [Quantum Singular Value Transformation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-singular-value-transformation.html): A unifying framework that applies polynomial functions to the singular values of a block-encoded matrix.
- [Quantum Support Vector Machine](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-support-vector-machine.html): Two distinct approaches to quantum classification: fast kernel evaluation and linear-system-based training.
- [Quantum Supremacy Experiments](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-supremacy-experiments.html): Milestone demonstrations that a quantum processor performed a sampling task infeasible for classical supercomputers.
- [Quantum Teleportation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-teleportation.html): Teleportation transfers an unknown qubit state using a shared entangled pair and two classical bits — no faster-than-light communication, but the backbone of quantum networks.
- [Quantum Walk Search on Graphs](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-walk-search-on-graphs.html): Using quantum walks to find marked vertices faster than classical random walks, generalizing Grover search to graph structure.
- [Quantum Walks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-walk.html): Quantum walks are the quantum analogue of random walks — they spread quadratically faster and underpin fast algorithms for search and graph problems.
- [Quantum k-Means Clustering](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantum-k-means-clustering.html): Accelerating the assignment step of k-means using quantum distance estimation and amplitude amplification.
- [Random Circuit Sampling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/random-circuit-sampling.html): Running a random quantum circuit and sampling its output, the task behind superconducting quantum advantage demonstrations.
- [Shor's Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/shors-algorithm.html): Shor's algorithm factors large integers in polynomial time — the result that put quantum computing on the map and threatens RSA encryption.
- [Simon's Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/simons-algorithm.html): Simon's algorithm finds a hidden period of a 2-to-1 function exponentially faster than any classical method — the direct inspiration for Shor.
- [Superdense Coding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/superdense-coding.html): Superdense coding sends two classical bits by transmitting a single qubit — the mirror image of teleportation, powered by shared entanglement.
- [Szegedy Quantum Walk](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/szegedy-quantum-walk.html): A construction that turns any classical Markov chain into a quantum walk, quadratically shrinking hitting and mixing times.
- [The SWAP Test](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/swap-test.html): The SWAP test estimates how similar two quantum states are — the overlap |⟨ψ|φ⟩|² — using a controlled-SWAP and a single measured qubit.
- [VQE Hardware-Efficient Ansatz](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/vqe-hardware-efficient-ansatz.html): Shallow parameterized circuits built from a device's native gates, chosen for trainability on noisy hardware rather than physical fidelity.
- [VQE UCCSD Ansatz](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/vqe-uccsd-ansatz.html): The unitary coupled-cluster singles-and-doubles trial state, a chemistry-motivated ansatz with built-in physical structure.
- [Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/variational-quantum-eigensolver.html): VQE finds the lowest energy of a quantum system using a hybrid loop — a parameterized quantum circuit tuned by a classical optimizer — and is a leading near-term algorithm.
- [Variational Quantum Eigensolver Workflow](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/variational-quantum-eigensolver-workflow.html): The hybrid loop that estimates a Hamiltonian's ground-state energy by minimizing a parameterized quantum circuit's expectation value.
- [Variational Quantum Imaginary-Time Evolution](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/variational-quantum-imaginary-time-evolution.html): Following the imaginary-time ground-state trajectory within a parameterized ansatz by evolving its parameters.
- [Variational Quantum Linear Solver](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/variational-quantum-linear-solver.html): A near-term hybrid method that solves linear systems by minimizing a cost function measuring how far Ax deviates from b.
- [Zero-Noise Extrapolation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/zero-noise-extrapolation.html): Deliberately amplifying noise, measuring the result at several noise levels, and extrapolating back to the zero-noise limit.

### Machine Learning
- [ARIMA Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/arima-models.html): ARIMA forecasts a series by combining autoregression, differencing for trend, and a moving average of past errors.
- [Active Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/active-learning.html): Active learning lets a model choose which unlabeled examples to have labeled, spending scarce annotation where it helps most.
- [Additive Decomposition Forecasting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/prophet-style-forecasting.html): Additive forecasters model a series as an interpretable sum of trend, seasonal, and holiday components with uncertainty.
- [Alternating Least Squares](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/alternating-least-squares.html): ALS fits matrix-factorization models by alternately solving closed-form least-squares problems for each factor.
- [Anomaly Detection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/anomaly-detection.html): Anomaly detection flags rare, unexpected observations, usually with few or no labeled examples of the anomalies.
- [Automated Machine Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/automl.html): AutoML automates the pipeline of feature processing, model selection, and tuning to build models with less manual effort.
- [Backpropagation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/backpropagation.html): Backpropagation computes a neural network's loss gradients efficiently by applying the chain rule backward through the layers.
- [Bagging](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bagging.html): Bagging trains models on bootstrap resamples and averages them, cutting variance without raising bias.
- [Baum-Welch Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/baum-welch-algorithm.html): Baum-Welch learns HMM transition and emission parameters from unlabeled sequences by expectation-maximization.
- [Bayesian Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bayesian-optimization.html): Bayesian optimization efficiently optimizes expensive black-box functions by modeling them and choosing where to sample next.
- [Bias-Variance Tradeoff](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bias-variance-tradeoff.html): Prediction error splits into bias, variance, and noise; reducing one of the first two often raises the other.
- [Boosting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/boosting-overview.html): Boosting turns weak learners into a strong one by training them in sequence, each focusing on the previous errors.
- [Categorical Encoding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/one-hot-encoding.html): Categorical encoding turns non-numeric labels into numbers a model can use, with one-hot, ordinal, and target schemes.
- [Classification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/classification-overview.html): Classification predicts a discrete label for each input, from spam-or-not to many mutually exclusive categories.
- [Clustering](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/clustering-overview.html): Clustering groups unlabeled points by similarity; the method and distance you pick define what a cluster even means.
- [Collaborative Filtering](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/collaborative-filtering.html): Collaborative filtering recommends items by finding patterns in the preferences of many users, without item content.
- [Conditional Random Fields](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/conditional-random-fields.html): CRFs are discriminative models for structured prediction that score whole label sequences given the full input.
- [Confusion Matrix](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/confusion-matrix.html): A confusion matrix tabulates predicted against actual classes, exposing exactly which errors a classifier makes.
- [Contrastive Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/contrastive-learning.html): Contrastive learning trains representations by pulling similar examples together and pushing dissimilar ones apart.
- [Counterfactual Explanations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/counterfactual-explanations.html): A counterfactual explanation states the smallest change to an input that would flip the model decision.
- [Curriculum Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/curriculum-learning.html): Curriculum learning orders training examples from easy to hard, mirroring how humans learn structured material.
- [Curse of Dimensionality](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/curse-of-dimensionality.html): As dimensions grow, data grows sparse and distances lose meaning, undermining distance-based methods and demanding more data.
- [DBSCAN](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dbscan.html): DBSCAN finds clusters as dense regions separated by sparse ones, discovering their number and flagging outliers as noise.
- [Data Augmentation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-augmentation.html): Data augmentation expands a training set by applying label-preserving transformations, improving generalization and robustness.
- [Data Leakage](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-leakage.html): Data leakage lets information unavailable at prediction time slip into training, inflating scores that collapse in production.
- [Decision Trees](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/decision-trees.html): A decision tree splits data on feature thresholds into a flowchart of rules, readable and nonlinear but prone to overfitting.
- [Dimensionality Reduction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dimensionality-reduction-overview.html): Dimensionality reduction compresses many features into a few, aiding visualization, speed, and defeating sparsity.
- [Elastic Net](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/elastic-net.html): Elastic net blends L1 and L2 penalties, gaining lasso's sparsity and ridge's stability with correlated features.
- [Ensemble Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ensemble-methods.html): Ensembles combine many models so their errors cancel, usually beating any single model through bagging, boosting, or stacking.
- [Entropy and Information Gain](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/entropy-information-gain.html): Entropy measures disorder in a set of labels; information gain, the drop in entropy from a split, guides decision trees.
- [Expectation-Maximization Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/em-algorithm.html): EM iteratively fits models with latent variables by alternating a soft-assignment step with a maximum-likelihood update.
- [Exponential Smoothing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/exponential-smoothing.html): Exponential smoothing forecasts by averaging past values with weights that decay geometrically into the past.
- [Fairness and Bias in Machine Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fairness-and-bias.html): Fairness in ML studies how models can encode or amplify social bias, and the trade-offs among competing fairness definitions.
- [Feature Engineering](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/feature-engineering.html): Feature engineering transforms raw data into inputs that expose the signal, often mattering more than the choice of model.
- [Feature Scaling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/feature-scaling.html): Feature scaling puts numeric features on a comparable range so distance- and gradient-based models are not skewed by units.
- [Feature Selection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/feature-selection.html): Feature selection keeps the informative inputs and drops the rest, reducing overfitting, cost, and complexity.
- [Federated Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/federated-learning.html): Federated learning trains a shared model across many devices or sites without moving their raw data to a central server.
- [Forward-Backward Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/forward-backward-algorithm.html): Forward-backward computes exact state posteriors in a hidden Markov model by two passes of dynamic programming.
- [Gaussian Mixture Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gaussian-mixture-models.html): A Gaussian mixture models data as a weighted sum of several Gaussian components, giving soft, probabilistic clustering.
- [Gradient Boosting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gradient-boosting.html): Gradient boosting builds an additive ensemble of small trees, each fitting the residual errors of those before it.
- [Handling Class Imbalance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/class-imbalance-handling.html): Class imbalance arises when one class dominates; naive training then ignores the rare class that usually matters most.
- [Hidden Markov Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hidden-markov-models.html): An HMM models a sequence of observations generated by a hidden state that evolves as a Markov chain.
- [Hierarchical Clustering](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hierarchical-clustering.html): Hierarchical clustering builds a tree of nested groups, letting you read clusters at any granularity from a dendrogram.
- [Hyperparameter Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperparameter-optimization.html): Hyperparameter optimization searches for the training settings, learning rate, depth, regularization, that yield the best model.
- [Hyperparameter Tuning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperparameter-tuning.html): Hyperparameters set before training, learning rate, depth, regularization, are searched to find the best model configuration.
- [Imbalanced Classification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/imbalanced-classification.html): When one class is rare, standard training and accuracy fail; resampling, reweighting, and better metrics restore balance.
- [Implicit-Feedback Recommendation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/implicit-feedback-recommendation.html): Implicit feedback infers preference from behavior like clicks and plays, where non-interaction is ambiguous.
- [Isolation Forest](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/isolation-forest.html): Isolation forest detects anomalies by how quickly random partitioning isolates a point from the rest.
- [K-Means Clustering](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/k-means-clustering.html): K-means partitions data into k clusters by alternately assigning points to the nearest center and recomputing centers.
- [K-Nearest Neighbors](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/k-nearest-neighbors.html): k-NN classifies or predicts a point by looking at its k closest training examples, storing all data and computing at query time.
- [Kernel Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/kernel-methods.html): Kernel methods compute inner products in a high-dimensional space implicitly, letting linear algorithms learn nonlinear patterns.
- [Knowledge Distillation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/knowledge-distillation.html): Distillation trains a small student model to mimic a large teacher, transferring its behavior into a cheaper package.
- [LIME Explanations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lime-explanations.html): LIME explains one prediction by fitting a simple, interpretable model to the black box behavior nearby.
- [Lasso Regression](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lasso-regression.html): Lasso regression adds an L1 penalty to least squares, driving weights to zero so it selects features while it fits.
- [Learning Curves](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/learning-curves.html): Learning curves plot error against training-set size or training progress, diagnosing whether more data or a better model helps.
- [Local Outlier Factor](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/local-outlier-factor.html): The local outlier factor scores anomalies by comparing a point density to the density of its neighbors.
- [Loss Functions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/loss-functions.html): A loss function scores how wrong a prediction is; minimizing it over the data is what training actually optimizes.
- [MLOps](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mlops.html): MLOps applies engineering discipline to the full machine-learning lifecycle: data, training, deployment, monitoring, and iteration.
- [Matrix Factorization for Recommendation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/matrix-factorization.html): Matrix factorization embeds users and items in a shared latent space so their dot product predicts preference.
- [Metric Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/metric-learning.html): Metric learning trains an embedding where distance reflects semantic similarity, enabling retrieval and verification.
- [Model Drift and Monitoring](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-drift-monitoring.html): Deployed models degrade as the world changes; monitoring detects data and concept drift so models can be retrained in time.
- [Model Interpretability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-interpretability.html): Interpretability methods explain why a model made a prediction, supporting trust, debugging, and accountability.
- [Model Pruning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-pruning.html): Pruning removes redundant weights or structures from a trained network to make it smaller and faster.
- [Model Quantization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-quantization.html): Quantization shrinks and speeds up models by storing and computing weights in low-precision integers instead of floats.
- [Model Selection and the No Free Lunch Theorem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-selection.html): No single algorithm wins everywhere; model selection compares candidates fairly to find the best fit for a given problem.
- [Multi-Armed Bandits](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multi-armed-bandits.html): Bandit algorithms balance exploring uncertain options against exploiting the best-known one to maximize cumulative reward.
- [Multi-Task Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multi-task-learning.html): Multi-task learning trains one model on several related tasks so shared structure improves all of them.
- [Multiclass Classification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multiclass-classification.html): Multiclass classification assigns one of several mutually exclusive labels, using softmax or by decomposing into binary problems.
- [Naive Bayes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/naive-bayes.html): Naive Bayes applies Bayes' rule with a strong independence assumption, giving a fast, surprisingly effective probabilistic classifier.
- [Neural Architecture Search](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neural-architecture-search.html): Neural architecture search automates designing network structures, searching over layers and connections for the best design.
- [One-Class SVM](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/one-class-svm.html): A one-class SVM learns a boundary that encloses normal data, treating outside points as anomalies.
- [Overfitting and Underfitting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/overfitting-underfitting.html): Overfitting memorizes training noise and fails on new data; underfitting is too simple to capture real structure.
- [Permutation Importance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/permutation-importance.html): Permutation importance ranks features by how much a model performance drops when a feature values are shuffled.
- [Precision, Recall, and F1](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/evaluation-metrics-classification.html): Precision, recall, and their harmonic mean F1 measure classifier quality where raw accuracy misleads on imbalanced data.
- [Principal Component Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pca.html): PCA finds orthogonal directions of maximum variance, giving a linear projection that compresses data with minimal loss.
- [Probability Calibration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/probability-calibration.html): A calibrated model outputs probabilities that match observed frequencies, so a 0.7 prediction is right about 70 percent of the time.
- [ROC and AUC](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/roc-auc.html): The ROC curve traces true-positive against false-positive rate across thresholds; AUC summarizes it in one number.
- [Random Forests](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/random-forests.html): A random forest averages many decorrelated decision trees, cutting variance for strong, robust tabular predictions.
- [Regression Metrics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/regression-metrics.html): Regression metrics such as MSE, MAE, and R-squared quantify how far continuous predictions fall from the truth.
- [Regularization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/regularization.html): Regularization constrains a model to prefer simpler solutions, trading a little training fit for better generalization.
- [Ridge Regression](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ridge-regression.html): Ridge regression adds an L2 penalty to least squares, shrinking weights to reduce variance and tame correlated features.
- [SHAP Values](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/shap-values.html): SHAP attributes a prediction to its features using Shapley values, a fair-division rule from cooperative game theory.
- [SMOTE and Synthetic Oversampling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/smote-oversampling.html): SMOTE balances classes by creating synthetic minority examples along lines between real minority neighbors.
- [Saliency Maps](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/saliency-maps.html): Saliency maps highlight which parts of an input a neural network relied on, usually via gradients of the output.
- [Seasonal Decomposition](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/seasonal-decomposition.html): Decomposition splits a time series into trend, seasonal, and remainder parts to reveal and model each separately.
- [Self-Supervised Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/self-supervised-learning.html): Self-supervised learning creates its own labels from unlabeled data by hiding part of the input and predicting it.
- [Semi-Supervised Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/semi-supervised-learning.html): Semi-supervised learning combines a small labeled set with a large unlabeled one to train better than labels alone allow.
- [Stationarity and Autocorrelation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/stationarity-and-autocorrelation.html): Stationarity means a series statistics do not change over time; autocorrelation measures how a series relates to its own lags.
- [Supervised Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/supervised-learning.html): Supervised learning fits a function from labeled examples so it can predict labels for new, unseen inputs.
- [Support Vector Machines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/support-vector-machines.html): An SVM finds the boundary with the widest margin between classes, using kernels to draw nonlinear separators.
- [Temperature Scaling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/temperature-scaling.html): Temperature scaling recalibrates a neural network confidence with a single learned parameter, without changing predictions.
- [The Kalman Filter](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/kalman-filter.html): The Kalman filter tracks a continuous hidden state over time by fusing a linear motion model with noisy measurements.
- [Time-Series Forecasting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/time-series-forecasting.html): Time-series forecasting predicts future values of a temporally ordered signal from its own past and covariates.
- [Train/Validation/Test Split](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/train-val-test-split.html): Splitting data into training, validation, and test sets keeps model selection honest and the final estimate unbiased.
- [UMAP](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/umap.html): UMAP is a fast nonlinear embedding that preserves local and some global structure, useful for both visualization and features.
- [Unsupervised Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/unsupervised-learning.html): Unsupervised learning finds structure in data that carries no labels: groups, low-dimensional coordinates, or a density.
- [Viterbi Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/viterbi-algorithm.html): Viterbi finds the single most probable hidden state sequence in an HMM using dynamic programming over paths.
- [XGBoost](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/xgboost.html): XGBoost is a fast, regularized gradient-boosting library that dominates tabular benchmarks through engineering and second-order optimization.
- [t-SNE](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/t-sne.html): t-SNE is a nonlinear method that maps high-dimensional data to 2-D or 3-D, preserving local neighborhoods for visualization.

### Neural Architectures
- [Activation Functions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/activation-functions.html): Activation functions inject the nonlinearity that gives deep networks their expressive power, and their shape controls how gradients flow.
- [AdamW Optimizer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adamw-optimizer.html): AdamW fixes how Adam applies weight decay, decoupling it from the adaptive gradient scaling to make regularization behave as intended.
- [Augmented Neural ODEs](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/augmented-neural-ode.html): Augmenting a neural ODE with extra state dimensions removes a fundamental expressiveness limit caused by trajectories that cannot cross.
- [Autoencoders](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/autoencoders.html): Autoencoders learn compact representations by training a network to reconstruct its own input through a narrow bottleneck.
- [Autoregressive Language Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/autoregressive-language-modeling.html): Autoregressive models factor the probability of a sequence into a product of conditional next-token probabilities, the foundation of generative text models.
- [BERT and Masked Language Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bert-masked-language-models.html): BERT is a bidirectional transformer encoder pretrained by predicting randomly masked tokens, producing context-rich representations for classification and extraction tasks.
- [BERT and Masked Language Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bert-masked-language-modeling.html): BERT pretrains a bidirectional transformer encoder by predicting masked words, producing representations that read context from both directions.
- [Backpropagation Through Time](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/backpropagation-through-time.html): BPTT trains recurrent networks by unrolling the loop over time and applying the chain rule across every step.
- [Batch Normalization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/batch-normalization.html): Batch normalization standardizes layer activations across a mini-batch, stabilizing and accelerating the training of deep networks.
- [CLIP and Contrastive Multimodal Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/clip-contrastive-multimodal.html): CLIP trains an image encoder and a text encoder together so that matching image-caption pairs land nearby in a shared embedding space.
- [Capsule Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/capsule-networks.html): Capsule networks represent entities as vectors whose length encodes presence and whose orientation encodes properties, aiming to preserve part-whole spatial relationships.
- [Contrastive Loss and Metric Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/contrastive-loss-metric-learning.html): Metric learning trains embeddings so that distance reflects semantic similarity, using contrastive objectives that attract similar items and repel dissimilar ones.
- [Convolutional Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/convolutional-neural-networks.html): CNNs exploit the spatial structure of images by sharing small filters across a grid, learning local patterns that compose into global understanding.
- [Cross-Attention](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cross-attention.html): Cross-attention lets one sequence attend to another, the bridge that connects an encoder's representation to a decoder's generation.
- [Decoder-Only Language Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gpt-decoder-only-models.html): Decoder-only transformers predict the next token from all previous tokens, using causal masking so a single model both learns from and generates text.
- [Dense Connectivity (DenseNet)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dense-connectivity-densenet.html): DenseNet connects each layer to every earlier layer by concatenation, maximizing feature reuse and gradient flow with few parameters.
- [DenseNet](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/densenet.html): DenseNet connects every layer to all later layers by concatenation, maximizing feature reuse and gradient flow with few parameters.
- [Diffusion Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/diffusion-models.html): Diffusion models generate data by learning to reverse a gradual noising process, denoising random noise step by step into a sample.
- [Dilated Causal Convolutions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dilated-causal-convolutions.html): Dilated causal convolutions insert gaps between kernel taps to widen the receptive field exponentially while keeping outputs strictly dependent on the past.
- [Dilated Convolutions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dilated-convolutions.html): Dilated (atrous) convolutions insert gaps between kernel elements to expand the receptive field without adding parameters or losing resolution.
- [Dropout](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dropout.html): Dropout randomly disables neurons during training, forcing the network to build redundant, robust features and reducing overfitting.
- [Dynamic Routing Between Capsules](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dynamic-routing-capsules.html): Dynamic routing iteratively assigns lower-level capsule outputs to the higher-level capsules whose predictions they most agree with.
- [Embeddings](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/embeddings.html): An embedding maps discrete items into a continuous vector space where geometric closeness reflects semantic similarity.
- [Encoder-Decoder Architecture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/encoder-decoder-architecture.html): The encoder-decoder pattern separates understanding an input from generating an output, a template reused across many modern architectures.
- [Fine-Tuning Pretrained Encoders](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bert-fine-tuning.html): Fine-tuning adapts a pretrained encoder to a specific task by attaching a small head and continuing training with a low learning rate on labeled data.
- [Flash Attention](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/flash-attention.html): Flash attention computes exact attention faster by tiling the calculation to keep intermediate results in fast on-chip memory, never materializing the full score matrix.
- [Foundation Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/foundation-models.html): Foundation models are large networks pretrained on broad data that adapt to many downstream tasks, a shift from task-specific to general-purpose AI.
- [GELU and Swish](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gelu-swish-activations.html): Smooth, self-gated activations that behave like ReLU for large inputs but curve gently near zero, now standard in transformers and modern vision models.
- [GPT and Autoregressive Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gpt-autoregressive-models.html): Decoder-only transformers predict the next token given all previous ones, a simple objective that scales into general-purpose language models.
- [Gated Recurrent Unit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gru.html): The GRU is a streamlined gated recurrent cell that merges the LSTM's memory and gating into fewer parameters with often-similar performance.
- [Generative Adversarial Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/generative-adversarial-networks.html): GANs pit a generator against a discriminator in a game, training the generator to produce data realistic enough to fool its critic.
- [Graph Attention Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/graph-attention-networks.html): Graph attention networks weight the contribution of each neighbor with a learned attention coefficient, letting a node emphasize its most relevant connections.
- [Graph Convolutional Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/graph-convolutional-networks.html): Graph convolutional networks generalize convolution to graphs by averaging each node's features with its neighbors' using a normalized adjacency matrix.
- [Graph Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/graph-neural-networks.html): GNNs extend deep learning to graph-structured data by learning node representations from the pattern of connections around each node.
- [Group Normalization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/groupnorm.html): Group normalization splits channels into groups and normalizes within each group per sample, giving batch-independent normalization for vision models.
- [Highway Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/highway-networks.html): Highway networks use learned gates to control how much of each layer's input passes through unchanged versus transformed, an early route to training very deep networks.
- [Hypernetworks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hypernetworks.html): A hypernetwork is a network that generates the weights of another network, letting one model produce parameters adapted to a context or task.
- [LAMB Optimizer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lamb-optimizer.html): LAMB rescales each layer's update to match the norm of its weights, enabling stable training at very large batch sizes.
- [Layer Normalization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/layer-normalization.html): Layer normalization standardizes across features within a single example, making it independent of batch size and ideal for transformers.
- [Learning-Rate Schedules](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/learning-rate-schedules.html): A learning-rate schedule changes the step size over training, typically warming up then decaying, to balance fast early progress against stable final convergence.
- [Linear Attention](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/linear-attention.html): Linear attention replaces the softmax with a kernel feature map, reordering the computation so cost grows linearly rather than quadratically with sequence length.
- [Lion Optimizer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lion-optimizer.html): Lion updates each weight by the sign of a momentum-smoothed gradient, using less memory than Adam while remaining competitive on large models.
- [Long Short-Term Memory](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lstm.html): LSTM cells add a gated memory pathway that lets recurrent networks carry information across hundreds of steps without vanishing gradients.
- [Mamba and Selective State-Space Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mamba-selective-ssm.html): Mamba makes state-space model parameters depend on the input, giving content-aware selectivity with linear-time sequence processing and no attention matrix.
- [Memory-Augmented Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/memory-augmented-networks.html): Memory-augmented networks pair a controller with an external, addressable memory it can read from and write to, separating computation from storage.
- [Message Passing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/message-passing.html): Message passing is the unifying recipe of graph neural networks: gather from neighbors, aggregate symmetrically, then update each node.
- [Message-Passing Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/message-passing-neural-networks.html): The message-passing framework describes most graph neural networks as three steps: compute messages on edges, aggregate them at nodes, and update node states.
- [Mixture of Experts](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mixture-of-experts.html): Mixture-of-experts models route each input to a few specialized subnetworks, growing total capacity while keeping per-input computation low.
- [Mixture-of-Experts Routing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mixture-of-experts-routing.html): A mixture of experts routes each input to a few specialized subnetworks out of many, growing total capacity while keeping per-input computation low.
- [Multi-Head Attention](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multi-head-attention.html): Running several attention operations in parallel lets a model attend to different kinds of relationships at once, then combine them.
- [Multi-Query and Grouped-Query Attention](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multi-query-attention.html): Multi-query attention shares a single set of keys and values across all attention heads, shrinking the memory needed to cache them during generation.
- [Multilayer Perceptron](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multilayer-perceptron.html): Stacking layers of neurons with nonlinear activations turns a linear classifier into a universal function approximator.
- [Multimodal Fusion Strategies](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multimodal-fusion-strategies.html): Multimodal models combine signals from different modalities at different depths, trading simplicity against the richness of cross-modal interaction.
- [Neural Ordinary Differential Equations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neural-ode.html): Neural ODEs treat a network's depth as continuous time, defining the transformation as the solution of a differential equation parameterized by a neural network.
- [Neural Turing Machines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neural-turing-machines.html): A Neural Turing Machine couples a neural controller to a differentiable memory using content and location-based addressing, learning simple algorithms end to end.
- [Normalization Variants Compared](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/layer-normalization-variants.html): Batch, layer, instance, and group normalization differ only in which axes they compute statistics over, and that choice determines where each works best.
- [Normalizing Flows](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/normalizing-flows.html): Normalizing flows build generative models from invertible transformations, giving exact likelihoods where VAEs and GANs give only approximations.
- [Patch Embeddings and Positional Encoding in ViT](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/vit-patch-embeddings.html): Patch embedding turns a 2D image into a token sequence with one strided convolution, and position embeddings restore the spatial layout the transformer would otherwise ignore.
- [Pointer Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pointer-networks.html): Pointer networks use attention as the output itself, selecting positions in the input sequence rather than tokens from a fixed vocabulary.
- [Pooling Layers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pooling-layers.html): Pooling downsamples feature maps by summarizing local regions, shrinking resolution while building a degree of invariance to small shifts.
- [Positional Encoding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/positional-encoding.html): Because attention ignores order, transformers add positional encodings so the model knows where each token sits in the sequence.
- [RMSNorm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rmsnorm.html): RMSNorm normalizes activations by their root-mean-square alone, dropping the mean-centering of layer normalization for a cheaper, equally effective operation.
- [RMSprop Optimizer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rmsprop-optimizer.html): RMSprop scales each parameter's step by a running average of its squared gradients, adapting the learning rate per parameter to handle varying gradient magnitudes.
- [ReLU and Variants](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/relu-and-variants.html): The rectified linear unit is the default hidden activation of deep learning: cheap, non-saturating, and easy to differentiate.
- [Recurrent Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/recurrent-neural-networks.html): RNNs process sequences one step at a time, carrying a hidden state that acts as memory of everything seen so far.
- [ResNet and Skip Connections](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/resnet-skip-connections.html): Residual connections let a layer learn a correction to its input rather than a full transformation, making very deep networks trainable.
- [Residual Connections](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/residual-connections.html): A residual connection adds a layer's input to its output, letting networks learn refinements to the identity and making very deep stacks trainable.
- [Retrieval-Augmented Generation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/retrieval-augmented-generation.html): Retrieval-augmented generation fetches relevant documents from an external store and conditions a generative model on them, grounding outputs in retrievable knowledge.
- [Rotary Position Embeddings](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rotary-position-embeddings.html): Rotary position embeddings encode position by rotating query and key vectors, so attention depends on the relative distance between tokens.
- [Self-Attention](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/self-attention.html): Self-attention lets every position in a sequence attend to every other, building context-aware representations in a single parallel operation.
- [Sequence-to-Sequence Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sequence-to-sequence.html): Seq2seq models map an input sequence to an output sequence of different length using an encoder that reads and a decoder that generates.
- [Siamese Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/siamese-networks.html): Siamese networks pass two inputs through the same shared-weight encoder and compare their embeddings, learning similarity rather than fixed class labels.
- [Sigmoid and Tanh](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sigmoid-tanh-activations.html): The classic S-shaped activations squash inputs into bounded ranges; still useful at outputs and gates, but prone to vanishing gradients in deep hidden layers.
- [Sparse Attention](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sparse-attention.html): Sparse attention restricts each token to attend to a chosen subset of positions, cutting the quadratic cost of full attention while preserving important connections.
- [Spiking Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/spiking-neural-networks.html): Spiking neural networks communicate with discrete timed events rather than continuous values, modeling neurons that integrate inputs and fire when a threshold is crossed.
- [Structured State-Space Models (S4)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/state-space-models-s4.html): Structured state-space models represent a sequence layer as a linear dynamical system, computed as a long convolution to capture very long-range dependencies efficiently.
- [Surrogate Gradient Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/surrogate-gradient-learning.html): Surrogate gradients let spiking networks train with backpropagation by replacing the non-differentiable spike function's derivative with a smooth stand-in.
- [Temporal Convolutional Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/temporal-convolutional-networks.html): Temporal convolutional networks model sequences with stacked dilated causal convolutions, offering a parallel alternative to recurrent networks for time-series tasks.
- [The Attention Mechanism](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/attention-mechanism.html): Attention lets a model dynamically weight different parts of its input, focusing on what is relevant to each step of its output.
- [The Convolution Operation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/convolution-operation.html): Convolution slides a learnable kernel over an input, computing dot products that measure how strongly a local pattern is present at each position.
- [The Perceptron](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/perceptron.html): The perceptron is the simplest trainable neuron: a weighted sum passed through a threshold, and the historical seed of neural networks.
- [The Softmax Function](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/softmax-function.html): Softmax turns a vector of scores into a probability distribution, the standard output layer for multi-class classification and attention weights.
- [The Transformer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/the-transformer.html): The transformer builds sequence models entirely from attention and feedforward layers, enabling the parallel training that produced modern foundation models.
- [Tokenization and Subwords](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tokenization-subword.html): Tokenization splits text into the units a model processes; subword schemes balance vocabulary size against the ability to represent any word.
- [Transfer Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/transfer-learning.html): Transfer learning reuses knowledge from a model trained on a large dataset to solve a related task with far less data.
- [Transposed Convolution](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/transposed-convolution.html): Transposed convolution learns to upsample feature maps, the workhorse of decoders in autoencoders, segmentation networks, and generators.
- [Triplet Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/triplet-networks.html): Triplet networks learn embeddings from an anchor, a positive, and a negative example, enforcing that the anchor sits closer to the positive than to the negative.
- [U-Net](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/u-net.html): U-Net pairs a downsampling encoder with an upsampling decoder and skip connections, producing precise dense predictions like segmentation maps.
- [Vanishing and Exploding Gradients](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/vanishing-exploding-gradients.html): In deep and recurrent networks, gradients can shrink to nothing or blow up as they propagate, stalling or destabilizing training.
- [Variational Autoencoders](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/variational-autoencoders.html): VAEs turn the autoencoder into a generative model by mapping inputs to probability distributions over a smooth, sampleable latent space.
- [Vision Transformer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/vision-transformer.html): The Vision Transformer applies the pure transformer to images by cutting them into patches and treating each patch as a token.
- [Vision Transformer (ViT)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/vision-transformer-vit.html): The Vision Transformer treats an image as a sequence of patches and applies a standard transformer encoder, showing convolution is not required for strong image models.
- [Warmup and Cosine Decay](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/warmup-and-cosine-decay.html): The warmup-then-cosine schedule ramps the learning rate up briefly, then lowers it along a cosine curve to a small floor, a widely used default.
- [WaveNet](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/wavenet.html): WaveNet generates raw audio one sample at a time using a deep stack of dilated causal convolutions with gated activations, modeling waveforms directly.
