- [Weight Initialization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/weight-initialization.html): Weight initialization sets the starting values of parameters so that signals and gradients keep a stable scale through a deep network at the first step.
- [Word Embeddings](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/word-embeddings.html): Word embeddings learn vector representations of words from co-occurrence in text, placing words with similar meanings near one another.

### Reinforcement Learning
- [A Gridworld Worked Example](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-gridworld-example.html): A small gridworld makes the abstractions of MDPs, value functions, and value iteration concrete and inspectable.
- [A2C and A3C](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-a2c-a3c.html): A3C runs many parallel actor-critic workers asynchronously; A2C is its synchronous, simpler variant that often matches it.
- [Actor-Critic Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-actor-critic.html): Actor-critic methods pair a policy that acts with a value estimator that critiques, combining low-variance updates with direct policy optimization.
- [AlphaZero](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/alphazero-and-mcts.html): AlphaZero replaces MCTS rollouts with a learned network and trains purely by self-play from the rules alone.
- [Curiosity and Intrinsic Motivation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/curiosity-intrinsic-motivation.html): Intrinsic rewards drive exploration when the environment's own reward is sparse or absent.
- [DAgger: Dataset Aggregation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dagger-algorithm.html): DAgger fixes behavior cloning's drift by querying the expert on the states the learner itself visits.
- [Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-ddpg.html): DDPG is an off-policy actor-critic method for continuous control, learning a deterministic policy alongside a Q-function critic.
- [Deep Q-Networks (DQN)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-deep-q-networks.html): DQN scales Q-learning to high-dimensional inputs using a neural network, experience replay, and a slowly updated target network.
- [Deterministic Policy Gradients and DDPG](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/deterministic-policy-gradient-ddpg.html): DDPG learns a deterministic continuous-control policy off-policy, using a critic's action gradient to improve the actor.
- [Distributional RL and C51](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/distributional-rl-c51.html): Distributional RL learns the full distribution of returns, not just its mean, capturing risk and multi-modality.
- [Distributional Reinforcement Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-distributional-rl.html): Instead of predicting the mean return, distributional RL models the full distribution of possible returns, improving stability and risk awareness.
- [Domain Randomization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/domain-randomization-rl.html): Randomizing simulator parameters during training forces policies robust enough to treat reality as one more variation.
- [Double Q-Learning and Overestimation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-double-q-learning.html): The max in Q-learning systematically overestimates values; double Q-learning corrects it by decoupling action selection from evaluation.
- [Dynamic Programming for MDPs](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-dynamic-programming.html): When the environment model is known, dynamic programming solves an MDP exactly by iterating the Bellman equations over all states.
- [Experience Replay](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-experience-replay.html): Experience replay stores past transitions and reuses them in random minibatches, breaking correlations and improving sample efficiency.
- [Exploration Strategies in Deep RL](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-exploration-strategies.html): Beyond random actions, deep RL uses intrinsic curiosity, count bonuses, and posterior sampling to explore hard, sparse-reward tasks.
- [Exploration vs Exploitation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-exploration-vs-exploitation.html): An agent must balance exploiting what it knows to gain reward now against exploring the unknown to find something better.
- [Exploration with Upper Confidence Bounds](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/exploration-ucb.html): UCB explores by acting optimistically under uncertainty: prefer actions whose value might still be high.
- [Function Approximation in RL](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-function-approximation.html): When states are too many to tabulate, value functions and policies are represented by parameterized functions that generalize across states.
- [GAIL: Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adversarial-imitation-gail.html): GAIL imitates an expert by matching state-action distributions through an adversarial game, skipping explicit reward recovery.
- [Generalized Policy Iteration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-generalized-policy-iteration.html): Nearly every RL algorithm is a case of two processes — value estimation and policy improvement — pushing toward mutual consistency.
- [Goal-Conditioned RL](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/goal-conditioned-rl.html): A single goal-conditioned policy learns to reach any goal, turning many tasks into one parameterized problem.
- [Hierarchical RL and the Options Framework](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hierarchical-rl-options.html): Options are temporally extended actions that let an agent plan over skills rather than primitive steps.
- [Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-hierarchical-rl.html): Hierarchical RL decomposes long tasks into reusable sub-behaviors, letting a high-level policy select among temporally extended options.
- [Hindsight Experience Replay](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hindsight-experience-replay.html): HER turns failures into learning by relabeling trajectories with the goals that were actually achieved.
- [Imitation Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-imitation-learning.html): Imitation learning trains a policy to mimic expert demonstrations, bypassing reward design when good examples are available.
- [Imitation Learning and Behavior Cloning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/imitation-learning-behavior-cloning.html): Behavior cloning turns imitation into supervised learning: predict the expert's action from the state.
- [Inverse Reinforcement Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/inverse-reinforcement-learning.html): Inverse RL recovers the reward function that best explains observed expert behavior, then optimizes it.
- [Inverse Reinforcement Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-inverse-rl.html): Inverse RL infers the reward function that best explains observed expert behavior, rather than optimizing a given reward.
- [Markov Decision Processes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-markov-decision-process.html): A Markov decision process formalizes sequential decision making as states, actions, transition probabilities, rewards, and a discount factor.
- [Meta-Reinforcement Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/meta-reinforcement-learning.html): Meta-RL learns how to learn, producing agents that adapt to a new task within a handful of episodes.
- [Model-Based RL and Dyna](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-based-rl-dyna.html): Dyna blends real experience with simulated experience from a learned model to accelerate value learning.
- [Model-Based Reinforcement Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-model-based-rl.html): Model-based RL learns a model of the environment's dynamics and uses it to plan or generate simulated experience.
- [Model-Predictive Control and RL](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-predictive-control-rl.html): MPC plans a short action sequence with a model, executes one step, then replans, and pairs naturally with learned models.
- [Monte Carlo Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-monte-carlo-methods.html): Monte Carlo methods learn values from complete episodes by averaging the actual returns that follow each state.
- [Monte Carlo Tree Search](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mcts-fundamentals.html): MCTS builds an asymmetric search tree by repeated simulation, focusing effort on the most promising moves.
- [Monte Carlo Tree Search](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-monte-carlo-tree-search.html): Monte Carlo tree search plans by selectively growing a search tree, balancing promising moves against unexplored ones through sampled rollouts.
- [MuZero](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/muzero.html): MuZero plans with a learned model of dynamics in a latent space, so it needs no access to the true game rules.
- [Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multi-agent-rl.html): When many learning agents share an environment, each faces a moving target: the others are learning too.
- [Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-multi-agent-rl.html): When several learning agents share an environment, each faces a moving target as the others adapt, reshaping the learning problem.
- [Multi-Armed Bandits](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bandit-algorithms.html): The bandit is RL stripped to one decision: choose among actions with unknown payoffs to maximize total reward.
- [Multi-Armed Bandits](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-multi-armed-bandits.html): The multi-armed bandit is the simplest reinforcement learning problem, isolating exploration versus exploitation with no state transitions.
- [Multi-Objective RL](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multi-objective-rl.html): When several goals conflict, multi-objective RL seeks the Pareto front of policies rather than a single optimum.
- [Offline RL: Conservative Q-Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/offline-rl-cql.html): CQL learns from a fixed dataset by pushing down Q-values on unseen actions, preventing overestimation of out-of-distribution behavior.
- [Offline RL: Implicit Q-Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/offline-rl-iql.html): IQL learns entirely within the dataset by never evaluating actions it has not seen, using expectile regression on the value function.
- [Offline Reinforcement Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-offline-rl.html): Offline RL learns policies entirely from a fixed dataset of logged experience, without any further interaction with the environment.
- [Offline-to-Online RL](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/offline-to-online-rl.html): Pretrain a policy on logged data, then fine-tune it with limited online interaction, combining safety and adaptability.
- [On-Policy vs Off-Policy Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-on-policy-vs-off-policy.html): On-policy methods learn about the policy they follow; off-policy methods learn about one policy from data generated by another.
- [PETS: Probabilistic Ensembles with Trajectory Sampling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pets-probabilistic-ensembles.html): PETS captures model uncertainty with an ensemble of probabilistic networks and plans with sampling-based model-predictive control.
- [POMDPs and Belief States](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pomdp-belief-states.html): When the agent cannot observe the full state, it must act on a belief, a probability distribution over states.
- [Partial Observability and POMDPs](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-partial-observability.html): When the agent cannot observe the full state, it must act on incomplete information and maintain beliefs about what it cannot see.
- [Policies](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-policies.html): A policy is the agent's behavior: a rule, deterministic or stochastic, that maps states to actions.
- [Policy Iteration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-policy-iteration.html): Policy iteration alternates full policy evaluation with greedy improvement, converging to an optimal policy in a finite number of steps.
- [Prioritized Experience Replay](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/prioritized-experience-replay.html): Replay transitions in proportion to how surprising they are, so the agent learns fastest from its biggest errors.
- [Proximal Policy Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-ppo.html): PPO improves policies with a clipped objective that permits several update steps per batch while preventing destructively large policy changes.
- [Q-Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-q-learning.html): Q-learning is an off-policy temporal-difference method that learns the optimal action-value function regardless of how the agent explores.
- [Quantile Regression DQN](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantile-regression-dqn.html): QR-DQN represents the return distribution by learned quantile locations, removing C51's fixed value grid.
- [REINFORCE](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-reinforce.html): REINFORCE is the simplest policy-gradient algorithm, updating policy parameters using Monte Carlo returns as the action weight.
- [RL for Continuous Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-continuous-control.html): Continuous action spaces demand policy-gradient and actor-critic methods rather than discrete value maximization.
- [RL for Tokamak and Plasma Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-tokamak-plasma-control.html): Deep RL has been applied, in published work, to control the magnetic shape of tokamak plasmas.
- [RL from Human Feedback](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-rlhf.html): RLHF learns a reward model from human preference judgments, then optimizes a policy against it to align behavior with human intent.
- [Rainbow DQN](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rainbow-dqn.html): Rainbow combines six independent improvements to DQN and shows they are largely complementary.
- [Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rlhf-human-feedback.html): RLHF trains a reward model from human preference comparisons, then optimizes a policy against it.
- [Return and Discounting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-return-and-discounting.html): The return is the cumulative reward an agent seeks to maximize; the discount factor sets how much future reward counts against the present.
- [Reward Hacking](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reward-hacking-rl.html): Agents optimize the reward you write, not the goal you meant; the gap between them is reward hacking.
- [Reward Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reward-modeling.html): A reward model is a learned proxy for what we want, standing in for a true objective that is hard to specify.
- [Reward Shaping](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reward-shaping-rl.html): Reward shaping adds guidance signals to speed learning, but only potential-based shaping is guaranteed to be safe.
- [Reward Shaping](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-reward-shaping.html): Reward shaping adds guidance signals to sparse rewards to speed learning, but poorly designed shaping can change what the agent learns.
- [SARSA](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-sarsa.html): SARSA is an on-policy temporal-difference control method that learns the value of the policy it actually follows, including its exploration.
- [Safe RL and Constrained MDPs](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/safe-rl-constrained-mdps.html): Safe RL maximizes reward subject to constraints, so the agent respects safety limits during and after learning.
- [Safety in Reinforcement Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-safe-rl.html): Safe RL seeks policies that respect constraints and avoid harmful behavior during both learning and deployment.
- [Sample Efficiency in RL](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-sample-efficiency.html): How much interaction an algorithm needs to learn is often the deciding factor when environment steps are slow or costly.
- [Self-Play](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/self-play-rl.html): In self-play an agent improves by competing against copies of itself, generating an ever-stronger curriculum.
- [Sim-to-Real Transfer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sim-to-real-transfer.html): Policies trained in simulation must survive the reality gap; domain randomization and adaptation help them cross it.
- [Sim-to-Real Transfer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-sim-to-real.html): Policies trained in simulation must bridge the reality gap to work on physical systems, using randomization and robust training.
- [Soft Actor-Critic](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/soft-actor-critic-sac.html): SAC maximizes reward plus policy entropy, giving a stable, sample-efficient, exploration-friendly control algorithm.
- [Soft Actor-Critic (SAC)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-soft-actor-critic.html): SAC is an off-policy actor-critic that maximizes reward plus policy entropy, yielding robust exploration and strong continuous control.
- [States, Actions, and Rewards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-states-actions-rewards.html): The three raw ingredients of any reinforcement learning problem: what the agent sees, what it can do, and how it is scored.
- [Successor Features and Representations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/successor-features-rl.html): Successor representations factor value into expected future state occupancy times reward, enabling fast transfer.
- [TD(lambda) and Eligibility Traces](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-td-lambda.html): TD(lambda) blends one-step temporal-difference learning and Monte Carlo returns using eligibility traces to assign credit over multiple steps.
- [TD3: Twin Delayed DDPG](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/td3-twin-delayed.html): TD3 fixes DDPG's overestimation with twin critics, delayed policy updates, and smoothed target actions.
- [Temporal-Difference Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-temporal-difference-learning.html): Temporal-difference learning updates value estimates from one step of experience by bootstrapping off its own next estimate.
- [The Advantage Function](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-advantage-function.html): The advantage function measures how much better an action is than the policy's average, sharpening the learning signal for policy gradients.
- [The Agent-Environment Loop](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-agent-environment-loop.html): Every reinforcement learning problem is a cycle: observe a state, act, receive reward and next state, repeat.
- [The Bellman Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-bellman-equation.html): The Bellman equation expresses a value as immediate reward plus the discounted value of what follows, making long-horizon value recursive.
- [The Bellman Optimality Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-bellman-optimality.html): The Bellman optimality equation replaces the policy average with a maximum, characterizing the value of acting optimally.
- [The Credit Assignment Problem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-credit-assignment.html): When reward arrives long after the actions that earned it, the agent must figure out which decisions deserve credit or blame.
- [The Exploration-Exploitation Trade-off](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/exploration-exploitation-tradeoff.html): Every learning agent must balance taking known-good actions against gathering information about uncertain ones.
- [The Markov Property](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-markov-property.html): A state is Markov when it captures all history relevant to the future, so the past adds nothing once the present is known.
- [The Policy Gradient Theorem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-policy-gradient-theorem.html): The policy gradient theorem gives the gradient of expected return with respect to policy parameters without differentiating the environment.
- [Thompson Sampling in RL](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/thompson-sampling-rl.html): Thompson sampling explores by acting greedily with respect to a randomly sampled belief about the world.
- [Trust Region Policy Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-trpo.html): TRPO improves a policy while limiting how far it moves, using a constraint on policy change to guarantee monotonic improvement.
- [Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-td3.html): TD3 fixes DDPG's overestimation and instability with twin critics, delayed policy updates, and target smoothing.
- [Value Functions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-value-functions.html): A value function estimates expected future return, giving the agent a way to compare states and actions without simulating the full future.
- [Value Iteration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-value-iteration.html): Value iteration solves an MDP by repeatedly applying the Bellman optimality update to every state until the value function stops changing.
- [What Is Reinforcement Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-what-is-reinforcement-learning.html): Reinforcement learning trains an agent to choose actions that maximize cumulative reward through trial-and-error interaction with an environment.
- [World Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/world-models-rl.html): A world model learns to predict how an environment evolves, letting an agent train and plan inside its own simulation.

### Control Theory
- [Adaptive Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adaptive-control.html): Adaptive controllers adjust their own parameters online as the plant changes, maintaining performance without a fixed model.
- [Anti-Windup](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/anti-windup.html): Anti-windup schemes prevent an integrator from accumulating error while the actuator is saturated, avoiding large overshoot and sluggish recovery.
- [BIBO Stability and Impulse Response](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bibo-stability.html): Bounded-input bounded-output stability holds exactly when the impulse response is absolutely integrable, equivalent to left-half-plane poles.
- [Backstepping](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/backstepping-control.html): Backstepping builds a stabilizing nonlinear controller recursively, treating intermediate states as virtual controls step by step.
- [Block Diagrams and Signal Flow](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/block-diagrams.html): Block diagrams represent interconnected transfer functions; algebra on them reduces complex loops to a single input-output relation.
- [Bode Plots](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bode-plots.html): A Bode plot shows a system's gain and phase versus frequency on log scales, making loop shaping and margin reading direct.
- [Calculus of Variations for Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/calculus-of-variations-control.html): The calculus of variations finds functions that minimize integral cost functionals, the mathematical foundation of optimal control.
- [Cascade Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cascade-control.html): Cascade control nests a fast inner loop inside a slower outer loop so the inner loop rejects disturbances before they reach the primary variable.
- [Control Allocation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-allocation.html): Control allocation distributes a commanded virtual control among redundant actuators, respecting their limits and secondary objectives.
- [Control Systems Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-systems-overview.html): A control system drives a physical process toward desired behavior by shaping its inputs based on goals and measurements.
- [Controllability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/controllability.html): A system is controllable if the input can drive its state from any starting point to any target in finite time.
- [Controllability and Observability Gramians](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/controllability-observability-gramians.html): Gramians quantify how strongly states can be reached by inputs and seen by outputs, grading the degree of controllability and observability.
- [Dead-Time Compensation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dead-time-compensation.html): Dead-time compensation restores control performance to processes with transport delay by predicting or accounting for the delayed response.
- [Describing-Function Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/describing-function-analysis.html): The describing function approximates a nonlinearity by its gain to a sinusoid, extending frequency-domain analysis to predict limit cycles.
- [Describing-Function Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/describing-functions.html): The describing function approximates a nonlinearity by its gain to a sinusoid, letting frequency methods predict limit cycles.
- [Descriptor and Singular Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/descriptor-singular-systems.html): Descriptor systems mix differential and algebraic equations, capturing constraints and interconnections that ordinary state-space models cannot.
- [Discrete-Time Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/discrete-time-control.html): Digital controllers act at discrete sample instants, requiring difference equations, the z-transform, and attention to sampling effects.
- [Distributed Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/distributed-control.html): Distributed control coordinates many local controllers, each using limited local information, to achieve a global objective without a central authority.
- [Disturbance Rejection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/disturbance-rejection.html): Disturbance rejection is a control loop's ability to hold the output near its target despite unwanted inputs, governed by the sensitivity function.
- [Dual Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dual-control.html): Dual control balances two competing goals: controlling the plant well now and probing it to reduce uncertainty for better control later.
- [Duality of Controllability and Observability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/duality-controllability-observability.html): Controllability and observability are mirror images: each result about one becomes a result about the other by transposing the system.
- [Dynamic Programming in Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dynamic-programming-control.html): Dynamic programming solves sequential decision problems by working backward from the goal, building optimal policies from optimal subproblems.
- [Economic Model Predictive Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/economic-mpc.html): Economic MPC optimizes a general performance objective directly rather than tracking a setpoint, driving the plant toward the best operating regime.
- [Event-Triggered Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/event-triggered-control.html): Event-triggered control updates the control action only when a state-dependent condition signals that an update is needed, saving computation and communication.
- [Explicit Model Predictive Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/explicit-mpc.html): Explicit MPC precomputes the optimal control law offline as a piecewise-affine function of the state, replacing online optimization with a lookup.
- [Feedback Fundamentals](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/feedback-fundamentals.html): Feedback compares output to reference and acts on the difference, reshaping a system's dynamics through the closed-loop gain.
- [Feedback Linearization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/feedback-linearization.html): Feedback linearization cancels a system's nonlinearities with a change of coordinates and control, exposing linear dynamics for standard design.
- [Feedforward Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/feedforward-control.html): Feedforward acts on a measured reference or disturbance before it affects the output, complementing feedback's after-the-fact correction.
- [Frequency Response Basics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/frequency-response-basics.html): A system's frequency response is how it scales and phase-shifts sinusoids of each frequency, the basis of Bode and Nyquist analysis.
- [Gain Scheduling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gain-scheduling.html): Gain scheduling controls a nonlinear plant by interpolating a family of linear controllers designed at fixed operating points.
- [Gain and Phase Margin](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gain-and-phase-margin.html): Stability margins measure how much extra gain or phase lag a stable loop can tolerate before it begins to oscillate.
- [Gain and Phase Margins](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gain-phase-margins.html): Gain and phase margins quantify how much loop gain or phase lag a stable feedback system can absorb before it becomes unstable.
- [H-Infinity Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/h-infinity-control.html): H-infinity control minimizes the worst-case gain from disturbances to errors, giving a systematic route to robust multivariable design.
- [H-Infinity Optimal Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hinfinity-optimal-control.html): H-infinity control minimizes the worst-case gain from disturbances to regulated outputs, delivering guaranteed robustness against bounded uncertainty.
- [H2 Optimal Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/h2-optimal-control.html): H2 control minimizes the energy of the closed-loop response to white-noise or impulsive disturbances by minimizing a system's H2 norm.
- [Hybrid and Switched Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hybrid-switched-systems.html): Hybrid systems combine continuous dynamics with discrete transitions; switched systems select among continuous modes according to a switching signal.
- [Integral Quadratic Constraints](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/integral-quadratic-constraints.html): IQCs certify stability of uncertain and nonlinear feedback loops through frequency-domain quadratic bounds on the troublesome component's signals.
- [Integral Windup and Anti-Windup](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/integral-windup.html): When an actuator saturates, an integrator keeps accumulating error, causing large overshoot; anti-windup schemes prevent this.
- [Lead and Lag Compensation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lead-lag-compensation.html): Lead compensators add phase for speed and stability; lag compensators add low-frequency gain for accuracy; together they shape the loop.
- [Limit Cycles and Bifurcation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/limit-cycles-bifurcation.html): Limit cycles are isolated periodic orbits of nonlinear systems; bifurcations are qualitative changes in behavior as a parameter varies.
- [Linear Matrix Inequalities in Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/linear-matrix-inequalities-control.html): LMIs recast many control problems as convex feasibility or optimization over positive-definite matrices, solvable reliably by interior-point methods.
- [Linear Parameter-Varying Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/linear-parameter-varying-control.html): LPV control designs one controller for a family of linear models indexed by measurable parameters, guaranteeing performance across the whole operating envelope.
- [Linear-Quadratic Regulator (LQR)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lqr.html): LQR computes the state-feedback gain that minimizes a quadratic cost trading state error against control effort, yielding a robust optimal controller.
- [Linear-Quadratic-Gaussian Control (LQG)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lqg.html): LQG combines an LQR optimal feedback gain with a Kalman filter estimator to control a noisy system using only its measured outputs.
- [Loop Shaping](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/loop-shaping.html): Loop shaping designs a controller by directly molding the open-loop frequency response to meet performance and robustness specifications.
- [Loop Transfer Recovery](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/loop-transfer-recovery.html): LTR tunes an LQG design so the observer-based loop recovers the robustness margins of the ideal full-state feedback loop.
- [Lyapunov Redesign](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lyapunov-redesign.html): Lyapunov redesign adds a robustifying term to a nominal controller so a known Lyapunov function keeps decreasing despite matched uncertainty.
- [Lyapunov Stability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lyapunov-stability.html): Lyapunov theory judges stability from an energy-like function, applying to nonlinear systems without solving their equations.
- [Lyapunov's Direct Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lyapunov-direct-method.html): The direct method proves stability by exhibiting a positive-definite function whose derivative along trajectories is negative.
- [Mixed H2/H-Infinity Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mixed-h2-hinfinity-control.html): Mixed synthesis optimizes average performance under an H2 objective while enforcing a hard worst-case robustness bound in the H-infinity norm.
- [Model-Predictive Control (MPC)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-predictive-control.html): MPC repeatedly solves an online optimization over a finite horizon, applies the first move, and re-plans, handling constraints directly.
- [Model-Reference Adaptive Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-reference-adaptive-control.html): MRAC adjusts controller parameters online so the plant output tracks the response of a chosen reference model despite unknown plant parameters.
- [Model-Reference Adaptive Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mrac.html): MRAC adjusts controller parameters online so the closed loop matches a chosen reference model despite plant uncertainty.
- [Moving-Horizon Estimation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/moving-horizon-estimation.html): MHE estimates states by solving a constrained optimization over a sliding window of recent measurements, the estimation dual of predictive control.
- [Multi-Agent Consensus](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multi-agent-consensus.html): Consensus protocols drive a network of agents to agree on a common value using only communication with neighbors.
- [Multivariable (MIMO) Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mimo-control.html): Multivariable systems have coupled inputs and outputs, so each actuator affects several variables, demanding coordinated design.
- [Networked Control Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/networked-control-systems.html): Networked control systems close feedback loops over shared communication networks, contending with delay, packet loss, jitter, and limited bandwidth.
- [Nonlinear Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/nonlinear-control.html): Nonlinear control handles systems where superposition fails, using tools like linearization, Lyapunov methods, and geometric techniques.
- [Nonlinear Model Predictive Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/nonlinear-mpc.html): Nonlinear MPC solves a constrained optimal control problem over a nonlinear model at each step, applying the first move and re-optimizing.
- [Nyquist Plots](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/nyquist-plots.html): The Nyquist plot traces the loop gain in the complex plane as frequency varies, encoding closed-loop stability in its encirclements.
- [Observability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/observability.html): A system is observable if its full internal state can be reconstructed from the outputs over a finite time interval.
- [Open Loop vs Closed Loop](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/open-loop-vs-closed-loop.html): Open-loop control commands blindly; closed-loop control measures the result and corrects, buying disturbance rejection and robustness.
- [Optimal Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/optimal-control.html): Optimal control finds the input that minimizes a cost functional subject to the system dynamics, unifying many design methods under one principle.
- [PID Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pid-control.html): The PID controller sums proportional, integral, and derivative action on the error, covering most industrial control needs with three tunable gains.
- [PID Tuning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pid-tuning.html): Tuning sets the three PID gains to balance speed, overshoot, and disturbance rejection, by rule, by model, or by iterative adjustment.
- [Passivity-Based Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/passivity-based-control.html): Passivity-based control exploits energy conservation and dissipation, ensuring stability because interconnecting passive systems remains passive.
- [Persistency of Excitation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/persistency-of-excitation.html): Persistent excitation is the richness condition on input signals that guarantees adaptive and identification algorithms converge to true parameters.
- [Phase-Plane Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/phase-plane-analysis.html): Phase-plane analysis studies second-order nonlinear systems by plotting trajectories in the plane of the two states, revealing global behavior at a glance.
- [Pole Placement by State Feedback](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pole-placement.html): State feedback u = -K x can move a controllable system's closed-loop poles to any chosen locations, setting its dynamics by design.
- [Poles and Zeros](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/poles-and-zeros.html): Poles set a system's natural modes and stability; zeros shape how those modes appear in the output, sometimes causing undershoot.
- [Pontryagin's Maximum Principle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pontryagin-maximum-principle.html): Pontryagin's principle gives necessary conditions for optimal control through a Hamiltonian and an adjoint costate system.
- [Ratio Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ratio-control.html): Ratio control holds two flows or quantities in a fixed proportion by driving one to track a scaled version of the other.
- [Robust Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/robust-control.html): Robust control guarantees stability and performance despite bounded uncertainty in the plant model, designing for the worst case.
- [Robust Model Predictive Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/robust-mpc.html): Robust MPC guarantees constraint satisfaction and stability for every disturbance in a bounded set, not just for the nominal prediction.
- [Root Locus](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/root-locus.html): The root locus traces how closed-loop poles move through the s-plane as a single gain is varied from zero to infinity.
- [Sampled-Data Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sampled-data-systems.html): Sampled-data systems mix a continuous plant with a discrete controller, requiring analysis of sampling, holds, and aliasing together.
- [Self-Triggered Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/self-triggered-control.html): Self-triggered control predicts the next update time at the current update, eliminating the continuous monitoring that event-triggered control requires.
- [Self-Tuning Regulators](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/self-tuning-regulators.html): A self-tuning regulator estimates plant parameters online and continually redesigns the controller as if the estimates were exact.
- [Sensitivity and Complementary Sensitivity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sensitivity-complementary-sensitivity.html): The sensitivity and complementary sensitivity functions summarize disturbance rejection, tracking, robustness, and noise attenuation in one algebraic identity.
- [Sensitivity and Complementary Sensitivity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sensitivity-functions.html): The sensitivity and complementary sensitivity functions quantify disturbance rejection and noise sensitivity, bound by the constraint that they sum to one.
- [Sliding-Mode Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sliding-mode-control.html): Sliding-mode control forces the state onto a stable surface and holds it there, giving strong robustness at the cost of chattering.
- [Sliding-Mode Control in Detail](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sliding-mode-control-detail.html): Sliding-mode control forces the state onto a designed surface and holds it there, giving strong robustness to matched uncertainty at the cost of chattering.
- [Smith Predictor](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/smith-predictor.html): The Smith predictor compensates for process dead time by using a model to predict the delayed output and control against the prediction.
- [Stability Fundamentals](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/stability-fundamentals.html): A system is stable if bounded inputs produce bounded outputs; for LTI systems this reduces to all poles lying in the left half-plane.
- [State Observers and the Luenberger Observer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/observers-luenberger.html): An observer reconstructs unmeasured states by running a model of the plant corrected by the difference between predicted and actual outputs.
- [State-Space Representation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/state-space-representation.html): State-space models describe a system by first-order equations in a state vector, handling multivariable and nonlinear dynamics naturally.
- [Steady-State Error and System Type](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/steady-state-error.html): Steady-state error is the residual tracking error after transients settle, set by the number of integrators in the open loop.
- [Stochastic Model Predictive Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/stochastic-mpc.html): Stochastic MPC handles random disturbances with chance constraints, enforcing limits with a specified probability rather than for the worst case.
- [System Identification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/system-identification.html): System identification builds mathematical models of dynamic systems from measured input-output data rather than first principles.
- [The Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hamilton-jacobi-bellman.html): The HJB equation is the dynamic-programming condition for optimal control, defining the value function whose gradient yields the optimal feedback law.
- [The Internal Model Principle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/internal-model-principle.html): To track or reject a signal with zero error, a feedback loop must contain a model of that signal's generating dynamics.
- [The Laplace Domain](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/laplace-transform.html): The Laplace transform converts differential equations into algebra by mapping time functions to functions of a complex frequency variable s.
- [The Nyquist Stability Criterion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/nyquist-stability-criterion.html): Closed-loop stability follows from counting how many times the open-loop Nyquist curve encircles the critical point minus one.
- [The Routh-Hurwitz Criterion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/routh-hurwitz.html): Routh-Hurwitz decides stability from the characteristic polynomial's coefficients alone, without computing any roots.
- [The Separation Principle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/separation-principle.html): For linear systems, the optimal controller and optimal estimator can be designed independently and combined without loss of optimality.
- [The Small-Gain Theorem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/small-gain-theorem.html): The small-gain theorem guarantees closed-loop stability when the product of the gains of two interconnected systems is less than one.
- [The State Transition Matrix](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/state-transition-matrix.html): The matrix exponential propagates a linear system's state forward in time and forms the core of its solution.
- [The Structured Singular Value](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/structured-singular-value.html): The structured singular value mu measures exactly how much structured uncertainty a system can tolerate before losing stability.
- [The Z-Transform](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/z-transform.html): The z-transform maps discrete-time sequences to functions of a complex variable, turning difference equations into algebra.
- [Time-Delay Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/time-delay-systems.html): Pure time delays add frequency-dependent phase lag that limits achievable bandwidth and can destabilize otherwise sound loops.
- [Transfer Functions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/transfer-functions.html): A transfer function is the Laplace-domain ratio of output to input for a linear time-invariant system, capturing its dynamics as a rational function.
- [Transient Response Specifications](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/transient-response-specs.html): Rise time, overshoot, and settling time quantify how a system responds to a step, translating design goals into measurable targets.
- [Tube Model Predictive Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tube-mpc.html): Tube MPC keeps the true state inside a bounded tube around a nominal trajectory by combining a nominal optimizer with an ancillary error-rejecting feedback.
- [Youla Parametrization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/youla-parametrization.html): The Youla parametrization describes every stabilizing controller for a plant with a single free stable transfer function, making closed-loop maps affine.
- [Ziegler-Nichols Tuning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ziegler-nichols.html): The Ziegler-Nichols rules give quick starting PID gains from a single closed-loop or open-loop experiment on the plant.
- [mu-Synthesis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mu-synthesis.html): mu-synthesis designs controllers that are robust against structured uncertainty by minimizing the structured singular value of the closed loop.

### AI Plasma Control
- [Actuator Commissioning and Characterization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-actuator-commissioning.html): Before an actuator can be trusted in a loop, its real response, limits, and quirks must be measured and modeled.
- [Actuator Management and Allocation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/actuator-management-allocation.html): Mapping many competing control demands onto a limited set of shared, constrained actuators without violating hardware limits.
- [Actuator Saturation Management](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-actuator-saturation-management.html): Every actuator has limits; managing saturation keeps a loop stable and honest when it runs out of authority.
- [Actuator Sharing and Allocation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-actuators-allocation.html): Many control goals compete for the same limited actuators; allocation decides who gets them, when, and how much.
- [Beta-Limit Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/beta-limit-control.html): Keeping the plasma pressure below the stability ceiling set by pressure-driven magnetohydrodynamic modes.
- [Between-Shot Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-between-shot-analysis.html): Between shots, automated analysis turns the last discharge into corrections for the next, tightening the loop over an operating day.
- [Breakdown and Start-Up Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-breakdown-startup-control.html): Breakdown is the moment the gas becomes a plasma; control must reliably initiate and grow the discharge from nothing.
- [Burn Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burn-control.html): Regulating fusion power in a burning plasma, where self-heating couples temperature and reaction rate in a potentially unstable loop.
- [Control Actuator Inventory](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-actuator-inventory.html): The hardware the control stack can command - coils, power supplies, heating, current drive, and fueling - and each one's character.
- [Control Allocation Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-allocation-methods.html): The mathematics of distributing control demands across redundant, constrained actuators - pseudo-inverses, weighting, and optimization.
- [Control Latency Budget](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-latency-budget.html): The latency budget accounts for every microsecond between a measurement and the resulting actuator response, and must fit inside the loop period.
- [Control Loop Fundamentals](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-loop-fundamentals.html): The feedback basics - error, gain, stability, and bandwidth - that underlie every plasma control loop.
- [Control Room Human Factors](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-control-room-human-factors.html): Human factors design shapes displays, alarms, and procedures so operators make good decisions under time pressure and complexity.
- [Control of a Tandem-Mirror Burner](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tandem-mirror-control.html): How control differs for an open-ended mirror machine, where confinement rests on end-plug fields and potentials rather than a closed current.
- [Control of the Tandem-Mirror Burner](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-burner-mirror-control.html): The burner generator is a tandem mirror, not a tokamak, so its control centers on plug fields, axial confinement, and direct conversion.
- [Control-Oriented Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-control-oriented-modeling.html): Control-oriented models capture just enough physics to predict the input-output response controllers need, fast enough to run in real time.
- [Control-Oriented Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-oriented-modeling.html): Building models simple and fast enough for control yet faithful to the dynamics that matter - a different craft from physics modeling.
- [Controllability and Observability in Plasma Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/controllability-observability.html): Two structural properties that decide whether a plasma quantity can be driven by the actuators and inferred from the sensors.
- [Current-Profile and q-Profile Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-current-profile-control.html): Controlling the current profile controls the safety-factor profile, which sets both stability and confinement in advanced scenarios.
- [Density Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-density-control.html): Density control regulates how many particles the plasma holds, using gas puffing and pellet injection against pumping and the density limit.
- [Detached Divertor Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-divertor-detachment.html): Divertor detachment spreads exhaust heat over volume by radiation and neutral collisions; control holds the detachment front in a safe location.
- [Diagnostic-to-Control Data Pipeline](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-diagnostic-pipeline.html): The data pipeline moves diagnostic signals to the controllers with bounded, predictable latency, the nervous system of real-time control.
- [Digital Twins, in General](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/digital-twin-general.html): The general concept of a live, validated simulation paired with a physical system, and what makes one trustworthy.
- [Digital-Twin-Assisted Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-digital-twin-control.html): A digital twin runs a live model of the machine alongside the real one, supporting estimation, prediction, and validation of control actions.
- [Disruption Avoidance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-disruption-avoidance.html): Avoidance keeps the plasma away from the boundaries where disruptions occur, always preferred over cleaning up after one.
- [Disruption Avoidance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/disruption-avoidance.html): Acting on early warning to steer the plasma away from a disruption while keeping the discharge alive.
- [Disruption Mitigation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-disruption-mitigation.html): When a disruption cannot be avoided, mitigation spreads the energy release and suppresses runaway electrons to protect the machine.
- [Disruption Mitigation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/disruption-mitigation.html): When a disruption is unavoidable, spreading the released energy safely and suppressing runaway electrons to protect the machine.
- [Disruption Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-disruption-prediction.html): Prediction gives the control system advance warning of an approaching disruption so it can avoid or mitigate in time.
- [Disruption Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/disruption-prediction.html): Estimating in real time whether a plasma is approaching a sudden loss of confinement, early enough for the stack to act.
- [Divertor Detachment Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/divertor-detachment-control.html): Regulating the plasma edge so the heat reaching the divertor is radiated away before it can damage the target.
- [ELM Control and Pacing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-elm-control.html): Edge-localized modes are periodic edge bursts; control aims to make them small and frequent rather than large and rare.
- [Error Field Correction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-error-field-correction.html): Tiny asymmetries in the magnetic field can lock modes and disrupt the plasma; correction coils cancel them under feedback.
- [Error-Field Correction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/error-field-correction.html): Detecting and cancelling small, unintended non-axisymmetric magnetic fields that can lock modes and trigger disruptions.
- [Exception Handling and Graceful Degradation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-watchdog-graceful-degradation.html): A robust control system degrades gracefully, falling back to simpler safe behavior when a sensor, actuator, or computation fails.
- [Exception Handling in Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/exception-handling-control.html): How the stack detects off-normal conditions and branches to pre-validated recovery or termination rather than improvising in a crisis.
- [Feedforward and Feedback Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-feedforward-feedback.html): Feedforward applies the planned command in advance; feedback corrects the difference between plan and reality. Good control uses both.
- [Flat-Top Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/flattop-control.html): Holding steady plasma conditions during the useful phase of a discharge, regulating current, shape, density, and profiles against drift.
- [Fueling and Pellet Injection Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-fueling-injection-control.html): Fueling control times and places fuel delivery, using gas and pellets to build and hold density where the plasma needs it.
- [Grad-Shafranov Equation for Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/grad-shafranov-for-control.html): The force-balance equation that underlies equilibrium reconstruction, and why its structure shapes real-time control.
- [Heating Power Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-heating-power-control.html): Heating power control modulates auxiliary systems to regulate temperature, stored energy, and profiles while respecting source limits.
- [Human Oversight and the Control Room](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-control-room-human-oversight.html): Automation runs the fast loops, but humans set intent, supervise, and hold authority to intervene from the control room.
- [Impurity and Radiation Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-impurity-control.html): Impurity control balances the radiation that protects walls against the core dilution and radiative collapse that too many impurities cause.
- [Integrated Commissioning of the Control System](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-integrated-commissioning.html): Commissioning brings the control system online in careful stages, proving each layer before the next depends on it.
- [Interferometry for Density Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/interferometry-for-control.html): How laser interferometry provides the fast, reliable density measurement that closes the density-control loop.
- [Isoflux versus Rigid Shape Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/isoflux-vs-rigid-control.html): Two ways to frame the shape-control problem: matching flux at boundary points, or moving a rigid outline.
- [Kalman Filtering for Plasma State](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/kalman-filtering-plasma-state.html): Fusing noisy diagnostics over time into a best estimate of the plasma state with quantified uncertainty.
- [Kinetic and Profile Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-kinetic-profile-control.html): Kinetic control shapes the radial profiles of temperature, density, and rotation rather than just their scalar averages.
- [Latency and Jitter in Control Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-latency-jitter.html): Why bounded, predictable timing matters as much as raw speed in a real-time plasma control system.
- [Layer 1: Deterministic Hardware Reflexes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/layer-deterministic-reflexes.html): The fastest control layer: microsecond trip lines and interlocks implemented in fixed logic that protect the machine without waiting on any software decision.
- [Layer 2: Fast Feedback Loops](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/layer-fast-feedback.html): Sub-millisecond feedback that stabilizes the fastest-growing plasma instabilities, chiefly vertical position and resistive-wall modes.
- [Layer 4: Real-Time State Estimation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/layer-realtime-state-estimation.html): The layer that fuses raw diagnostics into a coherent, physically consistent estimate of the plasma state for every controller above it.
- [Layer 6: Scenario and Trajectory Supervision](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/layer-scenario-supervision.html): The layer that schedules references through a discharge - ramp-up, flat-top, ramp-down - and adapts the plan as conditions evolve.
- [Layer 7: The Predictive Digital Twin](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/layer-predictive-digital-twin.html): A forward-running simulation of the plasma that forecasts where the current trajectory leads, so the stack can act before limits are reached.
- [Layer 8: Human Oversight](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/layer-human-oversight.html): The slowest and highest layer: human operators who set intent, approve exceptions, and make the judgments no automated layer should make alone.
- [Locked-Mode Detection and Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-locked-mode-control.html): A locked mode is a non-rotating magnetic island that often precedes a disruption; detecting and unlocking it is a priority for the off-normal layer.
- [Loop Tuning and Gain Scheduling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-loop-tuning-gain-scheduling.html): Tuning sets a loop's responsiveness; gain scheduling changes the tuning as the plasma moves through very different operating conditions.
- [Machine Protection Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-machine-protection.html): The machine protection system is the last line of defense, acting to protect hardware even when it means abandoning the plasma.
- [Magnetic Diagnostics for Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/magnetic-diagnostics-control.html): Flux loops, pickup coils, and saddle sensors - the fast, robust magnetic measurements that anchor real-time control.
- [Model Predictive Control for Plasmas](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-model-predictive-control.html): Model predictive control optimizes actuator commands over a short future horizon each cycle, handling constraints and coupling directly.
- [Model Predictive Control for Plasmas](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-predictive-control-plasma.html): Optimizing actuator commands over a receding horizon while explicitly honoring the plasma's and hardware's hard limits.
- [Neoclassical Tearing Mode Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-ntm-control.html): Neoclassical tearing modes form magnetic islands that degrade confinement; control locates and shrinks them with targeted current drive.
- [Neural Networks in Real-Time Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neural-network-realtime-control.html): Using trained networks as fast surrogates, estimators, or controllers inside the real-time loop - with the verification burden that implies.
- [Off-Normal Event Detection and Response](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-off-normal-detection.html): Off-normal detection watches for the early signs of a failing discharge and switches from performance to recovery or safe termination.
- [PID and Modern Control in Fusion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pid-vs-modern-control.html): When simple proportional-integral-derivative loops suffice and when model-based multivariable control is needed.
- [Plasma Control System Architecture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-architecture-overview.html): A plasma control system links diagnostics, real-time computation, and actuators into feedback loops that hold a discharge on its intended trajectory.
- [Plasma Control System Architecture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-control-system-architecture.html): The hardware and software organization that lets many control functions run at different rates while sharing sensors and actuators.
- [Plasma Control: An Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-control-overview.html): Why a burning plasma must be actively steered every millisecond, and how a layered control system keeps it inside a narrow operating window.
- [Plasma Current Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-plasma-current-control.html): Plasma current control regulates the total toroidal current, the quantity that anchors confinement, stability, and the safety factor.
- [Plasma Current Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-current-control.html): Regulating the toroidal plasma current with the central solenoid and, in steady state, with non-inductive current drive.
- [Plasma Density Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/density-control.html): Regulating the plasma density with gas puffing and pellet injection while respecting confinement, fueling efficiency, and stability limits.
- [Plasma Response Models for Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-response-models.html): Reduced linear models of how the plasma reacts to coil and actuator changes - the basis for designing magnetic control loops.
- [Plasma Shape Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-shape-control.html): Holding the plasma boundary to a target shape by regulating the currents in the poloidal field coils that surround it.
- [Plasma State Estimation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-plasma-state-estimation.html): State estimation fuses many noisy diagnostics into a single best estimate of the plasma state for controllers to act on.
- [Radiated Power Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/radiated-power-control.html): Managing how much of the plasma's power is radiated - useful for protecting the wall, dangerous if it runs away.
- [Radiated-Power Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-radiated-power-control.html): Radiated-power control regulates how much and where the plasma radiates, protecting surfaces without collapsing the core.
- [Ramp-Down Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-rampdown-control.html): Ramp-down safely unwinds a discharge from flat-top to termination, avoiding the disruptions that a careless shutdown can trigger.
- [Ramp-Down Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rampdown-control.html): Bringing current and stored energy down on a controlled path - a phase as disruption-prone as ramp-up if handled carelessly.
- [Ramp-Up Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-rampup-control.html): Ramp-up brings a discharge from breakdown to the flat-top current while keeping the plasma stable and the current profile well behaved.
- [Ramp-Up Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rampup-control.html): The early, fragile phase where current and shape are established while avoiding the instabilities that thrive at low current and density.
- [Real-Time Computing for Plasma Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-real-time-computing.html): Plasma control depends on hard real-time computing, where meeting a deadline every cycle matters more than raw average throughput.
- [Real-Time Diagnostics for Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/realtime-diagnostics-for-control.html): The subset of plasma diagnostics fast and reliable enough to close control loops, and what each contributes.
- [Real-Time Equilibrium Reconstruction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-realtime-equilibrium.html): Equilibrium reconstruction infers the plasma shape, position, and internal fields from magnetic and other measurements, fast enough for control.
- [Real-Time Equilibrium Reconstruction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/realtime-equilibrium-reconstruction.html): Fitting the plasma's magnetic equilibrium every few milliseconds so that shape, position, and profile controllers act on a consistent picture.
- [Real-Time Plasma Flight Simulators](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-flight-simulator.html): A plasma flight simulator runs a fast physics model in place of the real machine so controllers can be tested and tuned before a discharge.
- [Reinforcement Learning for Plasma Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-rl-plasma-control.html): Reinforcement learning trains control policies against a simulator, offering a route to coordinate many actuators toward hard-to-specify goals.
- [Reinforcement Learning for Shape Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reinforcement-learning-shape-control.html): Training control policies in simulation to steer plasma shape and position, and the honest limits of the approach.
- [Resistive-Wall-Mode Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/resistive-wall-mode-control.html): Stabilizing slow, wall-limited magnetohydrodynamic modes with feedback coils to allow operation above the no-wall pressure limit.
- [Rotation and Momentum Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-rotation-momentum-control.html): Plasma rotation stabilizes some instabilities and shears turbulence; control adjusts it through momentum input and magnetic braking.
- [Runaway Electron Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-runaway-electron-control.html): Runaway electrons accelerated during a quench can damage the wall; control aims to prevent their formation or safely dissipate the beam.
- [Safe Shutdown Sequences](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/safe-shutdown-sequences.html): The controlled procedures that bring a plasma to rest with minimal stress on the machine, whether planned or triggered by fault.
- [Safety Factor and q-Profile Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/safety-factor-q-control.html): Controlling the winding of the magnetic field, which governs stability, through the current profile.
- [Safety Interlocks and Instrumented Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-safety-interlocks.html): Interlocks are simple, independent safety functions that act automatically when a hard limit is crossed, regardless of the control software.
- [Safety Interlocks and Machine Protection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-safety-interlocks.html): The independent protection system that guards the machine regardless of what the control system is trying to do.
- [Sawtooth Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-sawtooth-control.html): Sawteeth are periodic core relaxations; control tunes their period so they flush impurities without seeding larger instabilities.
- [Scenario and Trajectory Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/scenario-trajectory-control.html): Designing and executing the time-varying reference trajectories that carry a plasma safely from breakdown to controlled termination.
- [Scenario and Trajectory Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-scenario-optimization.html): Scenario optimization searches for an actuator trajectory that reaches a target plasma state while respecting every operational and stability limit.
- [Shape and Position Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-shape-position-control.html): Shape control holds the plasma boundary on its target outline and gaps, keeping it clear of walls and on the divertor strike points.
- [State Estimation for Plasma Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/state-estimation-plasma.html): The general problem of inferring the full plasma state from limited diagnostics, and the observers that solve it in real time.
- [Stored-Energy and Beta Feedback](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-beta-stored-energy.html): Beta and stored-energy feedback keeps plasma pressure near its performance target while staying below the limit where pressure-driven instabilities appear.
- [Supervisory Control and State Machines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-supervisory-control.html): The supervisor sequences discharge phases, enables and disables controllers, and holds the logic that ties fast loops into one discharge.
- [Tearing-Mode and NTM Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tearing-mode-control.html): Detecting and suppressing magnetic islands that degrade confinement and can lock into disruptions.
- [The 8-Layer Control Architecture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/eight-layer-control-architecture.html): A layered control stack that spans microsecond hardware reflexes to a predictive digital twin and human oversight, each layer with its own latency budget.
- [The Digital Twin for Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/digital-twin-for-control.html): A continuously validated simulation model that mirrors the plasma, used for prediction, testing, and operator situational awareness.
- [The Discharge Scenario Library](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-scenario-library.html): A scenario library stores proven pulse schedules and their outcomes so operators build on validated starting points rather than from scratch.
- [The Exception Matrix and Event Handling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-exception-matrix.html): An exception matrix maps detected off-normal conditions to defined responses, making fault handling explicit, reviewable, and testable.
- [The Gatekeeper Decision Layer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-gatekeeper-decision-layer.html): A gatekeeper continuously decides whether to keep pushing performance, hold, or abandon the discharge, arbitrating avoidance and mitigation.
- [The Greenwald Limit in Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/greenwald-limit-control.html): How the empirical density limit constrains real-time density control and why staying below it is a scenario design requirement.
- [The Kronos Layered Control Stack in Operation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-layered-kronos-stack.html): The Kronos control stack layers fast stabilization, feedback regulation, supervision, and protection into one coordinated system.
- [The Pulse Schedule and Waveform Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-pulse-schedule-waveforms.html): The pulse schedule is the time-programmed plan of references and actuator waveforms that defines a discharge before it begins.
- [Timing and Synchronization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-timing-synchronization.html): A shared, precise clock lets distributed control nodes act together and lets measurements be fused correctly across the system.
- [Verification and Validation of Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/verification-validation-control.html): Establishing that a control system does what it should before it is trusted with a machine - and keeping that trust over time.
- [Verification and Validation of Control Software](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-verification-validation.html): Control software must be shown correct before it commands a machine; verification checks the code, validation checks it against reality.
- [Vertical Position Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/vertical-position-control.html): Actively stabilizing the vertical position of an elongated plasma, which is intrinsically unstable and must be corrected faster than it grows.
- [Vertical Stability of Elongated Plasmas](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/vertical-stability-physics.html): The physics behind why shaped plasmas are vertically unstable and how conducting structures and feedback set the stability limit.
- [Vertical Stabilization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pcs-vertical-stabilization.html): Elongated plasmas are vertically unstable and drift toward the wall unless a fast feedback loop actively holds them in place.

### Surrogates & Uncertainty
- [Active Subspaces](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/active-subspaces.html): Active subspaces find the few input directions along which a function changes most, collapsing high-dimensional problems onto a low-dimensional ridge.
- [Adaptive Sampling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adaptive-sampling.html): Adaptive sampling adds training points sequentially where a surrogate is weakest, balancing exploration of unseen regions against refinement of complex ones.
- [Adaptive Sampling and Active Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adaptive-sampling-active-learning.html): Active learning chooses the next expensive evaluation where it most improves the surrogate, building accurate models from few runs.
- [Adjoint-Based UQ](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adjoint-based-uq.html): Adjoint methods compute the sensitivity of an output to all inputs at a cost independent of the number of inputs, powering efficient local UQ.
- [Aleatoric versus Epistemic Uncertainty](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/aleatoric-vs-epistemic-uncertainty.html): Aleatoric uncertainty is inherent randomness you cannot reduce; epistemic uncertainty is ignorance you can reduce with more data or better models.
- [Autoregressive Co-Kriging](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/co-kriging-autoregressive.html): Autoregressive co-kriging couples Gaussian processes across fidelity levels so a few accurate runs correct many cheap ones.
- [Bayesian Model Calibration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bayesian-model-calibration.html): Bayesian calibration infers uncertain model parameters from data, yielding posterior distributions rather than single best-fit values.
- [Bayesian Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bayesian-neural-networks.html): Bayesian neural networks place distributions over weights, turning point predictions into predictive distributions with quantified uncertainty.
- [Calibration of Predictive Uncertainty](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/calibration-of-predictive-uncertainty.html): A model is calibrated when its stated probabilities match observed frequencies; miscalibration makes uncertainty estimates untrustworthy.
- [Calibration of Probabilistic Predictions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/calibration-of-probabilistic-predictions.html): A well-calibrated model's stated probabilities match observed frequencies, so a ninety percent interval really contains the truth ninety percent of the time.
- [Choosing a Surrogate Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/surrogate-model-selection.html): The right surrogate depends on dimensionality, data budget, smoothness, output type, and whether you need calibrated uncertainty.
- [Co-Kriging](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/co-kriging.html): Co-kriging fuses a primary variable with correlated secondary data or a lower-fidelity model to sharpen predictions and their uncertainty.
- [Conformal Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/conformal-prediction.html): Conformal prediction wraps any model to produce prediction sets with guaranteed coverage, assuming only that data are exchangeable.
- [Control Variates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-variates.html): Control variates reduce Monte Carlo variance by subtracting a correlated quantity whose expectation is known and adding it back.
- [Cross-Entropy Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cross-entropy-method.html): The cross-entropy method adaptively learns a good importance-sampling distribution for rare events by iteratively fitting to the best samples.
- [Cross-Validation for Surrogates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cross-validation-surrogates.html): Cross-validation reuses scarce data by rotating holdout folds, estimating a surrogate's out-of-sample error without new expensive runs.
- [Deep Ensembles](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/deep-ensembles.html): Training several neural networks from different random initializations and combining their predictions gives a simple, strong estimate of model uncertainty.
- [Deep-Learning Surrogates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/deep-learning-surrogates.html): Neural networks learn complex, high-dimensional input-output maps from simulation data, serving as fast surrogates where classical methods struggle.
- [Derivative-Based Sensitivity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/derivative-based-sensitivity-dgsm.html): Derivative-based global sensitivity measures average squared gradients over the input distribution, cheaply bounding Sobol total effects.
- [Dimension Reduction for UQ](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dimension-reduction-for-uq.html): High-dimensional uncertainty problems become tractable only after reducing inputs or outputs to the directions that actually matter.
- [Dimensionality Reduction for Surrogates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/dimensionality-reduction-for-surrogates.html): Reducing inputs or outputs to their essential few directions makes high-dimensional surrogate modeling tractable and more accurate.
- [Emulator Error Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/emulator-error-control.html): A surrogate is only useful if its own error is bounded and propagated; emulator error control keeps the approximation honest.
- [Epistemic vs Aleatoric Uncertainty](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/epistemic-vs-aleatoric-uncertainty.html): Aleatoric uncertainty is irreducible randomness in the system; epistemic uncertainty is reducible ignorance about the model, and the two demand different responses.
- [Error Bars on Predictions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/error-bars-on-predictions.html): A prediction without an error bar hides how much to trust it; sound surrogates report calibrated uncertainty alongside every value.
- [First-Order Reliability Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/first-order-reliability-method.html): FORM estimates a failure probability by finding the most probable failure point and linearizing the limit state there.
- [Forward Uncertainty Propagation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/forward-uncertainty-propagation.html): Forward UQ pushes known input distributions through a model to compute the resulting distribution, moments, and failure probabilities of the output.
- [Gaussian-Process Kernels](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gaussian-process-kernels.html): The kernel encodes every assumption a Gaussian process makes about smoothness, scale, and structure, and choosing it well is the modeling task.
- [Global vs Local Sensitivity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/global-vs-local-sensitivity.html): Local sensitivity measures response to small perturbations at one point; global sensitivity apportions output variance across the whole input range.
- [Gradient-Enhanced Kriging](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gradient-enhanced-kriging.html): When gradients are available, gradient-enhanced kriging uses them as extra training data to build accurate surrogates from fewer function evaluations.
- [Heteroscedastic Noise Surrogates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/heteroscedastic-noise-surrogates.html): When observation noise varies across input space, the surrogate must model an input-dependent noise level rather than a single constant.
- [Hierarchical Bayesian Calibration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hierarchical-bayesian-calibration.html): Hierarchical models calibrate across multiple experiments or units by sharing information through population-level priors.
- [Importance Sampling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/importance-sampling.html): Importance sampling estimates expectations by drawing from a cleverly chosen distribution and reweighting, cutting variance for rare-event and tail problems.
