- [The Energy Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/energy-equation-fluid.html): The evolution of internal energy or pressure for a plasma fluid, closing the fluid hierarchy with heat flux and sources.
- [The Fokker-Planck Collision Operator](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fokker-planck-collision-operator.html): The velocity-space diffusion and drag operator describing cumulative small-angle Coulomb collisions.
- [The Fokker-Planck Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fokker-planck-equation.html): The kinetic equation that adds small-angle Coulomb collisions as a drift-and-diffusion operator in velocity space.
- [The Frozen-In Flux Theorem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/frozen-in-flux-theorem.html): Alfven's theorem: in a perfectly conducting fluid, magnetic field lines move with the plasma.
- [The Fusion Cross Section](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cross-section-fusion.html): The energy-dependent probability that two colliding nuclei fuse, the microscopic input to all reaction rates.
- [The Fusion Triple Product](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/triple-product.html): The single figure of merit n T tau_E that compresses the ignition requirement into one number.
- [The Gamow Peak and Quantum Tunneling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gamow-peak-tunneling.html): The narrow energy window where the odds of tunneling the Coulomb barrier and finding a fast particle combine.
- [The Generalized Ohm's Law](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ohms-law-generalized.html): The electron momentum balance that connects electric field, current, and the two-fluid and Hall terms.
- [The Grad-Shafranov Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/grad-shafranov-equation.html): The nonlinear elliptic PDE that sets the equilibrium of an axisymmetric magnetically confined plasma.
- [The Grad-Shafranov Solver](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/grad-shafranov-solver.html): How the axisymmetric equilibrium equation is discretized and solved to find nested flux surfaces.
- [The Greenwald Density Limit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/greenwald-density-limit.html): An empirical ceiling on the line-averaged density set by the plasma current and minor radius.
- [The Gyrokinetic Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gyrokinetic-equation.html): A reduced kinetic equation that averages over fast gyromotion to make turbulence simulation tractable.
- [The Heat Conduction Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/heat-conduction-equation.html): The energy-transport counterpart of diffusion, governing how temperature relaxes through conductive heat flux.
- [The Ideal MHD Equations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ideal-mhd-equations.html): The single-fluid model of a perfectly conducting magnetized plasma: mass, momentum, energy, and induction.
- [The Ion-Temperature-Gradient Mode](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ion-temperature-gradient-mode.html): A drift-type microinstability driven by steep ion temperature gradients, a leading cause of core heat loss.
- [The Kruskal-Shafranov Limit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/kruskal-shafranov-limit.html): The current-driven external kink threshold requiring the edge safety factor to exceed unity.
- [The Lawson Criterion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lawson-criterion.html): The condition on density and confinement time under which fusion self-heating balances plasma energy losses.
- [The Lorentz Force and Equation of Motion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lorentz-force-equation.html): The force law that governs every charged particle and, aggregated, all plasma behavior.
- [The Lundquist Number](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lundquist-number.html): The ratio of resistive diffusion time to Alfven transit time, controlling the rate of magnetic reconnection.
- [The MHD Energy Principle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mhd-energy-principle.html): A variational test for ideal stability: an equilibrium is stable if every allowed displacement raises the potential energy.
- [The MHD Energy Principle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/energy-principle-mhd.html): A variational test for ideal stability: if any displacement lowers the potential energy, the plasma is unstable.
- [The Magnetic Diffusion Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/magnetic-diffusion-equation.html): The induction equation in the static-fluid limit, describing how magnetic field decays and penetrates by resistivity.
- [The Magnetic Moment Adiabatic Invariant](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/magnetic-moment-adiabatic-invariant.html): The conserved ratio of perpendicular energy to field strength that governs magnetic mirroring.
- [The Magnetic Reynolds Number](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/magnetic-reynolds-number.html): The dimensionless ratio of magnetic advection to magnetic diffusion in a conducting flow.
- [The Maxwell-Boltzmann Distribution](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/maxwell-boltzmann-distribution.html): The equilibrium velocity distribution of a plasma species, from which reactivities and rates are computed.
- [The Mercier Criterion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mercier-criterion.html): The local stability condition against pressure-driven interchange modes on a single flux surface.
- [The Momentum Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/momentum-equation-fluid.html): Newton's second law for a plasma fluid element, balancing inertia against pressure and electromagnetic forces.
- [The Newcomb Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/newcomb-equation.html): The marginal ideal-MHD equation governing the perturbed flux outside a resistive layer.
- [The Pfirsch-Schluter Current](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pfirsch-schluter-current.html): The parallel return current that keeps a toroidal equilibrium divergence-free despite the outboard-inboard field asymmetry.
- [The Plasma Beta Parameter](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-beta-parameter.html): The ratio of plasma pressure to magnetic pressure, the primary measure of magnetic confinement efficiency.
- [The Plasma Dielectric Tensor](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-dielectric-tensor.html): The frequency-dependent response tensor that encodes how a magnetized plasma polarizes and conducts under an oscillating field.
- [The Plasma Frequency](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-frequency.html): The natural oscillation frequency of electrons displaced from equilibrium, setting the plasma's electromagnetic response.
- [The Radial Electric Field and Flow Shear](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/radial-electric-field-shear.html): How a sheared radial electric field suppresses turbulence and enables transport barriers.
- [The Resistive MHD Equations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/resistive-mhd-equations.html): Ideal MHD plus finite resistivity, admitting magnetic diffusion, reconnection, and tearing instabilities.
- [The Resistive-Wall Mode](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/resistive-wall-mode.html): A slow external kink that grows on the wall's resistive timescale in the gap between the no-wall and ideal-wall limits.
- [The Rutherford Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rutherford-equation.html): The nonlinear equation governing the growth and saturation of magnetic islands from tearing modes.
- [The Safety Factor Formula](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/safety-factor-formula.html): The number of toroidal transits a field line makes per poloidal transit, the master parameter of tokamak stability.
- [The Safety Factor q](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/safety-factor-q.html): The number of toroidal transits a field line makes per poloidal transit, central to tokamak stability.
- [The Saha Ionization Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/saha-equation.html): The thermodynamic relation giving the ionization balance of a gas in local thermal equilibrium.
- [The Sauter Bootstrap Formula](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sauter-bootstrap-formula.html): A widely used analytic fit for the neoclassical bootstrap current valid across collisionality regimes.
- [The Shafranov Shift](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/shafranov-shift.html): The outward displacement of inner flux surfaces relative to the plasma boundary, driven by pressure and internal current.
- [The Suydam Criterion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/suydam-criterion.html): The cylindrical local stability condition against pressure-driven interchange in a screw pinch.
- [The Tearing-Mode Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tearing-mode-equation.html): The resistive-MHD instability that reconnects field lines at rational surfaces, forming magnetic islands.
- [The Tritium Breeding Ratio](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tritium-breeding-ratio-equation.html): The ratio of tritium produced in the blanket to tritium consumed in the plasma, which must exceed one for D-T self-sufficiency.
- [The Troyon Beta Limit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/troyon-beta-limit.html): The empirical and theoretical ceiling on normalized plasma pressure set by ideal-MHD stability.
- [The Troyon Beta Limit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/troyon-limit.html): The empirical maximum on normalized beta set by ideal MHD kink and ballooning stability.
- [The Two-Fluid Plasma Equations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/two-fluid-plasma-equations.html): Separate momentum and continuity equations for electrons and ions, coupled through electromagnetic fields and collisions.
- [The Vlasov Equation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/vlasov-equation.html): The collisionless kinetic equation that evolves a particle distribution function in six-dimensional phase space.
- [The Vlasov-Poisson System](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/vlasov-poisson-system.html): The kinetic description of a collisionless plasma: a phase-space transport equation coupled to its self-consistent electric field.

### Optimization
- [Acquisition Functions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/acquisition-functions.html): The decision rule of Bayesian optimization: score candidate points by expected usefulness to balance exploration and exploitation.
- [AdaGrad](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adagrad.html): Adapt a per-parameter learning rate by dividing by the accumulated history of squared gradients, favoring rarely updated directions.
- [Adadelta](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-adadelta.html): Adadelta extends Adagrad with a decaying gradient average and a matching decaying average of updates, removing the need to choose a global learning rate.
- [Adagrad](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-adagrad.html): Adagrad gives each parameter its own learning rate, shrinking it in proportion to the accumulated size of that parameter's past gradients.
- [Adam](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adam-optimizer.html): Combine momentum and per-parameter adaptive scaling with bias correction: the default optimizer for training deep neural networks.
- [AdamW](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adamw.html): Adam with decoupled weight decay: apply regularization directly to the parameters instead of folding it into the adaptive gradient.
- [Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-admm.html): ADMM splits a large problem into smaller pieces coupled by a linear constraint, then coordinates their solutions through a dual variable.
- [Augmented Lagrangian](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/augmented-lagrangian-method.html): Combine a quadratic penalty with explicit multiplier estimates to reach feasibility without driving the penalty weight to infinity.
- [BFGS](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bfgs-algorithm.html): The Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno update maintains a positive-definite inverse-Hessian approximation for fast, robust unconstrained optimization.
- [Bandit Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-bandit-optimization.html): Bandit optimization chooses actions to minimize loss when only the chosen action's outcome is observed, forcing a trade-off between exploration and exploitation.
- [Barrier Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/barrier-methods.html): Keep iterates strictly inside the feasible region by adding a barrier that grows to infinity at the boundary of inequality constraints.
- [Block Coordinate Descent](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-block-coordinate-descent.html): Block coordinate descent updates a group of correlated variables jointly at each step, restoring efficiency when single-coordinate updates stall.
- [Branch and Bound](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-branch-and-bound.html): Branch and bound solves hard discrete problems by recursively splitting the search space and pruning branches that cannot beat the best solution found.
- [Branch and Cut](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-branch-and-cut.html): Branch and cut combines branch-and-bound search with cutting planes that tighten the relaxation at each node, the core of modern MIP solvers.
- [CMA-ES](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-cma-es.html): The covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy samples candidates from a Gaussian and reshapes that Gaussian toward better regions, needing no gradients.
- [Condition Number and Convergence](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/condition-number-and-convergence.html): The ratio of largest to smallest curvature controls how fast first-order methods converge and why ill-conditioned problems crawl.
- [Condition Number in Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-condition-number-optimization.html): The condition number, the ratio of largest to smallest curvature, predicts how slowly gradient methods converge and why preconditioning helps.
- [Constrained Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/constrained-optimization-overview.html): Minimize an objective while respecting equality and inequality constraints, the setting for most real engineering design.
- [Convex Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/convex-optimization.html): When the objective and feasible set are convex, every local minimum is global and efficient solvers guarantee the optimum.
- [Convex Sets and Functions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/convex-sets-and-functions.html): The geometric and analytic building blocks of convex optimization: sets closed under line segments and functions that curve upward.
- [Coordinate Descent](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-coordinate-descent.html): Coordinate descent optimizes one variable at a time, holding the rest fixed, and cycles or samples through the coordinates until convergence.
- [Coordinate Descent](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/coordinate-descent.html): Optimize one variable at a time while holding the rest fixed, effective when single-coordinate updates are cheap and closed-form.
- [Cutting-Plane Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-cutting-plane-methods.html): Cutting-plane methods build an outer polyhedral approximation of a convex problem, adding one linear inequality at a time to trim the search region.
- [Derivative-Free Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-derivative-free-optimization.html): Derivative-free optimization minimizes functions using only their values, essential when gradients are unavailable, unreliable, noisy, or expensive.
- [Differential Evolution](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/differential-evolution.html): A population-based method that mutates candidates using scaled differences between other population members, effective for continuous global search.
- [Distributionally Robust Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-distributionally-robust-optimization.html): Distributionally robust optimization hedges against uncertainty in the probability distribution itself, optimizing the worst case over a set of plausible distributions.
- [Evolutionary Strategies](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/evolutionary-strategies.html): Evolve continuous solutions by sampling from a distribution and adapting its mean and covariance toward better regions.
- [Gaussian Process Surrogates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gaussian-process-surrogates.html): A nonparametric model that predicts a function and its uncertainty at every point, the standard surrogate for Bayesian optimization.
- [Genetic Algorithms](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/genetic-algorithms.html): Evolve a population of candidate solutions through selection, crossover, and mutation, guided by a fitness function.
- [Global Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/global-optimization-overview.html): Seek the best solution over an entire landscape of many local minima, where gradient methods alone are not enough.
- [Gradient Descent](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gradient-descent.html): The workhorse of continuous optimization: step downhill along the negative gradient to minimize a differentiable objective.
- [Gradient-Free Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gradient-free-optimization.html): Optimize when gradients are unavailable, unreliable, or expensive, using only objective values to guide the search.
- [Integer Programming](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-integer-programming.html): Integer programming optimizes a linear objective over linear constraints where some or all variables must take whole-number values.
- [Interior-Point Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/interior-point-methods.html): Solve linear and convex programs by following a smooth central path through the interior of the feasible region.
- [KKT Conditions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/kkt-conditions.html): The Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions generalize Lagrange multipliers to inequality constraints, characterizing constrained optima.
- [Kelley's Cutting-Plane Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-kelley-cutting-plane.html): Kelley's method minimizes a convex function by building a lower model from its supporting linear pieces and minimizing that model each round.
- [L-BFGS](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lbfgs-algorithm.html): Limited-memory BFGS stores only a handful of recent vectors, scaling quasi-Newton optimization to millions of variables.
- [LP Duality](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/duality-in-linear-programming.html): Every linear program has a dual whose optimum equals the primal optimum, providing bounds, certificates, and shadow prices.
- [LP Relaxation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-lp-relaxation.html): The LP relaxation drops integrality from an integer program, yielding a tractable linear program whose optimum bounds the true integer optimum.
- [Lagrange Multipliers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lagrange-multipliers.html): Convert an equality-constrained optimization into stationarity of a single Lagrangian, with multipliers measuring constraint sensitivity.
- [Lagrangian Duality](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lagrangian-duality.html): Fold constraints into the objective with multipliers, minimize over the primal variables, and obtain a dual problem of lower bounds.
- [Latin Hypercube Sampling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/latin-hypercube-sampling.html): A stratified sampling scheme that spreads points evenly across every input dimension, ideal for computer experiments.
- [Learning-Rate-Free Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-learning-rate-free-methods.html): Learning-rate-free methods aim to match a well-tuned step size automatically, removing the most fragile hyperparameter of gradient-based optimization.
- [Line Search](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-line-search.html): Line search chooses how far to move along a descent direction each iteration, turning a direction into a concrete, safely sized step.
- [Line Search Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/line-search-methods.html): Given a descent direction, choose a step length that sufficiently decreases the objective, guaranteeing global convergence.
- [Linear Programming](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/linear-programming.html): Optimize a linear objective subject to linear equality and inequality constraints: the most widely used class of optimization.
- [Loss Landscape Geometry](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-loss-landscape-geometry.html): The geometry of a model's loss surface, its valleys, barriers, and flatness, shapes how training proceeds and how well the result generalizes.
- [Mini-Batch Gradient Descent](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mini-batch-gradient-descent.html): The middle ground between full-batch and single-sample updates: average gradients over a small batch for stable, hardware-friendly steps.
- [Mirror Descent](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-mirror-descent.html): Mirror descent generalizes gradient descent by measuring distance with a problem-adapted geometry instead of the Euclidean norm.
- [Mixed-Integer Programming](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-mixed-integer-programming.html): Mixed-integer programming combines continuous and integer variables, letting a single model capture both discrete decisions and continuous quantities.
- [Momentum](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/momentum-optimization.html): Accumulate a velocity vector from past gradients to accelerate along consistent directions and damp oscillations across valleys.
- [Multi-Objective Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multi-objective-optimization.html): Optimize several conflicting objectives at once, seeking the set of trade-off solutions rather than a single best point.
- [NSGA-II](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/nsga-ii.html): A fast elitist genetic algorithm that finds a diverse approximation of the whole Pareto front in a single run.
- [Natural Gradient](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-natural-gradient.html): The natural gradient rescales the ordinary gradient by the Fisher information matrix, following the steepest descent direction in distribution space.
- [Nesterov Accelerated Gradient](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/nesterov-accelerated-gradient.html): A momentum variant that evaluates the gradient at a look-ahead point, achieving the optimal first-order convergence rate for smooth convex problems.
- [Newton's Method for Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/newtons-method-optimization.html): Use the Hessian to model local curvature and jump to the minimum of a quadratic approximation, achieving quadratic convergence near the optimum.
- [Nonconvex Optimization Landscapes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-nonconvex-landscapes.html): Nonconvex objectives have multiple minima, saddles, and plateaus, so no method guarantees a global optimum, yet local methods often work well in practice.
- [Online Convex Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-online-convex-optimization.html): Online convex optimization makes a sequence of decisions against an adversary revealing convex losses one at a time, judged by regret against the best fixed choice.
- [Pareto Fronts](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pareto-fronts.html): The frontier of non-dominated solutions in objective space, showing the best achievable trade-offs among competing goals.
- [Particle Swarm Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/particle-swarm-optimization.html): A swarm of candidate solutions moves through the search space, each pulled toward its own best and the swarm's best position.
- [Penalty Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/penalty-methods.html): Convert constraints into a penalty term added to the objective, then solve a sequence of unconstrained problems with growing penalty.
- [Powell's Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-powells-method.html): Powell's method minimizes a function by successive line searches along a set of directions that it updates to become mutually conjugate, without derivatives.
- [Projected Gradient Descent](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/projected-gradient-descent.html): Take a gradient step, then project back onto the feasible set, a simple and effective method for constrained problems with easy projections.
- [Proximal Gradient Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-proximal-gradient.html): Proximal gradient descent minimizes a smooth term plus a nonsmooth term by taking a gradient step, then a proximal step.
- [Proximal Gradient Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/proximal-gradient-methods.html): Split a smooth loss from a nonsmooth regularizer: gradient-step the smooth part, then apply the proximal operator of the rest.
- [Quadratic Programming](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quadratic-programming.html): Minimize a quadratic objective subject to linear constraints: convex when the quadratic term is positive semidefinite.
- [Quasi-Newton Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quasi-newton-methods.html): Approximate the Hessian from successive gradients, capturing curvature without ever computing second derivatives.
- [RMSProp](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rmsprop.html): Fix AdaGrad's vanishing step size by scaling gradients with an exponentially decaying average of their recent magnitudes.
- [RMSprop for Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-rmsprop.html): RMSprop adapts per-parameter learning rates using an exponentially decaying average of squared gradients, curing Adagrad's vanishing step size.
- [Regret Minimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-regret-minimization.html): Regret measures how much worse a sequence of decisions did than the best fixed choice in hindsight; minimizing it is the goal of online learning.
- [Response Surface Methodology](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/response-surface-methodology.html): Fit simple polynomial models to experimental data, then optimize on the fitted surface to find good operating conditions.
- [Robust Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-robust-optimization.html): Robust optimization guards against uncertain data by optimizing for the worst case within a defined uncertainty set, requiring no probability distribution.
- [SDP Relaxation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-sdp-relaxation.html): SDP relaxation replaces a hard nonconvex problem with a tractable semidefinite program by lifting variables into a matrix and dropping a rank constraint.
- [Saddle Points](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-saddle-points.html): Saddle points are critical points that are minima in some directions and maxima in others; they dominate high-dimensional nonconvex landscapes.
- [Saddle Points and Nonconvexity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/saddle-points-and-nonconvexity.html): In high-dimensional nonconvex problems, saddle points, not local minima, are the main obstacle to gradient-based training.
- [Sample Average Approximation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-sample-average-approximation.html): Sample average approximation replaces an intractable expectation with an average over sampled scenarios, converting a stochastic program into a solvable one.
- [Scalarization Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/scalarization-methods.html): Reduce a multi-objective problem to a single objective by combining goals, then vary the combination to trace the Pareto front.
- [Second-Order Cone Programming](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-second-order-cone-programming.html): Second-order cone programming optimizes a linear objective subject to constraints that a norm is bounded by an affine function, generalizing quadratic programs.
- [Semidefinite Programming](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-semidefinite-programming.html): Semidefinite programming optimizes a linear objective over symmetric matrices constrained to be positive semidefinite, generalizing linear programming.
- [Simplex Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/simplex-method.html): Solve linear programs by walking from vertex to adjacent vertex of the feasible polyhedron, improving the objective at each pivot.
- [Simulated Annealing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/simulated-annealing.html): Borrow the physics of slow cooling: accept worse solutions with a temperature-dependent probability to escape local minima.
- [Stochastic Approximation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/stochastic-approximation.html): Find the root or minimizer of a function observed only through noisy measurements, the theoretical basis of stochastic gradient methods.
- [Stochastic Gradient Descent](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/stochastic-gradient-descent.html): Estimate the gradient from a random sample of the data each step, trading noise for enormous savings in per-step cost.
- [Stochastic Programming](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-stochastic-programming.html): Stochastic programming optimizes decisions when some data is random, using probability distributions to model uncertainty and expected outcomes.
- [Subgradient Calculus](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-subgradient-calculus.html): Rules for computing subdifferentials of sums, maxima, and compositions let algorithms find a valid descent direction even at nondifferentiable points.
- [Subgradient Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-subgradient-methods.html): Subgradient methods minimize nondifferentiable convex functions by stepping along any subgradient, using a diminishing step size for convergence.
- [Subgradient Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/subgradient-methods.html): Optimize nondifferentiable convex functions by stepping along any subgradient, trading speed for the ability to handle kinks.
- [Surrogate-Based Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/surrogate-based-optimization.html): Replace an expensive objective with a cheap approximate model, optimize on the surrogate, and validate with occasional true evaluations.
- [The Frank-Wolfe Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-frank-wolfe.html): Frank-Wolfe minimizes a smooth function over a convex set using only linear subproblems, never projecting back onto the set.
- [The Hessian and Curvature](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-hessian-and-curvature.html): The Hessian matrix of second derivatives describes an objective's local curvature, classifying critical points and governing how fast optimizers converge.
- [The Multi-Armed Bandit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-multi-armed-bandit.html): The multi-armed bandit is the simplest model of learning by trial and error: repeatedly pull one of several arms with unknown reward, aiming to maximize total reward.
- [The Nelder-Mead Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-nelder-mead.html): The Nelder-Mead simplex method minimizes a function by moving and reshaping a geometric simplex of points, using only function values.
- [The Proximal Operator](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-proximal-operator.html): The proximal operator generalizes projection: it finds the point that balances staying near a target against reducing a possibly nonsmooth function.
- [The UCB Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-ucb-algorithm.html): The upper-confidence-bound algorithm handles the explore-exploit trade-off by playing the arm with the highest optimistic estimate of its reward.
- [The Wolfe Conditions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-wolfe-conditions.html): The Wolfe conditions are two inequalities a line-search step must satisfy to guarantee both sufficient decrease and enough curvature progress.
- [Trust-Region Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/trust-region-methods.html): Build a local model, trust it only within a region, and expand or shrink that region based on how well the model predicted reality.
- [Two-Stage Stochastic Programming](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-two-stage-stochastic.html): The two-stage model makes a here-and-now decision, observes the random outcome, then takes a recourse action to correct for it, minimizing total expected cost.
- [Uncertainty Sets](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/opt-uncertainty-sets.html): The uncertainty set is the modeling choice at the heart of robust optimization; its shape controls both conservatism and computational tractability.
- [Weak and Strong Duality](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/weak-and-strong-duality.html): Weak duality always bounds the primal by the dual; strong duality closes the gap under convexity and a constraint qualification.

### Numerical Methods
- [Adaptive Mesh Refinement](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adaptive-mesh-refinement.html): Dynamically concentrating grid resolution where the solution demands it, following features as they move and evolve.
- [Adaptive Quadrature](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adaptive-quadrature.html): Numerical integration that automatically refines where the integrand varies rapidly and coarsens where it is smooth.
- [Adaptive Step-Size Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adaptive-step-ode.html): Adaptive ODE solvers estimate local error each step and adjust the step size to hold error near a tolerance, saving work where the solution is smooth.
- [Algebraic Multigrid](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/algebraic-multigrid.html): A multilevel solver that builds its coarse problems purely from the matrix entries, needing no knowledge of the underlying geometry.
- [Automatic Differentiation: Forward and Reverse](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/automatic-differentiation-forward-reverse.html): A technique to compute exact derivatives of code by applying the chain rule mechanically, distinct from both symbolic and finite differences.
- [Barycentric Interpolation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/barycentric-interpolation.html): A numerically stable and fast reformulation of polynomial interpolation through a set of points.
- [Boundary Condition Treatment](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/boundary-condition-treatment.html): How discretized PDEs incorporate the conditions at domain edges, where accuracy and stability are most easily lost.
- [Catastrophic Cancellation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/catastrophic-cancellation.html): Subtracting two nearly equal floating-point numbers annihilates leading digits and amplifies the relative error already present in the inputs.
- [Chebyshev Spectral Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/chebyshev-spectral-methods.html): High-accuracy discretizations for non-periodic problems that represent solutions as sums of Chebyshev polynomials.
- [Classifying Partial Differential Equations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pde-classification.html): PDEs split into elliptic, parabolic, and hyperbolic types, and the type dictates which discretization and boundary conditions are appropriate.
- [Collocation Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/collocation-methods.html): Solving differential equations by requiring the approximate solution to satisfy the equation exactly at a chosen set of points.
- [Conditioning and Backward Stability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/conditioning-and-backward-stability.html): Two distinct ideas that together explain when a computed answer can be trusted: sensitivity of the problem and quality of the algorithm.
- [Conditioning and Stability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/conditioning-and-stability.html): Conditioning measures how sensitive a problem is to input perturbations; stability measures how faithfully an algorithm solves the problem it was given.
- [Convergence Theory of Krylov Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/krylov-convergence-theory.html): How the spectrum and structure of a matrix determine, through polynomial approximation, how fast a Krylov solver converges.
- [Convergence and Error Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/convergence-and-error-analysis.html): Convergence studies confirm that a numerical solution approaches the true one as resolution increases, and measure the rate at which it does.
- [Cubic Splines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cubic-splines.html): Cubic splines join cubic pieces with matched first and second derivatives, giving smooth interpolation that avoids high-degree oscillation.
- [Deflation and Restarting in Krylov Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/deflation-and-restarting.html): Techniques to control memory and rescue convergence in Krylov solvers by recycling or removing troublesome subspace directions.
- [Domain Decomposition and Schwarz Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/domain-decomposition-schwarz.html): Solvers that split a large problem into overlapping or non-overlapping subdomains, solving each locally and coordinating across interfaces.
- [Eigenvalue Algorithms](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/eigenvalue-algorithms.html): Numerical eigenvalue methods range from power iteration for a single dominant value to the QR algorithm for the full spectrum of a matrix.
- [Error Estimation and Adaptivity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/error-estimation-and-adaptivity.html): How solvers measure their own error and refine resolution where it is needed, delivering accuracy without uniform over-resolution.
- [Exponential Integrators](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/exponential-integrators.html): Time-stepping methods that solve the linear stiff part of a problem exactly using the matrix exponential, freeing the step size from stiffness.
- [Fixed-Point Iteration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fixed-point-iteration.html): Rewriting f(x)=0 as x=g(x) and iterating x_{n+1}=g(x_n) converges to a fixed point whenever g is a contraction near the root.
- [Floating-Point Error Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/floating-point-error-analysis.html): How finite-precision arithmetic introduces rounding error, and how to reason about its accumulation and worst cases.
- [Floating-Point Error and Stability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/floating-point-error-and-stability.html): Rounding errors are individually tiny but can accumulate or cancel; stable algorithms keep the total error close to the problem's inherent limit.
- [Floating-Point Representation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/floating-point-representation.html): Computers store real numbers as a sign, a fractional mantissa, and an exponent, trading exact range for finite precision.
- [Flux-Corrected Transport](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/flux-corrected-transport.html): A shock-capturing technique that blends a high-order flux with a diffusive low-order flux to prevent new extrema from forming.
- [Fourier Spectral Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fourier-spectral-methods.html): Discretizations for periodic problems that represent solutions as Fourier series, turning differentiation into multiplication.
- [GMRES](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gmres.html): GMRES solves general nonsymmetric systems by minimizing the residual over a growing Krylov subspace, at the cost of storing the accumulated basis.
- [GMRES vs BiCGStab vs MINRES](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gmres-vs-bicgstab-vs-minres.html): Three Krylov solvers for large linear systems, each trading memory, robustness, and problem structure differently.
- [Gaussian Quadrature](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gaussian-quadrature.html): Integration rules that achieve the highest possible accuracy for a given number of points by optimizing both nodes and weights.
- [Geometric Multigrid](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/geometric-multigrid.html): A multilevel method that uses a hierarchy of nested meshes to solve elliptic problems with work proportional to the number of unknowns.
- [Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gram-schmidt-orthogonalization.html): The process of turning a set of vectors into an orthonormal basis, and the numerical care needed to do it stably.
- [Implicit-Explicit (IMEX) Schemes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/imex-schemes.html): Time integrators that treat stiff terms implicitly and non-stiff terms explicitly, avoiding both instability and costly nonlinear solves.
- [Interpolation: Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/interpolation-overview.html): Interpolation constructs a function passing exactly through given data points, enabling evaluation, differentiation, and integration between samples.
- [Iterative Refinement](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/iterative-refinement.html): Recovering accuracy lost to rounding by computing a residual, solving for the correction, and adding it back.
- [Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/jacobi-and-gauss-seidel.html): These classic stationary iterations split the matrix and sweep repeatedly; Gauss-Seidel reuses updated values and usually converges faster than Jacobi.
- [Krylov Subspace Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/krylov-subspace-methods.html): A family of iterative solvers that build solutions from powers of a matrix applied to a vector, using only matrix-vector products.
- [Lagrange Interpolation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lagrange-interpolation.html): The Lagrange form writes the unique interpolating polynomial as a weighted sum of basis polynomials, each one at its own node and zero at the others.
- [Least Squares Problems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/least-squares-problems.html): Finding the best approximate solution to an overdetermined system by minimizing the sum of squared residuals.
- [Machine Epsilon and Rounding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/machine-epsilon-and-rounding.html): Machine epsilon is the smallest gap between 1 and the next representable number, and it sets the relative accuracy of every floating-point operation.
- [Mesh Generation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mesh-generation.html): Mesh generation partitions a domain into elements or cells; mesh quality strongly controls the accuracy and stability of every discretization on it.
- [Monte Carlo Integration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/monte-carlo-integration.html): Estimating integrals by random sampling, with error that shrinks independently of dimension.
- [Multigrid Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multigrid-methods.html): Multigrid solves elliptic systems in near-linear time by damping errors across a hierarchy of grids, each scale handling the errors it resolves best.
- [Multigrid as a Preconditioner](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multigrid-preconditioning.html): Using a single multigrid cycle to precondition a Krylov solver, combining multigrid speed with Krylov robustness.
- [Multistep Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multistep-methods.html): Multistep methods reuse several past values to advance a step, with Adams families for nonstiff problems and BDF families for stiff ones.
- [Newton's Divided Differences](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/newton-divided-differences.html): Newton's form builds the interpolating polynomial incrementally from divided-difference coefficients, so new data points extend the polynomial cheaply.
- [Newton-Krylov Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/newton-krylov-methods.html): Solving large nonlinear systems by combining Newton's method with a Krylov solver for the linear step, avoiding explicit Jacobians.
- [Newton-Raphson Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/newton-raphson-method.html): Newton's method follows the tangent line to a better estimate, converging quadratically near a simple root when the derivative is available.
- [Norms and the Condition Number](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/norms-and-condition-number.html): Vector and matrix norms measure size and error, and the matrix condition number bounds how much a linear solve can amplify input errors.
- [Numerical Differentiation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/numerical-differentiation.html): Finite-difference formulas estimate derivatives from function samples, balancing truncation error that falls with step size against rounding error that rises.
- [Numerical Integration: Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/numerical-integration-overview.html): Quadrature rules approximate a definite integral as a weighted sum of function values, chosen to be exact for polynomials up to some degree.
- [ODE Initial-Value Problems: Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ode-ivp-overview.html): Initial-value ODE solvers march a solution forward in time from a known state, trading accuracy, stability, and cost across method families.
- [Operator Splitting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/operator-splitting.html): Advancing a multi-physics problem by solving each physical process in sequence over each time step, using the best method for each.
- [Order of Convergence](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/convergence-order-root-finding.html): The order of convergence quantifies how fast an iterative method's error shrinks, distinguishing linear, superlinear, and quadratic methods.
- [Pivoting Strategies](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pivoting-strategies.html): Pivoting reorders rows or columns during elimination to avoid tiny pivots, keeping multipliers bounded and the factorization numerically stable.
- [Preconditioning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/preconditioning.html): A preconditioner transforms a linear system into an equivalent one with clustered eigenvalues, so Krylov solvers converge in far fewer iterations.
- [Preconditioning for Iterative Solvers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/preconditioning-basics.html): Transforming a linear system so that an iterative solver converges in far fewer steps by clustering the spectrum.
- [Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/randomized-numerical-linear-algebra.html): Using random projections to compute approximate factorizations of huge matrices far faster than deterministic methods.
- [Reordering and Nested Dissection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reordering-nested-dissection.html): Permuting the unknowns of a sparse matrix before factorization to minimize fill-in and expose parallelism.
- [Richardson Extrapolation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/richardson-extrapolation.html): A technique that combines approximations at different step sizes to cancel leading error terms and gain accuracy for free.
- [Romberg Integration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/romberg-integration.html): Romberg integration applies Richardson extrapolation to the trapezoidal rule, building a table that converges rapidly for smooth integrands.
- [Root Finding: Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/root-finding-overview.html): Root finding solves f(x)=0 numerically, choosing among bracketing, open, and hybrid methods that trade guaranteed convergence against speed.
- [Runge's Phenomenon](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/runges-phenomenon.html): High-degree polynomial interpolation on equally spaced nodes oscillates violently near the interval ends, a failure cured by better node placement or splines.
- [Runge-Kutta Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/runge-kutta-methods.html): A broad family of one-step time integrators that reach high accuracy by sampling the derivative at several intermediate stages.
- [Runge-Kutta RK4](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/runge-kutta-rk4.html): The classic fourth-order Runge-Kutta method combines four slope evaluations per step for high accuracy without needing derivatives of f.
- [Simpson's Rule](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/simpsons-rule.html): Simpson's rule fits parabolas through triples of points, achieving fourth-order accuracy that integrates cubics exactly.
- [Solving Linear Systems: Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/linear-systems-overview.html): Ax=b is the core of scientific computing; the choice between direct and iterative solvers depends on size, sparsity, and structure.
- [Sparse Direct Solvers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sparse-direct-solvers.html): Factorization-based solvers that exploit sparsity to solve linear systems exactly, trading memory for robustness against iterative failure.
- [Sparse Matrix Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sparse-matrix-methods.html): Sparse matrices store and operate on only their nonzero entries, making it possible to solve systems with millions of unknowns.
- [Spectral Methods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/spectral-methods.html): Spectral methods represent the solution as a global sum of smooth basis functions, achieving exponential accuracy for smooth problems.
- [Stability Regions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/stability-regions-ode.html): A method's stability region is the set of step-times-eigenvalue values for which it stays bounded, explaining why stiff problems need implicit solvers.
- [Stiff ODE Solvers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/stiff-ode-solvers.html): Implicit integrators designed for systems with widely separated time scales, where explicit methods demand impractically small steps.
- [Stiff Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/stiff-systems.html): Stiff ODEs combine widely separated time scales; explicit solvers require impractically small steps, so implicit methods are essential.
- [Successive Over-Relaxation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/successive-over-relaxation.html): SOR accelerates Gauss-Seidel by over-correcting each update with a relaxation factor, dramatically speeding convergence when the factor is tuned well.
- [Symplectic Integrators](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/symplectic-integrators.html): Time-stepping methods for Hamiltonian systems that preserve phase-space structure, keeping energy bounded over very long integrations.
- [The Adjoint Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adjoint-method.html): A technique to compute the gradient of a scalar objective with respect to many parameters at a cost independent of the parameter count.
- [The Arnoldi Iteration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/arnoldi-iteration.html): A Krylov method that reduces a large nonsymmetric matrix to a small upper-Hessenberg form, giving eigenvalues and underpinning GMRES.
- [The Backward Euler Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/backward-euler-method.html): Backward Euler evaluates the slope at the unknown next point, giving unconditional stability that makes it a workhorse for stiff systems.
- [The Bisection Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bisection-method.html): Bisection halves a sign-changing interval at every step, giving guaranteed but linear convergence to a root of a continuous function.
- [The CFL Condition](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cfl-condition.html): The stability limit that ties the time step of an explicit scheme to the grid spacing and the fastest wave speed.
- [The Conjugate Gradient Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/conjugate-gradient-method.html): The optimal short-recurrence Krylov solver for symmetric positive-definite systems, minimizing energy error with constant memory per step.
- [The Conjugate Gradient Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/conjugate-gradient.html): Conjugate gradient solves symmetric positive-definite systems by minimizing a quadratic along mutually conjugate search directions, using only matrix-vector products.
- [The Crank-Nicolson Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/crank-nicolson-method.html): Crank-Nicolson averages explicit and implicit steps to solve parabolic PDEs with second-order accuracy in time and unconditional stability.
- [The Finite Difference Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/finite-difference-method.html): Finite differences replace derivatives with difference quotients on a grid, turning a differential equation into a system of algebraic equations.
- [The Finite Element Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/finite-element-method.html): A discretization that represents the solution as a sum of local basis functions over a mesh and enforces the equation in a weak, integral sense.
- [The Finite Volume Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/finite-volume-method.html): A discretization that enforces conservation exactly by tracking fluxes across the faces of control volumes.
- [The Forward Euler Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/forward-euler-method.html): Forward Euler takes a single step along the current slope; it is the simplest ODE solver, first-order accurate and only conditionally stable.
- [The Lanczos Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lanczos-algorithm.html): A Krylov method that reduces a large symmetric matrix to a small tridiagonal one, yielding extreme eigenvalues cheaply.
- [The Method of Lines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/method-of-lines.html): A strategy for PDEs that discretizes space first, turning the problem into a large system of ordinary differential equations in time.
- [The Particle-in-Cell Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/particle-in-cell-method.html): A hybrid scheme that follows particles through continuous space while solving fields on a grid, the workhorse of kinetic plasma simulation.
- [The Power Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/power-method-eigenvalues.html): The simplest eigenvalue algorithm: repeatedly apply a matrix to a vector to converge onto the dominant eigenvector.
- [The QR Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qr-algorithm.html): The QR algorithm computes all eigenvalues of a matrix by repeated QR factorization, accelerated by Hessenberg reduction and shifts.
- [The QR Algorithm for Eigenvalues](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qr-algorithm-eigenvalues.html): The standard dense eigenvalue method: repeatedly factor a matrix into orthogonal times triangular, then reverse the product.
- [The Secant Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/secant-method.html): The secant method mimics Newton's step using a finite-difference slope from two prior points, avoiding derivatives at a modest cost in convergence speed.
- [The Singular Value Decomposition](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/singular-value-decomposition.html): A factorization that reveals the fundamental geometry of any matrix and underlies least squares, rank, and low-rank approximation.
- [The Spectral Element Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/spectral-element-method.html): A hybrid that combines the geometric flexibility of finite elements with the exponential accuracy of spectral methods.
- [The Thomas Algorithm](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/tridiagonal-thomas-algorithm.html): The Thomas algorithm solves tridiagonal systems in linear time, the specialized elimination behind splines and one-dimensional implicit schemes.
- [The Trapezoidal Rule](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/trapezoidal-rule.html): The trapezoidal rule approximates an integral by straight-line segments between samples, with error that falls as the square of the panel width.
- [Total Variation Diminishing Schemes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/total-variation-diminishing-schemes.html): High-resolution schemes that guarantee no new oscillations by ensuring the solution's total variation never increases.
- [Verification and Order of Convergence](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/verification-and-convergence-order.html): Confirming that a code solves its equations correctly by measuring how fast the error shrinks under mesh refinement.
- [Von Neumann Stability Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/von-neumann-stability-analysis.html): Von Neumann analysis tests a linear scheme's stability by tracking how each Fourier mode's amplitude grows or decays per time step.
- [WENO and ENO Schemes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/weno-eno-schemes.html): High-order finite-difference schemes for hyperbolic conservation laws that capture shocks sharply without spurious oscillations.

### Ml For Fusion
- [Accelerating Simulation with ML](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-accelerating-simulation.html): Using learned models to speed up, replace steps in, or guide expensive plasma and reactor simulations.
- [Active Learning for Costly Experiments](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/active-learning-costly-experiments.html): Active learning chooses which expensive simulations or discharges to run next, extracting the most information per costly evaluation.
- [Active Learning for Expensive Simulations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-active-learning-simulations.html): Spending a limited simulation budget on the points that most improve a model or answer a question.
- [Anomaly Detection on Diagnostics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-anomaly-detection-diagnostics.html): Flagging diagnostic signals that depart from normal behavior, often without labeled examples of every fault.
- [Anomaly Detection on Machine Subsystems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/anomaly-detection-subsystems.html): Unsupervised models learn normal behavior of machine subsystems and flag deviations that may signal faults before they cause failures.
- [Autoencoders for Plasma Data](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-autoencoders-plasma.html): Compressing high-dimensional diagnostic data into a low-dimensional latent space for detection, denoising, and analysis.
- [Autoencoders for Plasma Dimensionality Reduction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/autoencoders-plasma-dimensionality.html): Autoencoders compress high-dimensional plasma data into compact latent representations for visualization, anomaly detection, and surrogate modeling.
- [Bayesian Inference of Plasma State](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bayesian-inference-plasma-state.html): Bayesian methods combine diagnostics and priors into a probability distribution over the plasma state, giving best estimates with calibrated uncertainty.
- [Bayesian Optimization for Experiments](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-bayesian-optimization-experiments.html): Choosing the next expensive experiment or simulation to run so that few evaluations find a good setting.
- [Bayesian Optimization of Scenarios](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bayesian-optimization-scenario.html): Bayesian optimization tunes operating scenarios and design parameters by balancing exploration and exploitation over an expensive objective.
- [Calibration of Probabilistic Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-calibration-probabilistic-models.html): Making predicted probabilities and uncertainties mean what they say, so decisions can rely on them.
- [Class Imbalance and Rare Events](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-class-imbalance-rare-events.html): Why disruptions and other rare plasma events break naive accuracy, and how to train and evaluate honestly around them.
- [Clustering Plasma Regimes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-clustering-plasma-regimes.html): Grouping discharges or time slices into regimes without labels, to organize data and reveal structure.
- [Convolutional Networks for Plasma Imaging](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/convolutional-nets-plasma-imaging.html): Convolutional neural networks analyze camera and imaging-diagnostic data to detect events, track structures, and infer plasma conditions.
- [Cross-Machine Transfer and Domain Shift](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-domain-shift-cross-machine.html): Why models trained on one tokamak degrade on another, and how transfer learning helps.
- [Cross-Validation for Fusion Data](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-cross-validation-fusion.html): Estimating how a model will generalize when data are scarce, correlated, and grouped by shot.
- [Data Augmentation for Fusion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-data-augmentation-fusion.html): Expanding scarce, imbalanced datasets with transformations and synthetic examples, without inventing physics.
- [Data Pipelines for Fusion ML](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-data-pipelines-fusion.html): The unglamorous work of collecting, cleaning, aligning, and labeling data that determines whether any model succeeds.
- [Data-Driven Scaling Laws](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-data-driven-scaling-laws.html): Empirical relationships fit across devices that predict confinement and performance from engineering parameters.
- [Data-Driven Scaling Laws for Confinement](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-driven-scaling-laws.html): Regression across many devices yields empirical scaling laws that predict energy-confinement time from engineering parameters, guiding new-device design.
- [Deep Learning for Magnetic Probes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/deep-learning-magnetic-probes.html): Networks infer plasma position, shape, and current from arrays of magnetic sensors, and detect and correct faulty probe signals in real time.
- [Digital Twins and ML](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-digital-twin-fusion.html): Fast, data-informed models of a device that mirror its behavior for study, control design, and what-if analysis.
- [Dimensionality Reduction for Plasma Data](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-dimensionality-reduction-plasma.html): Compressing many correlated diagnostic channels into a few informative coordinates.
- [Disruption Avoidance and Mitigation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-disruption-avoidance.html): Turning a disruption prediction into an action: steering the plasma away from the boundary or safely shutting it down.
- [Disruption Early-Warning Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/disruption-early-warning.html): An end-to-end disruption warning system fuses diagnostics, a trained predictor, and a mitigation trigger under strict real-time latency budgets.
- [Disruption Prediction in Tokamaks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-disruption-prediction.html): Classifiers that estimate, from live diagnostics, whether a tokamak plasma is approaching a sudden loss of confinement.
- [Ensembles and Model Averaging](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-ensembles-fusion.html): Combining several models to improve accuracy and, importantly, to estimate uncertainty.
- [Equilibrium Reconstruction with Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-equilibrium-reconstruction-nn.html): Learning fast approximations to the Grad-Shafranov solution that maps magnetic measurements to plasma shape and current.
- [Feature Engineering for Plasma Signals](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-feature-engineering-plasma.html): Turning raw diagnostics into physically meaningful inputs that make models more accurate and portable.
- [Foundation Models for Plasma Physics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/foundation-models-plasma-physics.html): Large models pretrained on broad plasma data aim to transfer across tasks and devices with limited task-specific labels.
- [Gaussian Processes for Fusion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-gaussian-processes.html): A flexible regression method that reports calibrated uncertainty, well suited to small, expensive datasets.
- [Gaussian-Process Regression for Plasma](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gaussian-process-regression-plasma.html): Gaussian processes fit smooth plasma profiles from scattered measurements while returning principled uncertainty and gradient estimates.
- [Generative Models in Fusion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-generative-models-fusion.html): Models that learn to produce new plasma-like data, for scenario design, augmentation, and exploration.
- [Generative Scenario Design](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/generative-scenario-design.html): Generative models propose candidate operating scenarios that meet performance and stability targets, widening the search beyond hand-tuned recipes.
- [Generative Scenario Design](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-scenario-generative-design.html): Proposing candidate operating scenarios with learned models, then screening them with physics.
- [Image Diagnostics with CNNs](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-image-diagnostics-cnn.html): Applying convolutional networks to fast cameras, tomography, and other imaging diagnostics.
- [Instability and Event Classification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-instability-classification.html): Recognizing which MHD mode or plasma event is present from diagnostic signatures.
- [Interpretability and Explainability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-interpretability-fusion.html): Understanding why a model made a prediction, which matters when physicists and operators must trust it.
- [Kalman Filters and Learned Estimators](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-kalman-filters-vs-ml.html): How classical model-based filtering relates to and combines with data-driven state estimation.
- [Limits of ML in Fusion, and Honest Practice](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-limits-and-honest-practice.html): A candid summary of what machine learning can and cannot do for fusion, and the standards that keep it useful.
- [ML Tomography for Bolometry](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-tomography-bolometry.html): Learned tomographic inversion reconstructs 2D radiated-power maps from sparse bolometer lines of sight, aiding impurity and radiation control.
- [ML for Density-Limit Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-density-limit-prediction.html): Learned models estimate proximity to the operational density limit, where excessive fueling drives radiative collapse and disruption.
- [ML for Edge-Localized-Mode Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-elm-prediction-control.html): Machine learning forecasts edge-localized modes and supports control strategies that mitigate the transient heat loads they impose on plasma-facing components.
- [ML for Plasma State Classification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-tokamak-state-classification.html): Classifiers label the plasma regime in real time, distinguishing confinement modes and operational phases to inform control decisions.
- [ML-Assisted Diagnostics Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-diagnostics-overview.html): Across diagnostics, machine learning inverts sensor signals into plasma quantities, fuses multiple instruments, and flags faults faster than manual analysis.
- [ML-Assisted Interferometry Inference](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-interferometry-inference.html): Learned inversions turn line-integrated interferometer phase measurements into density profiles, handling fringe ambiguity and limited views.
- [ML-Assisted Thomson Scattering Inference](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-thomson-scattering-inference.html): Neural models infer electron temperature and density from Thomson scattering spectra faster and more robustly than fitting each spectrum by hand.
- [Machine Learning for Coil-Current Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-coil-current-optimization.html): Learned models find the coil-current set that produces a desired plasma shape and position, both offline for design and in real time for control.
- [Machine Learning for Divertor Heat-Flux Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-heat-flux-divertor.html): Models predict and monitor the intense, narrow heat-flux loads on the divertor, informing detachment control and component protection.
- [Machine Learning for Fusion: An Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-fusion-overview.html): How data-driven models complement physics simulation across control, prediction, reconstruction, and design in magnetic-confinement fusion.
- [Machine Learning for Impurity Transport](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-impurity-transport.html): Surrogates predict how impurities move and accumulate in the plasma, informing radiation control and avoidance of performance-limiting buildup.
- [Machine Learning for MHD Stability Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-mhd-stability-prediction.html): Surrogates estimate magnetohydrodynamic stability boundaries fast enough for scenario design and real-time avoidance of unstable operating points.
- [Machine Learning for Magnet and Coil Design](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-magnet-coil-design.html): Surrogates and optimizers explore coil geometries and current sets that produce a target magnetic field while respecting stress and superconductor limits.
- [Machine Learning for Materials-Degradation Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-materials-degradation.html): Data-driven models predict how neutron irradiation and thermal cycling degrade fusion materials, guiding material choice and component lifetime estimates.
- [Machine Learning for Neutral-Beam Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-neutral-beam-modeling.html): Surrogates approximate neutral-beam deposition and current drive, giving fast estimates of heating and driven current for scenario design and control.
- [Machine-Learned Acceleration of Gyrokinetics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-acceleration-gyrokinetics.html): Learned models accelerate gyrokinetic turbulence simulation by replacing costly subcomponents or emulating full flux outputs.
- [Machine-Learned Disruption Precursors](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-disruption-precursors.html): Classifiers learn the signatures that precede a plasma disruption, providing warning time for mitigation before confinement is abruptly lost.
- [Machine-Learned Pedestal Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-pedestal-prediction.html): Neural models predict the height and width of the edge transport barrier, a key driver of overall confinement in high-confinement plasmas.
- [Machine-Learned Profile Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-profile-prediction.html): Models predict steady-state or evolving temperature, density, and current profiles from engineering settings, accelerating scenario studies.
- [Machine-Learned Radiation-Transport Surrogates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-radiation-transport-surrogate.html): Learned surrogates approximate particle- and radiation-transport codes, speeding shielding design and dose estimation across many configurations.
- [Machine-Learned Reduced Transport Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-reduced-transport-models.html): Reduced transport surrogates learn the mapping from plasma profiles to transport coefficients, enabling whole-discharge simulation at interactive speed.
- [Machine-Learned Surrogate for RF Heating](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-rf-heating-surrogate.html): Surrogates approximate radio-frequency wave heating and current drive, replacing slow wave-propagation solvers in scenario and control loops.
- [Machine-Learned Surrogate for Tritium Breeding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-tritium-breeding-surrogate.html): A focused surrogate predicts the tritium breeding ratio from blanket design parameters, accelerating the search for a self-sufficient fuel cycle.
- [Machine-Learned Surrogates for Neutronics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-surrogate-neutronics.html): Surrogate models approximate expensive neutron-transport simulations, giving fast estimates of tritium breeding, heating, and shielding for design scans.
- [Machine-Learned Turbulence Closures](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-turbulence-closures.html): Neural closures replace unresolved turbulent fluxes in reduced plasma models, capturing effects that would otherwise require expensive kinetic simulation.
- [Monte Carlo Methods and ML](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-monte-carlo-methods.html): How random sampling underpins neutron transport and uncertainty studies, and where learning accelerates it.
- [Neural Network Architectures for Sequences and Fields](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-neural-net-architectures.html): Choosing recurrent, convolutional, attention, or graph models to match plasma data structure.
- [Neural Network Basics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-neural-network-basics.html): The building blocks of the models used across fusion ML, from layers to training.
- [Neural Operators for PDEs](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-neural-operators-pde.html): Networks that learn mappings between functions, approximating the solution operators of the equations governing plasmas.
- [Neural-Network Equilibrium Solvers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/nn-equilibrium-solvers.html): Neural networks learn to solve the Grad-Shafranov equation orders of magnitude faster than iterative solvers, enabling near-instant magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium estimates.
- [Operator Learning and Fourier Neural Operators](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/operator-learning-fno-plasma.html): Operator-learning methods approximate the solution operators of plasma partial differential equations, generalizing across inputs and resolutions.
- [Out-of-Distribution Detection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-out-of-distribution-detection.html): Recognizing when a model is being asked about inputs unlike anything it was trained on.
- [Overfitting and Regularization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-overfitting-regularization.html): Why models memorize small fusion datasets, and the techniques that make them generalize.
- [Physics-Constrained ML for Transport](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/physics-constrained-ml-transport.html): Embedding conservation laws and known limits into transport models keeps predictions physically valid and improves extrapolation beyond the training data.
- [Physics-Informed Networks for Grad-Shafranov](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pinns-grad-shafranov.html): Physics-informed neural networks solve the Grad-Shafranov equilibrium equation by minimizing the PDE residual directly, needing few or no labeled solutions.
- [Physics-Informed Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-physics-informed-networks.html): Neural networks trained to respect governing equations, improving data efficiency and extrapolation.
- [Plasma Profile Prediction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-plasma-profile-prediction.html): Predicting radial profiles of density, temperature, and pressure faster than transport simulation allows.
- [QLKNN-Style Neural Transport Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qlknn-neural-transport.html): Neural networks trained on quasilinear gyrokinetic flux databases predict turbulent transport in milliseconds, replacing runtime calls to slow physics codes.
- [Real-Time Equilibrium Reconstruction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-realtime-equilibrium-reconstruction.html): Neural surrogates reconstruct the plasma equilibrium from magnetic measurements within the control cycle, faster than iterative reconstruction codes.
- [Real-Time Inference for Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-real-time-inference-control.html): Running a model fast and reliably enough to sit inside a plasma control loop.
- [Real-Time State Estimation with ML](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-state-estimation-realtime.html): Inferring the current plasma state from partial, noisy diagnostics fast enough to feed control.
- [Recurrent Networks for Plasma Time Series](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/recurrent-nets-plasma-timeseries.html): Recurrent neural networks model the temporal dynamics of plasma signals for forecasting, event detection, and control.
- [Regression Methods for Fusion Data](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-regression-fusion.html): Fitting continuous relationships from data, from linear models to flexible learners, with fusion examples.
- [Reinforcement Learning for Heating and Current Drive](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rl-heating-current-drive.html): Reinforcement learning discovers policies that command heating and current-drive actuators to reach and hold target plasma states.
- [Reinforcement-Learning Basics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-reinforcement-learning-basics.html): The core concepts of learning to act, framed for readers who will meet RL in plasma control.
- [Reinforcement-Learning Control of Tokamaks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-rl-tokamak-control.html): Learning control policies that command magnetic coils to shape and stabilize a plasma, as demonstrated in published TCV work.
- [Reproducibility in Fusion ML](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-reproducibility-ml-fusion.html): Making results repeatable and auditable, the standard that separates credible work from a lucky run.
- [Reward Shaping for Plasma Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-reward-shaping-control.html): Designing the reward signal so a learned controller pursues the physical goal and not a loophole.
- [Safe Exploration in Learned Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-safe-exploration-control.html): Keeping a learning or learned controller inside physically safe bounds on hardware where mistakes are costly.
- [Sim-to-Real Transfer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-sim-to-real-transfer.html): Why a policy or model trained in simulation may fail on hardware, and how to narrow the gap.
- [Surrogate Models for Transport](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-transport-surrogates.html): Learned stand-ins for turbulent transport calculations that make integrated modeling and control feasible.
- [Surrogate Models for Turbulence](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-turbulence-surrogates.html): Emulating gyrokinetic turbulence results, the most expensive step in transport modeling, with learned models.
- [Surrogate Models: Concepts](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-surrogate-models.html): Fast approximations that stand in for expensive simulations, and the rules for using them without fooling yourself.
- [Surrogates for Neutronics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-neutronics-surrogates.html): Learned models that approximate expensive neutron-transport calculations for shielding, activation, and breeding studies.
- [Time-Series Classification for Plasma Diagnostics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-time-series-classification.html): Methods for labeling multichannel, non-stationary plasma signals in real time and offline.
- [Transfer Learning and Pretraining](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-transfer-pretraining-fusion.html): Reusing knowledge from large or related datasets to help models learn from scarce fusion data.
- [Transformer Models for Fusion Time Series](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/transformer-models-fusion-timeseries.html): Attention-based transformers model long-range dependencies in multi-channel plasma signals for prediction and representation learning.
- [Uncertainty Quantification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-uncertainty-quantification.html): Knowing how much to trust a model's prediction, and communicating that alongside the number.
- [Uncertainty-Aware ML Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/uncertainty-aware-ml-control.html): Control policies that quantify their own uncertainty can defer to safe fallbacks when they encounter conditions outside their training experience.
- [Worked Example: A Simple Disruptivity Classifier](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/ml-worked-example-disruptivity.html): A minimal, honest sketch of training and evaluating a disruption predictor, emphasizing correct practice.

### Quantum Hardware
- [Active Qubit Reset](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/active-qubit-reset.html): Active reset deterministically returns a qubit to its ground state in microseconds, instead of waiting many relaxation times for passive decay.
- [Arbitrary Waveform Generators](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/arbitrary-waveform-generators.html): Arbitrary waveform generators synthesize the precisely shaped pulses that drive qubit gates, one of the workhorses of quantum control.
- [Asymmetric SQUID Transmons](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/asymmetric-squid-transmon.html): Making the two junctions of a SQUID unequal reduces the tuning range but adds a lower sweet spot and limits the qubit's exposure to flux noise.
- [Bosonic and Cat Qubits](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/bosonic-cat-qubits.html): Bosonic qubits store information in the many levels of a microwave cavity mode, using redundancy in one physical element to resist errors.
- [CLOPS and Speed Benchmarking](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/clops-speed-benchmarking.html): CLOPS measures how fast a quantum processor runs circuits, capturing throughput that fidelity-based metrics like quantum volume ignore.
