- [Hybrid Physics-ML Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hybrid-physics-ml.html): Hybrid models combine a trusted physical model with a learned component that corrects its errors or supplies its missing pieces.
- [Inverse Problems with Machine Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/inverse-problems-ml.html): Inverse problems infer hidden parameters or fields from indirect measurements, and machine learning provides fast, regularized estimators.
- [Koopman Operator Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/koopman-operator-learning.html): The Koopman operator recasts nonlinear dynamics as a linear evolution of observables, enabling linear tools on nonlinear systems.
- [Kriging](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/kriging.html): Kriging is Gaussian process interpolation developed in geostatistics, predicting a spatial field with a best linear unbiased estimator.
- [Lagrangian Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/lagrangian-neural-networks.html): Lagrangian neural networks learn a system's Lagrangian, deriving physically consistent dynamics even in arbitrary or constrained coordinates.
- [Latent-Space Dynamics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/latent-space-dynamics.html): Latent-space dynamics models evolve a compressed representation forward in time, giving fast surrogates for high-dimensional simulations.
- [Learning GP Hyperparameters](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/gp-hyperparameter-learning.html): Gaussian process hyperparameters are set by maximizing the marginal likelihood, which balances data fit against model complexity automatically.
- [Monte Carlo Dropout](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mc-dropout.html): Monte Carlo dropout estimates uncertainty by keeping dropout active at prediction time and sampling many stochastic forward passes.
- [Multi-Fidelity Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/multi-fidelity-modeling.html): Multi-fidelity methods combine many cheap approximate runs with a few expensive accurate ones to build an accurate model efficiently.
- [Neural Closure Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neural-closure-models.html): Neural closures learn the unresolved subgrid terms of a coarse simulation, letting a cheap grid approximate expensive high-resolution physics.
- [Neural Operators](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/neural-operators-overview.html): Neural operators learn mappings between function spaces, so one trained model can solve a whole family of PDEs at any resolution.
- [Operator Learning Theory](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/operator-learning-theory.html): Operator learning studies when and how mappings between infinite-dimensional function spaces can be approximated and generalized from data.
- [PINN Loss and Collocation Points](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pinn-loss-and-collocation.html): The PINN objective is a weighted sum of residual, boundary, initial, and data losses evaluated at sampled collocation points.
- [PINN Training Pathologies](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pinn-training-pathologies.html): Physics-informed networks fail in characteristic ways: stiff gradients, spectral bias, and imbalanced loss terms that stall optimization.
- [POD and Galerkin Projection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/pod-galerkin.html): Proper orthogonal decomposition extracts an optimal linear basis from data, and Galerkin projection evolves the equations within it.
- [Physics-Constrained Optimization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/physics-constrained-optimization.html): Physics-constrained optimization searches for the best design while requiring that governing equations and physical limits are respected.
- [Physics-Informed Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/physics-informed-neural-networks.html): A PINN trains a neural network to satisfy a differential equation by penalizing the equation's residual at sampled points inside the domain.
- [Reduced-Order Modeling with ML](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reduced-order-modeling-ml.html): Reduced-order models compress a high-dimensional simulation into a few coordinates whose dynamics are cheap to evolve.
- [Scientific Machine Learning](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/scientific-machine-learning-overview.html): Scientific machine learning fuses data-driven models with the governing equations, symmetries, and constraints of physical systems.
- [Sparse Gaussian Processes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sparse-gaussian-processes.html): Sparse Gaussian processes summarize a large dataset with a small set of inducing points, cutting the cubic cost of exact inference.
- [Sparse Regression and SINDy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sparse-regression-sindy.html): SINDy discovers governing equations by selecting a few active terms from a large library of candidate functions using sparse regression.
- [Super-Resolution of Simulations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/super-resolution-simulations.html): Learned super-resolution reconstructs fine-scale simulation detail from a coarse field, mimicking a high-resolution run at lower cost.
- [Surrogate Modeling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/surrogate-modeling.html): A surrogate is a fast approximation of an expensive simulation, trained on solver outputs to enable many-query design and analysis.
- [Symbolic Regression](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/symbolic-regression.html): Symbolic regression searches the space of mathematical expressions for a compact formula that fits data and can be read and interpreted.
- [The Adjoint Method](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/adjoint-method-ml.html): The adjoint method computes the gradient of an objective with respect to many parameters at a cost independent of the number of parameters.
- [Uncertainty Quantification in ML](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/uncertainty-quantification-ml.html): Uncertainty quantification separates noise in the data from ignorance in the model, so predictions come with honest, actionable error bars.

### Quantum Ml
- [Amplitude Encoding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-amplitude-encoding.html): Amplitude encoding packs a classical vector into the amplitudes of a quantum state, storing 2^n numbers in n qubits but at a steep preparation cost.
- [Angle Encoding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-angle-encoding.html): Angle encoding writes each feature into a qubit rotation angle, giving a shallow, hardware-friendly embedding that dominates near-term quantum machine learning.
- [Basis Encoding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-basis-encoding.html): Basis encoding stores classical bitstrings directly as computational basis states, the simplest and most transparent way to load discrete data into a circuit.
- [Benchmarking Quantum ML Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-benchmarking.html): Fair benchmarking of quantum machine learning demands strong classical baselines, honest resource accounting, and datasets that actually test the claimed strength.
- [Classical Simulability and Dequantization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-classical-simulability.html): Some quantum machine learning methods can be matched by classical algorithms, so a proposed advantage only holds if no efficient classical method exists.
- [Cost Functions and Measurement](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-cost-functions.html): In quantum machine learning the loss is built from expectation values of observables, and its structure decides both what is learned and whether training is possible.
- [Data Encoding Strategies](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-data-encoding-overview.html): Getting classical data into a quantum state is a modeling decision with deep consequences for capacity, cost, and whether any speedup survives.
- [Data Re-uploading](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-data-reuploading.html): Data re-uploading feeds the input into a circuit multiple times, interleaved with trainable layers, letting even a single qubit approximate rich functions.
- [Encoding and Fourier Expressivity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-encoding-expressivity.html): A quantum model built by repeated data encoding computes a Fourier series in the input, so the encoding gates decide exactly which functions it can represent.
- [Entangling Layers and Ansatz Design](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-entangling-layers.html): Entangling layers create correlations between qubits that classical product states cannot represent, and their pattern shapes a circuit's power and trainability.
- [Expressivity of Quantum Circuits](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-expressivity.html): Expressivity measures how large a family of states or functions a parameterized circuit can reach, and it trades off directly against trainability.
- [Hybrid Quantum-Classical Training](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-hybrid-training.html): Near-term quantum machine learning runs a quantum circuit for evaluation and a classical optimizer for parameter updates, looping between the two.
- [Near-Term Feasibility and NISQ Constraints](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-near-term-feasibility.html): Today's noisy, intermediate-scale quantum devices limit qubit count, circuit depth, and reliability, which sets hard bounds on what quantum machine learning can do now.
- [Noise, Decoherence, and Error Mitigation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-noise-error.html): Hardware noise corrupts every quantum computation; error mitigation reduces its effect on expectation values without the full overhead of error correction.
- [Parameterized Quantum Circuits](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-parameterized-circuits.html): A parameterized quantum circuit is a fixed gate structure with tunable rotation angles, forming the trainable core of nearly all near-term quantum machine learning.
- [Quantum Advantage in ML: Claims and Caveats](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-quantum-advantage.html): Quantum advantage in machine learning means solving a learning task better or faster than any classical method, a bar that few results clearly meet.
- [Quantum Boltzmann Machines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-quantum-boltzmann.html): A quantum Boltzmann machine is an energy-based generative model whose distribution comes from the thermal state of a quantum Hamiltonian.
- [Quantum Circuit Born Machines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-born-machines.html): A quantum circuit Born machine is a generative model whose output distribution is the measurement probabilities of a trained parameterized circuit.
- [Quantum Feature Maps](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-feature-maps.html): A quantum feature map embeds classical data into a high-dimensional quantum Hilbert space, where linear separations may correspond to nonlinear boundaries in the original space.
- [Quantum Fisher Information and Natural Gradient](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-quantum-fisher.html): The quantum Fisher information defines the geometry of parameter space, enabling natural-gradient steps that often train quantum models faster than plain gradient descent.
- [Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-qgan.html): A quantum GAN pits a quantum generator against a discriminator in a minimax game, training the generator to produce samples the discriminator cannot distinguish from real data.
- [Quantum Generative Models](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-generative-models.html): Quantum generative models learn to produce samples from a target distribution using the native randomness of quantum measurement as the sampling engine.
- [Quantum Kernels](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-quantum-kernels.html): A quantum kernel measures similarity between data points as the overlap of the quantum states they are encoded into, estimated by running a circuit many times.
- [Quantum Machine Learning: A Map](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-overview.html): Quantum machine learning studies how quantum computers might represent, process, and learn from data using superposition, interference, and entanglement.
- [Quantum Neural Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-quantum-neural-networks.html): Quantum neural networks are parameterized quantum circuits trained like neural networks, borrowing the layered structure and gradient-based optimization of deep learning.
- [Quantum Principal Component Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-qpca.html): Quantum principal component analysis proposes to extract the dominant eigenvectors of a density matrix using quantum phase estimation, subject to strong assumptions.
- [Quantum Reservoir Computing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-quantum-reservoir.html): Quantum reservoir computing feeds data into a fixed, untrained quantum system and trains only a simple classical readout on its measured responses.
- [Quantum Support Vector Machines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-quantum-svm.html): A quantum support vector machine uses a quantum computer to compute a kernel matrix, then trains a standard maximum-margin classifier classically on that matrix.
- [Shot Noise and Sampling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-measurement-shots.html): Every quantum expectation value is estimated from a finite number of measurements, so shot noise sets the precision and the runtime of quantum machine learning.
- [Tensor Networks and Quantum ML](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-tensor-networks.html): Tensor networks efficiently represent low-entanglement quantum states, serving both as classical machine learning models and as the benchmark quantum methods must beat.
- [The Barren Plateau Problem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-barren-plateaus.html): In many parameterized quantum circuits the loss gradient shrinks exponentially with qubit count, leaving a nearly flat landscape that gradient descent cannot navigate.
- [The HHL Algorithm and Linear Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-hhl.html): The HHL algorithm solves linear systems on a quantum computer in time logarithmic in the matrix size, under conditions that sharply limit its practical reach.
- [The Kernel Trick](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-kernel-trick.html): The kernel trick lets linear algorithms operate in a high-dimensional feature space using only inner products, never computing the explicit coordinates.
- [The Parameter-Shift Rule](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-parameter-shift.html): The parameter-shift rule computes exact gradients of a quantum circuit by evaluating the same circuit at two shifted parameter values.
- [Trainability and Local Cost Functions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-trainability.html): A quantum model is trainable only if its gradients stay measurable as it scales; local cost functions and structured ansatze are the main ways to keep them so.
- [Variational Quantum Classifiers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/qml-variational-classifiers.html): A variational quantum classifier encodes data into a circuit, applies trainable gates, and measures an observable whose expectation is optimized to predict labels.

### 3D Model
- [Burner Aegis Housing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-aegis-housing.html): Aegis is the burner packaged for fixed defense installations, the same tandem-mirror generator in a site-hardened enclosure.
- [Burner Central Cell](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-central-cell.html): The central cell is the long middle region where the deuterium-helium-3 plasma burns, held between the two end plugs.
- [Burner Deuterium-Helium-3 Fuel Cycle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-d-he3-fuel-cycle.html): The burner fuses deuterium with helium-3, a reaction that releases its energy mostly as charged particles.
- [Burner Direct-Energy Converter](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-direct-energy-converter.html): The direct-energy converter turns the kinetic energy of escaping charged particles into electricity without a thermal cycle.
- [Burner End Tanks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-end-tanks.html): The end tanks terminate each end of the machine, housing the converter, handling exhaust, and maintaining the axial vacuum.
- [Burner Expander](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-expander.html): The expander is the flaring region beyond each plug where the escaping plasma spreads out along widening field lines.
- [Burner Heating Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-ecrh-heating.html): The burner uses radio-frequency and neutral-beam heating to reach the high temperatures deuterium-helium-3 fusion demands.
- [Burner High-Field Plug Throats](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-high-field-plug-throats.html): The plug throats are the intense high-field regions at each end that reflect plasma back into the central cell.
- [Burner MetroVolt Housing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-metrovolt-housing.html): MetroVolt is the burner packaged for data centers, delivering the tandem-mirror generator as an on-site power source.
- [Burner Mirror Coils](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-mirror-coils.html): The mirror coils shape the axial field, gentle in the central cell and intense at the plugs, to confine the plasma.
- [Burner Neutron Fraction and Shielding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-neutron-fraction-shielding.html): Deuterium-helium-3 fuel keeps neutrons to 5.44 percent of the fusion power, easing shielding compared with deuterium-tritium.
- [Burner Plasma Confinement Geometry](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-plasma-confinement-geometry.html): Confinement in the burner combines magnetic mirroring with electrostatic plugging along a single straight axis.
- [Burner Tandem-Mirror: Model Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/burner-tandem-mirror-model-overview.html): The burner is a deuterium-helium-3 tandem-mirror generator, a long linear machine with high-field plugs at each end.
- [Comparing the Breeder and Burner in the Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/comparing-breeder-and-burner.html): Viewing Hyperion and the burner side by side shows how differently two fusion machines can be built for different jobs.
- [Component Measurements and Design Parameters](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/component-measurements-and-parameters.html): Every component carries measurements and design parameters drawn from the frozen canon, readable directly in the model.
- [Coordinate Systems in the Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/coordinate-systems-in-the-model.html): How the toroidal frame of the breeder and the axial frame of the burner are set up so measurements are unambiguous.
- [Cryogenic Cooling Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cryogenic-cooling-model.html): The cryogenic system keeps the REBCO magnets cold enough to stay superconducting despite nuclear and ambient heat loads.
- [Cutaway and Section Views](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cutaway-and-section-views.html): Section planes remove half the machine so the layered build from plasma to cryostat is visible in a single glance.
- [Design Parameter Callouts](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/design-parameter-callouts.html): Callouts present a component's key parameters with their conditions, so a number is never shown without the context it needs.
- [Exploded View and Assembly Order](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/exploded-view-assembly-order.html): The exploded view separates components along their assembly axis, showing stacking order, interfaces, and maintenance access.
- [How to Read the 3D Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/how-to-read-the-3d-model.html): A short guide to selecting components, reading callouts, and moving between the exterior, cutaway, and exploded views.
- [Hyperion Breeder: Model Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-breeder-model-overview.html): The Hyperion model is a compact deuterium-tritium spherical tokamak whose layered shells breed tritium around the plasma.
- [Hyperion Breeding Blanket](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-breeding-blanket.html): The breeding blanket wraps the plasma to capture fusion neutrons, breed tritium in lithium, and carry away the fusion heat.
- [Hyperion Center Stack](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-center-stack.html): The center stack is the slender central column that carries the toroidal-field return, the solenoid, and the inboard shielding.
- [Hyperion Central Solenoid](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-central-solenoid.html): The central solenoid sits on the machine axis and drives plasma current inductively, acting as the primary of a transformer.
- [Hyperion Cryostat](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-cryostat.html): The cryostat is the outer vacuum enclosure that keeps the superconducting magnets cold by isolating them from ambient heat.
- [Hyperion Current Drive](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-current-drive.html): Non-inductive current drive sustains the 9.86 MA plasma current after the central solenoid's inductive flux runs out.
- [Hyperion Divertor](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-divertor.html): The divertor is the exhaust component that channels heat and helium ash out of the plasma while protecting the chamber walls.
- [Hyperion First Wall](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-first-wall.html): The first wall is the plasma-facing surface that takes the heat and particle flux and shields the breeding blanket behind it.
- [Hyperion Fueling and Pellet Injection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-fueling-pellet-injection.html): Fueling systems replace burned deuterium and tritium, with frozen pellets fired deep into the plasma to reach the core.
- [Hyperion Heating Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-heating-systems.html): External heating raises the plasma to fusion temperatures and, with current drive, sustains it beyond the inductive phase.
- [Hyperion Magnet Support Structure](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-magnet-support-structure.html): The support structure carries the enormous magnetic forces on the coils, holding the field geometry rigid under load.
- [Hyperion Neutron Shield](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-neutron-shield.html): The neutron shield sits behind the blanket to protect the vacuum vessel, the superconducting coils, and the structure from radiation.
- [Hyperion Plasma Shape and Negative Triangularity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-plasma-shape-triangularity.html): Hyperion runs a D-shaped plasma with negative triangularity of -0.30, a shaping choice drawn honestly in the model.
- [Hyperion Poloidal-Field Coils](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-poloidal-field-coils.html): The poloidal-field coils shape and position the plasma, setting its elongation, its negative triangularity, and its vertical stability.
- [Hyperion Toroidal-Field Coils](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-toroidal-field-coils.html): The toroidal-field coils produce the field that circles the torus, confining the plasma at 8 T on axis and 16.84 T peak.
- [Hyperion Tritium Plant Interface](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-tritium-plant-interface.html): The tritium plant interface extracts bred tritium from the blanket, processes it, and returns clean fuel to the machine.
- [Hyperion Vacuum Vessel](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-vacuum-vessel.html): The vacuum vessel is the sealed chamber that holds the plasma in high vacuum and forms the primary confinement boundary.
- [Hyperion Vessel Ports](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hyperion-vessel-ports.html): Ports are the vessel penetrations that admit heating, fueling, diagnostics, and maintenance access to the plasma.
- [Isolating and Hiding Components](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/isolating-and-hiding-components.html): Isolate a single part or hide obscuring shells to inspect any component of either machine without clutter.
- [Level of Detail in the Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/level-of-detail-in-the-model.html): The model swaps mesh detail by distance and device speed while keeping every selectable part and every measurement intact.
- [Linking the Model to This Library](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/linking-model-to-library.html): Every component in the model connects to an explanatory page here, so geometry and explanation form one reference.
- [Magnet Quench Protection Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/magnet-quench-protection-model.html): A quench is a sudden loss of superconductivity; protection systems detect it early and safely dissipate the stored energy.
- [Material Annotations in the Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-materials-annotations.html): Each component is tagged with its material class, so the model shows not just where a part is but what it must be made of.
- [Measurement Tools in the Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/measurement-tools-in-the-model.html): Point-to-point, radial, and layer-thickness measurement tools let you read true dimensions directly off the geometry.
- [Model Honesty and Physics Gates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-honesty-and-gates.html): The model shows what is designed and computed, states clearly that the machines are unbuilt, and flags the gates that remain.
- [Model Versioning and Provenance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-versioning-and-provenance.html): Each model release is a versioned snapshot tied to a frozen design state, so any component can be cited unambiguously.
- [Navigating the 3D Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-navigation-controls.html): Orbit, pan, zoom, and framing controls, plus the keyboard and touch shortcuts that make the model quick to explore.
- [Public vs Signed-In Detail](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/public-vs-signed-in-detail.html): The model shows a full public teaser with real geometry and physics, and reveals deeper internal detail to signed-in users.
- [REBCO Coil Winding Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rebco-coil-winding-model.html): Coils are built by stacking and winding REBCO tapes into turns, then into pancakes, insulated and clamped against huge forces.
- [REBCO Tape Architecture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rebco-tape-architecture.html): REBCO conductor is a thin layered tape: a superconducting film on a metal substrate, protected by silver and copper.
- [Reading a Poloidal Cutaway](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reading-a-poloidal-cutaway.html): A vertical section through Hyperion's centerline is the single most informative view, showing plasma shape and every shell.
- [Reading an Axial Cutaway](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/reading-an-axial-cutaway.html): A section along the burner's long axis shows the confine-then-convert chain from central cell to direct converter.
- [The Component Labeling System](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/component-labeling-system.html): A consistent naming and tagging scheme lets every part in both machines be selected, cited, and cross-referenced.
- [The Model as Design Record](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-as-design-record.html): The 3D model is a versioned design and simulation record of two unbuilt machines, not a depiction of existing hardware.
- [The Physics-Computable Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/physics-computable-model.html): Geometry in the model is tied to the frozen design parameters, so fields, currents, and dimensions read off the parts themselves.
- [The Shared REBCO Magnet Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rebco-magnet-model.html): Both Kronos machines rely on REBCO high-temperature superconductor to reach fields conventional magnets cannot deliver.
- [The Two Machines in One Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/model-overview-two-machines.html): The interactive 3D model holds both Kronos designs, the Hyperion breeder and the tandem-mirror burner, as fully explorable geometry.
- [Units and Scale in the Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/units-and-scale-in-the-model.html): The model uses SI units throughout, with a persistent scale reference so components never lose their true size.

### Component Control
- [Actuator Sharing and Control Arbitration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-actuator-sharing-arbitration.html): Many control goals compete for the same limited actuators, so an arbitration layer allocates them by priority and respects hard limits.
- [Balance-of-Plant Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-balance-of-plant-control.html): Beyond the reactor core, a fusion plant needs cooling, power distribution, and auxiliaries, all coordinated by a plant-wide control system.
- [Breeding Blanket Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-breeding-blanket-control.html): The blanket surrounding a D-T plasma captures neutrons to breed tritium and carry away heat, and its coolant and purge flows are actively controlled.
- [Burner Plug Magnet Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-plug-magnet-control-burner.html): A tandem mirror confines plasma between strong end plugs, so controlling the high-field plug coils is central to the burner's operation.
- [Coil Power-Supply Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-power-supply-control.html): Power supplies convert grid power into the precisely regulated currents the magnet coils need, and their fast inner loops underpin all magnetic control.
- [Cooling Water and Heat Rejection Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-cooling-water-control.html): Cooling loops carry heat from magnets, heating systems, and plasma-facing components to a heat sink, regulated to hold every component in its window.
- [Cryogenic System Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-cryogenic-control.html): Superconducting magnets run near a few kelvin, so a helium refrigeration plant must hold temperature and flow steady against a swinging heat load.
- [Current-Sharing Temperature Monitoring](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-superconductor-current-sharing.html): The current-sharing temperature marks where a superconductor starts to share current with its copper matrix, and temperature margin to it is the key health metric.
- [Direct Converter Electrical Output Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-dec-grid-synchronization.html): The high-voltage direct current from a direct energy converter must be conditioned and inverted into stable, standards-compliant electrical output.
- [Direct Energy Converter Control (Burner)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-direct-energy-converter-control.html): A direct energy converter turns the kinetic energy of charged fusion products straight into electricity by decelerating them against a voltage.
- [Divertor Detachment Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-divertor-detachment-control.html): Detachment cools and dilutes the plasma before it reaches the divertor target, spreading heat over gas and radiation instead of concentrating it on a surface.
- [Divertor Heat Flux Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-divertor-heat-flux-control.html): Keeping the power landing on divertor targets within material limits combines strike-point sweeping, flux spreading, and detachment.
- [Electron Cyclotron Heating Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-ecrh-control.html): Electron cyclotron systems deposit power at the electron gyro-frequency using high-power millimeter-wave beams from gyrotrons, aimed by steerable mirrors.
- [Equilibrium and Radial-Field Coil Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-radial-field-control.html): Equilibrium coils supply the vertical field that balances the plasma's outward force and set the plasma current profile through the central solenoid.
- [Error Field Correction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-error-field-correction.html): Small unavoidable asymmetries in the field can lock plasma modes and trigger disruptions, so correction coils cancel these error fields.
- [Fault Ride-Through and Safe Shutdown](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-fault-ride-through.html): When something goes wrong the plant must either ride through the disturbance or shut down safely in a controlled, predictable sequence.
- [Feedforward Control in Plant Scenarios](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-feedforward-control.html): Feedforward uses a known plan or disturbance to command actuators in advance, leaving feedback to correct only the residual error.
- [Gas Puffing Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-gas-puff-control.html): Gas puffing feeds fuel to the plasma edge through fast valves, giving quick but shallow density control that anchors the fueling system.
- [Gyrotron Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-gyrotron-control.html): A gyrotron is the high-power millimeter-wave source for electron cyclotron heating, and its operation depends on tight control of voltage, current, and field.
- [Heating Power Modulation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-heating-power-modulation.html): The total auxiliary heating power is the main lever on plasma temperature and stored energy, and it is modulated in real time to hit control targets.
- [Helium Refrigeration Cycle Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-cryoplant-helium-refrigeration.html): A large helium refrigerator uses staged compression, heat exchange, and turbine expansion to reach a few kelvin, and each stage is actively controlled.
- [Impurity Seeding Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-impurity-seeding-control.html): Injecting a small amount of a radiating impurity spreads exhaust power over the plasma volume and edge, protecting the divertor and first wall.
- [Infrared Thermography for Plasma-Facing Components](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-pfc-interferometry-thermography.html): Infrared cameras turn the glow of hot surfaces into real-time temperature maps that reveal heat-flux patterns and hot spots on the wall.
- [Ion Cyclotron Heating Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-icrh-control.html): Ion cyclotron systems heat plasma ions with tens-of-megahertz waves launched from in-vessel antennas, where coupling and matching dominate control.
- [Magnet Protection Interlocks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-magnet-protection-interlocks.html): A hard-wired interlock chain guards the coils, tripping the supply and firing the dump whenever any monitored condition leaves its safe window.
- [Neutral Beam Alignment and Interlocks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-nbi-beam-alignment.html): A neutral beam carries megawatts in a narrow line; misalignment can strike a wall, so aiming and geometric interlocks are safety-critical.
- [Neutral Beam Injection Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-neutral-beam-control.html): Neutral beams heat and drive current in the plasma by shooting energetic neutral atoms through the confining field, and their power is finely controlled.
- [PID Control Loops in Fusion Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-pid-control-loops.html): The proportional-integral-derivative loop is the workhorse regulator behind coil currents, temperatures, flows, and pressures throughout the plant.
- [Pellet Injection Fueling Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-pellet-injection-control.html): Frozen fuel pellets fired deep into the plasma deliver particles to the core where gas puffing cannot reach, giving efficient core fueling.
- [Persistent Current Mode](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-persistent-current-mode.html): A superconducting coil can hold current in a closed loop with no supply connected, using a superconducting switch, which stabilizes the field.
- [Plant Control State Machines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-state-machine-plant-control.html): A supervisory state machine sequences the whole plant through its operating phases and enforces the conditions required to move between them.
- [Plasma Density Feedback Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-density-feedback-control.html): Density control holds the plasma's particle content at a target by commanding gas and pellet fueling against real-time interferometer measurements.
- [Plasma Shape and Position Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-shape-position-control.html): Poloidal field coils sculpt the plasma boundary and hold it in place, controlled from a real-time reconstruction of the plasma equilibrium.
- [Plasma-Facing-Component Thermal Monitoring](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-pfc-thermal-monitoring.html): The wall and divertor tiles take intense heat while the plasma runs, so their temperatures are watched continuously to catch overloads before damage.
- [Quench Detection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-quench-detection.html): A quench is the loss of superconductivity in part of a coil; detecting the resistive voltage it produces fast enough is the core protection problem.
- [Quench Protection and Energy Dump](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-quench-protection.html): Once a quench is confirmed the magnet's stored energy must leave the coil fast enough to keep the hot spot below damaging temperature.
- [RF Antenna Impedance Matching](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-antenna-matching-control.html): An RF source delivers full power only into a matched load, so a tuning network continuously matches the antenna's changing plasma coupling to the generator.
- [Radio-Frequency Heating Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-rf-heating-control.html): Radio-frequency systems heat plasma by launching electromagnetic waves tuned to particle resonances, and each system regulates power, frequency, and coupling.
- [Real-Time Control Networks](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-real-time-control-network.html): Plasma and component control demand deterministic communication, so a real-time network moves sensor and command data on a fixed, guaranteed schedule.
- [Superconducting Magnet Current Ramps](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-magnet-current-ramp.html): Bringing a superconducting coil to field means ramping current slowly enough that induced losses and stresses stay within safe limits.
- [Tandem Mirror Confinement Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-mirror-confinement-control.html): Confinement in a tandem mirror depends on maintaining the axial potential profile and mirror fields against particle and energy losses.
- [Tritium Inventory Accounting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-tritium-inventory-accounting.html): Every gram of tritium in the plant is tracked through storage, processing, and the plasma so the mass balance always closes.
- [Tritium and Fuel-Cycle Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-tritium-fuel-cycle-control.html): A D-T device must recover, purify, and re-inject its fuel while accounting for every gram of tritium, all under continuous control.
- [Vacuum Leak Detection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-leak-detection-control.html): A single small leak can spoil the vacuum and, in a tritium plant, breach containment, so leak detection runs before and during operation.
- [Vacuum Pumping Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-vacuum-pumping-control.html): Pumping control regulates the removal of exhaust gas during a pulse, setting particle throughput while protecting each pump's operating window.
- [Vacuum System Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-vacuum-system-control.html): A fusion device needs a very high vacuum before and during operation, maintained by staged pumps under continuous control and interlocking.
- [Vertical Stabilization Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/cc-vertical-stability-control.html): Elongated plasmas are vertically unstable and drift toward the wall unless a fast feedback loop actively holds them centered.

### Real Time Systems
- [Actuator Interfaces](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/actuator-interfaces.html): Actuators turn control commands into physical action; the interface must convert, amplify, and safely drive them while confirming what actually happened.
- [Aliasing and Anti-Alias Filtering](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/aliasing-and-anti-alias-filtering.html): Frequencies above half the sampling rate masquerade as lower ones; an analog filter before the sampler is the only way to prevent this corruption.
- [Analog-to-Digital Conversion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/analog-to-digital-conversion.html): An ADC samples an analog signal and encodes it as a number; its architecture sets the trade-off between speed, resolution, and latency.
- [Clock Domains and Timing References](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/clock-domains-and-timing-references.html): Every digital system runs on clocks; their stability, and safe crossing between independent clock domains, underpin correct real-time timing.
- [Context Switching](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/context-switching.html): A context switch saves one task's processor state and restores another's; its cost and predictability directly affect real-time timing budgets.
- [Control Stability and Phase Margin](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-stability-and-phase-margin.html): A feedback loop is stable only if it does not build up oscillations; phase and gain margins quantify how much delay or gain error it can survive.
- [Control-Loop Timing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/control-loop-timing.html): A control loop must sense, compute, and actuate within its period every cycle; the choice of period couples timing engineering to control theory.
- [Data Acquisition Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/data-acquisition-systems.html): A data acquisition system turns physical quantities into timestamped digital data, and its timing and integrity determine what control and analysis can achieve.
- [Determinism in Real-Time Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/determinism-in-real-time-systems.html): Determinism is the property that a system's timing behavior is bounded and repeatable, so its worst case can be known before it runs.
- [Deterministic Networking](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/deterministic-networking.html): When control spans multiple nodes, the network must deliver messages with bounded latency and jitter, which ordinary best-effort networking cannot guarantee.
- [Digital Signal Processing Basics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/digital-signal-processing-basics.html): DSP transforms sampled signals numerically to filter, measure, and extract information, and in real-time control it must complete within each sample period.
- [Digital-to-Analog Conversion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/digital-to-analog-conversion.html): A DAC turns a numeric command into a continuous voltage or current, forming the output stage that lets a digital controller act on the physical world.
- [Earliest-Deadline-First Scheduling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/earliest-deadline-first.html): EDF always runs the task with the nearest deadline; it achieves full processor utilization but at the cost of dynamic priorities and harder overload behavior.
- [Edge Compute in Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/edge-compute-in-control.html): Placing computation near sensors and actuators cuts latency and keeps control loops running independent of network and cloud availability.
- [FPGA-Based Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fpga-based-control.html): FPGAs implement control logic as parallel hardware, giving nanosecond, jitter-free timing that software on a CPU cannot match for the fastest loops.
- [Fault Tolerance and Failover](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/fault-tolerance-and-failover.html): A fault-tolerant system keeps functioning despite component failures by detecting faults and switching to healthy resources without violating timing.
- [Feedback Loop Design](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/feedback-loop-design.html): Feedback compares a measurement to a target and drives the difference toward zero; good design balances responsiveness against stability and noise.
- [Hard vs Soft Real-Time](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hard-vs-soft-real-time.html): A real-time system is judged by whether it meets deadlines, not by raw speed; the cost of a missed deadline separates hard from soft.
- [Hardware vs Software Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/hardware-vs-software-control.html): The choice between implementing control in fixed hardware or in software trades determinism and speed against flexibility and complexity.
- [Interlocks and Permissives](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/interlocks-and-permissives.html): Interlocks block dangerous actions and permissives allow safe ones; together they enforce that a system operates only within its safe envelope.
- [Interrupt Handling and Latency](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/interrupt-handling-and-latency.html): Interrupts let hardware demand prompt attention; interrupt latency, the delay before the response begins, is a key determinant of real-time responsiveness.
- [Jitter: Sources and Mitigation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/jitter-sources-and-mitigation.html): Jitter is the variation in timing between cycles; even when average latency is fine, jitter degrades control quality and complicates timing proofs.
- [Latency Fundamentals](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/latency-fundamentals.html): Latency is the elapsed time from a stimulus to the completed response, and in control it must be measured end to end, not stage by stage.
- [Memory Locking and Cache Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/memory-locking-and-cache-control.html): Page faults and cache misses cause unpredictable delays; locking memory and controlling cache behavior are standard techniques for real-time determinism.
- [Mixed-Criticality Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/mixed-criticality-systems.html): When tasks of different importance share one platform, the architecture must ensure low-criticality work can never compromise high-criticality timing.
- [Plasma Control Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/plasma-control-systems.html): Confining a fusion plasma requires fast, multivariable real-time control coordinating many magnets and diagnostics within microsecond timing budgets.
- [Polling vs Interrupt-Driven I/O](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/polling-vs-interrupt-driven-io.html): Software can wait for an event by repeatedly checking or by being interrupted; each has distinct latency, overhead, and determinism characteristics.
- [Priority Inversion and Inheritance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/priority-inversion-and-inheritance.html): Priority inversion is when a high-priority task waits on a resource held by a low-priority one; inheritance protocols bound how long that wait can last.
- [Quantization and ADC Resolution](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/quantization-and-adc-resolution.html): Converting an analog value to a finite number of levels introduces quantization error, and resolution in bits sets the floor on measurement precision.
- [RTOS Scheduling Algorithms](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rtos-scheduling-algorithms.html): Scheduling decides which task runs when; in real-time systems the algorithm must be analyzable so deadlines can be guaranteed in advance.
- [Rate-Monotonic Scheduling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/rate-monotonic-scheduling.html): Rate-monotonic scheduling assigns higher priority to faster tasks; it is optimal among fixed-priority policies and comes with a simple sufficiency test.
- [Real-Time Data Logging](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/real-time-data-logging.html): Logging must capture high-rate control and diagnostic data without disturbing the real-time loop it observes, preserving both timing and integrity.
- [Real-Time Operating Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/real-time-operating-systems.html): An RTOS provides bounded, predictable scheduling and services so that timing guarantees, not just average performance, can be proven.
- [Redundancy Architectures](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/redundancy-architectures.html): Redundancy uses multiple channels so a single failure does not defeat a function; the architecture chosen trades availability against safe-fault detection.
- [Safety Integrity Levels](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sil-safety-integrity-levels.html): SILs grade how reliably a safety function must perform, turning a hazard's severity into a measurable target for the protective system's design.
- [Safety-Instrumented Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/safety-instrumented-systems.html): A safety-instrumented system is an independent layer that detects dangerous conditions and forces the process to a safe state, separate from normal control.
- [Sampling and the Nyquist Limit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sampling-and-nyquist.html): The Nyquist-Shannon theorem sets the minimum sampling rate to represent a signal without loss; violating it corrupts data irreversibly.
- [Sensor Fusion in Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sensor-fusion-in-control.html): Combining multiple imperfect sensors yields an estimate more accurate and robust than any single one, and lets control proceed when a sensor fails.
- [Sensor Interfaces](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/sensor-interfaces.html): Sensors convert physical quantities into signals; the interface must condition, protect, and digitize them without corrupting the measurement.
- [State-Space Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/state-space-control.html): State-space methods describe a system by its internal state vector, enabling systematic control of coupled, multivariable dynamics beyond single-loop PID.
- [Time Synchronization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/time-synchronization.html): Distributed real-time systems need a shared, precise clock so events can be ordered, timestamped, and coordinated across independent nodes.
- [Timing Budgets](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/timing-budgets.html): A timing budget allocates a control period among its stages so that the sum, in the worst case, provably fits within the deadline with margin.
- [Watchdog Timers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/watchdog-timers.html): A watchdog timer resets or safes a system when software stops servicing it, catching hangs and deadlocks that other checks would miss.
- [Worst-Case Execution Time](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ai/worst-case-execution-time.html): WCET is the provable upper bound on how long a piece of code can take; every real-time timing proof rests on trustworthy WCET values.
